articles.title: Checkers & Rally’s Celebrating 40 Years with Free Fries in NYC
articles.titleKo: Checkers & Rally’s Celebrating 40 Years with Free Fries in NYC
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Checkers & Rally’s is celebrating 40 years of bold flavor by bringing the Fry Love straight to the heart of New York City. On Wednesday, Sept. 23 – Checkers Day – from 11 a.m. to 3 p.m., the brand’s 43-foot Fry Love Express will roll into Herald Square in Manhattan, directly in front of Macy’s between 34th and 35th Streets, serving up complimentary Famous Seasoned Fries as part of Checkers & Rally’s 40th anniversary celebration. Guests can stop by throughout the day for complimentary Famous Seasoned Fries, games and giveaways, including an oversized Checkers game. The first 50 guests will also receive a Checkers & Rally’s Anniversary Cup as a souvenir. Power 105.1 will join the celebration with an on-air personality and street team on-site. And the Fry Love continues after the event: guests will receive a coupon for a complimentary small order of Famous Seasoned Fries at their local participating Checkers restaurant. The larger-than-life Fry Love Express travels the country delivering Checkers & Rally’s signature Famous Seasoned Fries and creating memorable experiences for fans along the way. Since hitting the road in 2021, the Fry Love Express has traveled more than 150,000 miles, attended 275+ events, spent more than 875 days on the road and served Famous Seasoned Fries to more than 225,000 people nationwide – that’s millions of hot, crispy, Famous Seasoned Fries handed out along the way. “For 40 years, Checkers & Rally’s has been all about big flavor, and there’s no better way to celebrate than by sharing the Fry Love with New York City,” said Jana Schubarth, Checkers & Rally’s Fry Love Express Mobile Marketing Manager. “The Fry Love Express was created to bring our Famous Seasoned Fries directly to fans and communities across the country, and we can’t wait to celebrate this milestone with everyone who stops by Herald Square.” The New York City stop is part of Checkers & Rally’s 40th “Flava Versary,” a celebration of four decades of doing things differently and delivering the bold, craveable flavors fans have come to expect from the iconic drive-thru brand. The celebration also includes new limited-time menu offerings, including the Flava Max Double and Flava Max Chicken Bites & Fries Box, starting at $3.49, available at participating Checkers & Rally’s locations nationwide. And the Fry Love won’t stop in Manhattan. Following the Herald Square celebration, the Fry Love Express will head to Sneaker Con Brooklyn on Saturday, Sept. 26 and Sunday, Sept. 27, bringing complimentary Famous Seasoned Fries to one of the country’s premier sneaker culture events. The back-to-back New York City stops bring Checkers & Rally’s anniversary celebration directly to fans through food, culture and unexpected experiences. To find out where the Fry Love Express will be next, follow @fryloveexpress on Instagram and Facebook. articles.title: Fresh Kitchen Opening 20th Florida Location in Fort Myers
articles.titleKo: Fresh Kitchen Opening 20th Florida Location in Fort Myers
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Fresh Kitchen (FK), the healthy, fast, modern-American bowl concept, announced the upcoming grand opening of its 20th Florida location — and its first in Southwest Florida — in Fort Myers, set for Spring 2027. Located at 16461 Corporate Commerce Way, Fort Myers, FL 33913, the new restaurant will bring FK’s signature scratchmade bowls, warm hospitality, and community-first spirit to Southwest Florida for the first time. “When we opened our first Fresh Kitchen in Tampa in 2014, we set out to make healthy food more available, and to show people it could taste good, be affordable, and convenient. Opening our 20th location in Fort Myers is proof that this is how people want to eat. Thank you for all the support, Florida,” said Steven Lanza, Founder, Fresh Kitchen “Fort Myers is an amazing community and a market we’ve wanted to be part of for a long time. We can’t wait to introduce Fresh Kitchen and share delicious, fresh, chef-made food with the people who call Fort Myers home. We hope this will be the first of multiple locations in the Fort Myers and Southwest Florida. We can’t wait to serve you,” added Tyler Azzarelli, CEO, Fresh Kitchen. The Fort Myers opening marks Fresh Kitchen’s first restaurant in Southwest Florida, bringing the brand to one of the state’s fastest-growing markets. FK has had its eye on the area for years, waiting for the right site to make its move. “We targeted this intersection for several years, waiting for the perfect location, and knew this freestanding building was the site to make our entry into the Fort Myers market,” said Matthew Livingston, Chief Development Officer, Fresh Kitchen. The company is already eyeing its next two or three restaurants in the Fort Myers trade area as it builds its presence in Southwest Florida. Guests build their own bowl from familiar flavors inspired by the places they love, choosing from seasonal ingredients including fresh greens, grilled meats, perfectly seasoned rices and roasted vegetables cut in-house daily. The entire menu features hormone- and antibioticfree proteins and sustainably sourced seafood, and is 100% gluten-free with dairy-free and vegan options available, prepared without ultra-processed ingredients or seed oils, and always cooked with olive oil. articles.title: Scooter’s Coffee Now Available for Delivery through DoorDash
articles.titleKo: Scooter’s Coffee Now Available for Delivery through DoorDash
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Today, DoorDash announced that Scooter’s Coffee is now available for delivery exclusively on the platform, giving the drive-thru chain’s fans a new way to order ahead of National Coffee Day on September 29. As the exclusive delivery partner of Scooter’s Coffee, the chain’s ‘Licious Lineup drinks, Red Bull Infusions, breakfast and anytime treats, crème cold brews, shakes, smoothies, and more can all be delivered directly to guests through the DoorDash app. In 2025, there were more than 80 million coffee orders placed on DoorDash – growth that Scooter’s Coffee has tapped into. Through this partnership, consumers now have delivery access to the chain’s menu for the first time through participating stores among the 900+ Scooter’s Coffee locations nationwide. “Scooter’s has built real loyalty around speed and a menu customers love. Bringing them onto DoorDash means that experience isn’t limited when life gets in the way of making a drive-thru run,” said Vishwa Chandra, Head of Enterprise Partnerships at DoorDash. “We’re proud to be the only place customers can get Scooter’s delivered, and it’s a good example of what we can do for merchants who’ve built something worth showing up for.” “Today’s guests expect maximum convenience and our DoorDash partnership makes it easier than ever to get your Scooter’s Coffee fix,” said Anna Faktorovich, Chief Marketing Officer at Scooter’s Coffee. To mark the launch and celebrate National Coffee Day, Scooter’s Coffee is offering a DoorDash exclusive buy one, get one free deal* on medium Caramelicious® drinks from September 27–29, 2026. This offer includes the original signature Caramelicious, the limited-time Pumpkin Caramelicious, the Caramelicious Crème Cold Brew, and any other drink with Caramelicious in its name. All espresso drinks can be ordered hot, iced, or blended. Scooter’s Coffee is live on DoorDash, and joins a growing roster of coffee brands on the platform. articles.originalSummary: Napoli on the Road’s latest accolade and the uncertain future of ‘London’s oldest’ Mexican restaurant are among this week’s top news stories. - London-based Napoli on the Road has been named the World’s Best Pizzeria at the 50 Top Pizza World Awards in Naples, marking the latest major accolade for founder Michele Pascarella. The pizzeria group, which has ranked among the world’s top five since 2024, began in 2016 with Pascarella serving Neapolitan-style pizzas from a wood-fired oven fitted into a three-wheeled Ape Piaggio van. Since then, the business has grown to restaurants in Chiswick, Richmond and, most recently, Soho, where its pizza tasting menu draws on Pascarella’s Italian heritage and childhood. Pascarella, who moved to the UK from Maddaloni near Naples at 19, was also named Pizza Maker of the Year by 50 Top Pizza in 2023. - The future of ‘London’s oldest’ Mexican restaurant Café Pacifico in Covent Garden is uncertain after liquidators were appointed to its operating company, Laverlathe Limited. Robert Dymond and Joanne Hammond of Begbies Traynor were appointed joint liquidators last month, following the company’s compulsory winding-up in March after a petition was filed in November. The restaurant remains open and is still taking bookings, although it is unclear whether it has been sold to a new operator or continues to trade under the liquidators’ control. Established on Langley Street in 1982, Café Pacifico describes itself as London’s oldest Mexican restaurant and tequila bar and claims to have been the first restaurant to bring Mexican cuisine to the UK.

articles.title: At Minnie Bird, Preparing to Franchise Starts Long Before the Map Fills In
articles.titleKo: At Minnie Bird, Preparing to Franchise Starts Long Before the Map Fills In
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . The first step toward scale is defining what must be true in every restaurant, on every shift, regardless of who is working or who owns the location. Most guests experience Minnie Bird through what is directly in front of them: hand-breaded chicken, a friendly team and a restaurant that feels energetic and easy. Behind the scenes, we are working on something much less visible: building the infrastructure that will allow the same experience to travel far beyond our first few restaurants. For an early stage brand, preparing for national growth may sound premature. But we know the complexity that comes with scale and we’d rather build for it before it arrives. The strongest foundations are built while we’re close enough to the restaurants to understand what works, candid enough to recognize what doesn’t, and nimble enough to improve quickly. A prospective franchisee is not simply buying a menu, a logo or the energy surrounding an emerging concept. They are betting that what works in the founders’ restaurants can be transferred to theirs, possibly hundreds or thousands of miles away.. An early stage brand does not need the executive team, overhead or bureaucracy of a 300-unit chain, but it does need the systems that make 300 units possible. The goal is not to cosplay as a large chain. It is to build a company whose systems can expand faster than its complexity—a brand that still has the energy and momentum of an emerging concept, but is steadily reducing the operational risk of being one. Here is an inside look at five things we are building now to prepare Minnie Bird for national franchise growth. 1. We are turning founder knowledge into a repeatable operating model What feels like flexibility at three restaurants can become inconsistency at thirty. One restaurant teaches a process one way, another adapts it, and a third creates its own shortcut. In isolation, those differences can feel harmless. At scale, they compound, creating operational friction, inconsistent execution and ultimately an uneven guest experience. The first step toward scale is defining what must be true in every restaurant, on every shift, regardless of who is working or who owns the location. For us, that means everything from how food is prepared and stations are set up to how shifts open and close, what great hospitality looks like, and what a team member must demonstrate before becoming certified. We are taking the hundreds of small details that make a Minnie Bird restaurant delight guests and turning them into clear, teachable standards another operator can consistently execute. But defining the standards is only part of the work. The next step is building systems that ensure those standards actually show up in the restaurant. Documentation preserves knowledge. Systems preserve execution. A binder or video can show someone what good looks like. A true system makes good execution teachable, verifiable and self-reinforcing, regardless of who is running the shift, leading the team or opening the next restaurant. That is what allows a brand to grow without diluting what made it successful in the first place. If a process can be taught, observed, verified and reinforced until it becomes part of how the restaurant naturally operates, it becomes self-reinforcing and truly scalable. 2. We are building a training system that does not depend on founders Small concepts often train through proximity. A strong operator stands next to a new employee and shows them what to do. It works, especially when the founder or best general manager is nearby. But proximity does not scale. We have worked to turn training into a sequence that can transfer from one capable leader to the next: explain the standard, demonstrate it, let the trainee perform it, coach in the moment and verify readiness in the restaurant. articles.title: 85°C Bakery Cafe top Open 100th U.S. Location in Aurora, Colorado
articles.titleKo: 85°C Bakery Cafe top Open 100th U.S. Location in Aurora, Colorado
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . 85°C Bakery Cafe, the Taiwanese bakery-café brand known for fresh-baked breads and pastries, handcrafted beverages and signature cakes, will open its 100th U.S. location on September 18 at Parker Commons in Aurora, Colorado. The opening will also introduce the brand to Colorado for the first time. 85°C entered the U.S. market in 2008 and has grown through a differentiated bakery-café model spanning four core categories: breads and pastries, cakes, handcrafted coffee, and tea beverages. As 85°C reaches triple-digit locations and enters Colorado, the brand begins a new stage of growth and works toward 150 U.S. locations by 2030. Cheng-Hsueh Wu founded 85°C Bakery Cafe in Taiwan in 2003 after visiting a café at a five-star hotel and questioning why high-quality pastries and beverages were priced beyond everyday reach. He envisioned a café offering premium coffee, bread and cake at approachable prices, a proposition that continues to guide the business more than two decades later. “Reaching 100 locations in the U.S. is an important milestone for 85°C and a reflection of the communities that have embraced the brand since we first entered the U.S. market,” said Dave Lazaro, Marketing Director of 85°C Bakery Cafe. “Our goal has always been to deliver high-quality coffee, bread and cake at prices that make 85°C part of our guests’ everyday lives. As we continue to grow, we’re excited to introduce that experience to even more communities across the country.” That combination of quality, variety and approachable pricing has helped 85°C establish a distinctive position within the U.S. bakery-café landscape. Each location features an in-shop bakery with more than 50 varieties of pastries baked fresh hourly, alongside handcrafted, made-to-order beverages and cakes created by the brand’s pastry teams. The company has offered coffee, tea, milk tea and boba in the U.S. since opening its first American location, well before boba achieved its current mainstream popularity. Its beverage menu ranges from signatures such as Sea Salt Coffee and Sea Salt Jasmine Green Tea to matcha drinks, fruit smoothies and newer consumer favorites including Vietnamese Coffee. Longtime 85°C menu favorites such as Milk Pudding Bread, Choco Bun, Marble Taro and the signature Egg Tart remain central to the brand’s bakery offering. Cakes including Mango Crème Brûlée and Deluxe Strawberry Cream Cake further demonstrate the breadth of its pastry program. El Pollo Loco, the leading fire-grilled chicken restaurant chain, announced a new lineup of limited-time offerings designed to bring bold, seasonal flavor to menu categories old and new. The lineup spans beverages, desserts and entrées, giving guests fresh reasons to visit any time of day. The new LTO items include: Caramel Apple ChataCoffee — El Pollo Loco’s classic Mexican-style horchata and iced coffee, layered with seasonal sweet and buttery caramel apple syrup, with the option to top it with a layer of creamy cold foam. articles.title: RTI Presents Food Waste Solutions at Climate Week NYC
articles.titleKo: RTI Presents Food Waste Solutions at Climate Week NYC
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Restaurant Technologies (RTI), a leading provider of automated cooking oil management for commercial kitchens, will unite with environmental leaders across policy, business, hospitality, and civil society at Climate Week NYC 2026 to discuss the role of commercial kitchens in waste reduction and providing solutions to the climate crisis. RTI will join Food Tank’s Solving Food Waste: A Key Solution to the Climate Crisis from 9 AM to 12 PM ET on Monday, September 21, at WNYC-NPR Studios’ The Greene Space in Manhattan. Presented in partnership with the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP), Food Planet Prize, NRDC, Walmart Foundation, CookUnity and Mill, the event will bring together a diverse group of leaders from government, business, hospitality and sustainability sectors to explore how reducing food waste can cut emissions, strengthen food security and build more resilient food systems. Diana Geseking, Chief Legal Officer and Impact Committee Chair at RTI, will speak on the panel Food Waste Action in Commercial Kitchens and Food Service and share insights on ways businesses can transform food waste from an operational challenge into an opportunity to reduce environmental impact and contribute to the circular economy. “Climate issues are addressed most effectively when industry, government, and society work together to find solutions,” said Geseking. “Restaurant Technologies is proud to stand alongside UNEP, NRDC, and our fellow co-hosts in advancing practical, scalable solutions to food waste, and to demonstrate how meaningful climate progress can make a big difference in kitchens around the world.” Restaurant Technologies addresses food waste through the automation of cooking oil delivery, filtration, monitoring and collection of used cooking oil for over 45,000 commercial kitchens nationwide, which includes McDonald’s, Shake Shack, Sheetz, Kroger, and more. In 2025, RTI recycled almost 400 million pounds of used cooking oil (UCO), and converted nearly 100% of its UCO into renewable diesel or biodiesel for vehicles on the road, or into sustainable aviation fuel for aircrafts. Geseking will join an accomplished group of food system and sustainability leaders participating in Food Tank’s Climate Week NYC event, including: Julie Gehrki, President, Walmart Foundation and Senior Vice President, Philanthropy, Walmart Inc.; María Bengochea, Director of Sustainability, Nutrition & Standards, CookUnity; Veleké Brown, Executive Director, E-RoadMap Corporation (Operation No Food Gap); Robert Jones, Vice President of Strategic Partnerships, Industry Leadership, and Impact, Culinary Institute of America; Matthew Jozwiak, CEO and Founder, Rethink; Adalberto Maluf, National Secretary for Urban Environment, Water Resources and Environmental Quality, Brazil’s Ministry of Environment and Climate Change; Danielle Nierenberg, President, Food Tank; U.S. Representative Andrea Salinas, Oregon’s 6th Congressional District; Gwyneth Rampton, Vice President of Sustainability, Compass Group USA and many more. From burritos and Beef Rollers to Crinkle Cut Fries, loaded nachos and queso with chips, the lineup gives guests a lot of ways to turn up the heat and new menu experiences to enjoy. Whether adding FLAMIN’ HOT flavored Queso to a handheld, loading it onto a favorite side or digging into a shareable option, there’s a combination for every Del Taco fan. The limited-time lineup adds FLAMIN’ HOT flavored Queso to an array of Del Taco favorites: FLAMIN’ HOT Queso Beef Roller: Seasoned beef, new FLAMIN’ HOT flavored Queso and fresh house-grated cheddar cheese rolled in a warm flour tortilla. FLAMIN’ HOT Queso Crispy Chicken Burrito: Crispy chicken strips, our famous Crinkle Cut fries, new FLAMIN’ HOT flavored Queso, fresh house-grated cheddar cheese, and cool sour cream, wrapped in a warm flour tortilla. FLAMIN’ HOT Queso Loaded Fries: Crinkle Cut Fries topped with seasoned beef, new FLAMIN’ HOT flavored Queso, fresh house-grated cheddar cheese, fresh diced tomatoes, cool sour cream and sliced jalapeños. Juice It Up!, one of the nation’s leading handcrafted smoothie, raw juice, açaí and superfruit bowl chains for over 30 years, is inviting guests to “Savor the Season” with a new lineup that offers something for everyone. Available now through January 5, the seasonal menu introduces a new Cold Brew Chia Pudding Parfait and two Toasted Favorites, alongside the return of the fan-favorite Horchata Smoothie. From a familiar seasonal favorite to protein-rich and coffee-forward options, the limited-time lineup brings together a variety of flavors, formats and functionality to give guests more ways to find something that fits their day. “We wanted to build a seasonal menu that gives guests more ways to find something that fits what they’re looking for, whether that’s a familiar flavor they wait for every year, a coffee-forward option to help power their day or a savory toast to pair with their favorite smoothie,” said Susan Taylor, President and CEO of Juice It Up! “Our new lineup reflects how we’re thinking about innovation today by bringing new flavors and formats to the menu while making sure there’s something for everyone in a way that feels distinctly Juice It Up!.” For Juice It Up! guests exploring flavors beyond the brand’s popular smoothies or superfruit bowls, and craving a comforting coffee-forward option, the new Cold Brew Chia Pudding Parfait layers almond milk, cold brew coffee, chia seeds and cinnamon, then is topped with Hemp Plus Granola, almonds, coconut flakes and honey. The result is a rich combination of coffee and cinnamon balanced by crunchy toppings. Each parfait contains 14 grams of protein and is an excellent source of calcium and iron, while its cold brew coffee provides caffeine equivalent to approximately one cup of coffee. The brand is also expanding its food offerings with a pair of new Toasted Favorites, giving guests two more satisfying options to enjoy throughout the day. Avocado + Cucumber Toast combines creamy Hass avocado with crisp sliced cucumber on toasted sourdough, finished with red pepper sauce and coarse salt for a fresh and flavorful combination. Delivering 11 grams of protein, the Protein Avocado Toast offers a protein-packed take on classic avocado toast with creamy Hass avocado and hard-boiled egg on toasted sourdough, finished with red pepper sauce and coarse salt. Rounding out the lineup, the Horchata Smoothie returns for its sixth consecutive year. Beloved for its smooth, creamy texture and sweet cinnamon flavor, the Horchata Smoothie brings the comforting taste of traditional horchata to a blended format. Crafted with almond milk, non-fat yogurt, dates, banana, cinnamon and chia seeds, the Horchata Smoothie offers a familiar seasonal favorite while providing an excellent source of calcium, fiber, B vitamins, vitamin A and vitamin E. Since its debut in 2020, the Horchata Smoothie has captured a devoted following and fueled an annual celebration each time it returns to the Juice It Up! menu. In addition to the new and returning menu offerings, Juice It Up! is testing a White Chocolate Raspberry Smoothie at select locations. This vibrant blend combines bright raspberry flavor with the sweetness of white chocolate and is crafted with soy milk and raspberry sherbet to deliver a creamy, rich finish. The limited test underscores the brand’s ongoing commitment to exploring fresh flavor combinations and seasonal offerings. The post Juice It Up! Famous Brands International, the parent company of iconic dessert brands Mrs. Fields and TCBY (The Country’s Best Yogurt), announced continued growth across the Southeast through an expanded development agreement with longtime franchisee and area developer Samuel Batt of Batt Enterprises. The agreement adds Georgia to Batt’s existing North Carolina and South Carolina territory, with plans to develop 15 new locations across the three states. Batt currently operates 15 TCBY and two Mrs. Fields locations and is experiencing his strongest year in the history of his TCBY ownership, with year-to-date sales up double digits compared with the same period last year. His continued investment reflects strong performance and sustained customer demand for both brands, while the expanded territory provides an opportunity to introduce TCBY and Mrs. Fields to more communities throughout the Southeast. As an area developer, Batt is building on the infrastructure he has established in the Greater Charlotte market with further expansion across North Carolina, including the Research Triangle region of Raleigh, Durham, and Chapel Hill. His development strategy prioritizes suburban growth corridors, college-adjacent neighborhoods with experienced local operators to support long-term, sustainable growth. The agreement represents a significant next phase of Batt’s investments in the brands and builds on more than 16 years of experience as a TCBY franchisee. With Georgia now included in his territory, Batt plans to carry the momentum established in the Carolinas into new markets while applying his experience operating and developing both brands. As he continues this growth, Batt is working closely with Famous Brands to identify and support franchisees who share his commitment to TCBY and Mrs. Fields and are equally as dedicated to building strong, lasting operations. “I’m proud to continue reinvesting in TCBY and Mrs. Fields,” said Samuel Batt, Franchise Owner. “These are iconic brands that generations of customers have known and loved for decades, and we continue to see that connection translate into strong performance today. Expanding across the Southeast gives us the opportunity to bring high-quality frozen yogurt and freshly baked treats to more communities throughout the region. I look forward to growing both brands and introducing them to even more families.” A franchisee since 2010, Batt has played a pivotal role in the evolution of TCBY, including piloting the brand’s first self-serve concept for the brand in Charlotte, an initiative that helped inform its broader rollout. In addition to operating his own locations, Batt supports other franchisees throughout the region by providing operational guidance and development support. He also takes pride in giving back to the communities his stores serve, having donated six figures over the years to local schools, sports organizations, and nonprofits. TCBY offers a broad selection of frozen yogurt flavors and treats designed to appeal to a range of tastes and dietary preferences. Its menu includes more than 50 soft-serve and 16 hand-scooped yogurt flavors, including low-fat, fat-free, dairy-free, gluten-free, vegan and no sugar added options. Guests can customize their orders with more than 35 toppings, including candy, fresh fruit, nuts and sauces. The menu at select locations also includes milkshakes, parfaits, sundaes, cakes, pies, chillers, sorbet fizz, and other frozen treats. For more than four decades, Mrs. Fields has delighted customers with its signature cookies, cookie cakes, brownies, and gift offerings. As the brand continues to evolve, it remains a destination for freshly baked treats that combine nostalgia with everyday indulgences for customers across generations. articles.title: Can Burger King Sustain Momentum? It Starts with What’s Still Left to Do
articles.titleKo: Can Burger King Sustain Momentum? It Starts with What’s Still Left to Do
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . A year ago, Sami Siddiqui fielded a similar question. What’s something people ask about Burger King, Popeyes, Tim Hortons, and Firehouse Subs owner Restaurant Brands International that surprises him? Or, similarly, what’s a topic he wonders doesn’t surface more often? Siddiqui, RBI’s CFO, and former president of Popeyes, speaking at the Barclays 19 th Annual Global Consumer Conference, said his response hasn’t changed much, year-over-year. But it has shifted a bit. The company, as you’d guess, gets a lot of asks about Burger King’s U.S. business, which represents about 17 percent of RBI’s operating income. Those still dominate the conversation. Yet people have begun progressing from questioning when a turnround will come to if it’s sustainable. Burger King U.S. in Q2 posted same-store sales growth of 8.5 percent (10 percent two-year stack). That outpaced the larger QSR burger field by north of 9 percentage points. And it followed a Q1 result of 5.8 percent (4.7 percent two-year). The narrative for Burger King throughout Reclaim the Flame, which turned four years old on September 9 , is none of it was flash-in-the-pan devised. It was structural and ran more than $2 billion, covering areas from marketing to store assets to, more recently, core upgrades of its Whopper and nuggets . Siddiqui said RBI’s answer splits between what’s happened over those four years and what’s left. With remodels, just a shade over 50 percent of the system has updated ( more here on how those are performing ). Meaning, naturally, close to half of the fleet has yet to tap into the sales bump witnessed in other parts of the business. Of elevated stores disclosed via Burger King’s 2026 FDD, 964 underwent a full remodel and 67 scrape and rebuilds. The average sales uplift was double-digits for each, but north of 25 percent for demolished restaurants. Full remodels appreciated an 11.9 percent average sales uplift, while scrape and rebuilds were at 26 percent. Stores that underwent a conversion to a double drive-thru observed average sales hikes of 16.8 percent (10.6 percent without). And restaurants that fixed from legacy to “modern image” posted average sales growth of 13.8 percent. Units from Burger King’s “20/20 Light” to a new look achieved 10.2 percent. Burger King still has a lot of work to do on store remodels and product upgrades. Lastly, Burger King’s most-present update—the “Sizzle” design—resulted in upticks of 14.9 percent. Simply, Siddiqui’s point is not a hollow one. The other corner of runway ahead is refranchising. Burger King has about 1,000 stores still to place in the “hands of the right operators,” he said. The brand took on a massive crop of corporate stores in early 2024 when it spent $1 billion to acquire its largest operator in Carrols. The goal being to sell those units back to smaller operators, and, ultimately, shift the company-run portfolio to a steady state level of about 300 locations. It was 1,100 last year. Burger King dealt the first batch ahead of schedule and said the latter half of 2026 would mark a ramp-up phase, with 2027 gathering speed. Again, Burger King has a ways to go. And like remodels from a more holistic view, the brand feels one of the reasons it’s enjoyed success of late is a “halo effect” where, from the look of stores to how they perform to the quality and consistency of products, customers are changing their perception of Burger King. It’s no longer a tired system. Siddiqui said the brand is selling more Whoppers now since upgrading the bun, mayo, and packaging. Whopper platform AUVs have climbed more than 20 percent since that campaign began in February. articles.title: Chi-Chi’s Revives Most-Requested Dishes, Introduces New Lunch Offerings
articles.titleKo: Chi-Chi’s Revives Most-Requested Dishes, Introduces New Lunch Offerings
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Chi-Chi's Seafood Nachos. Chi-Chi’s, the beloved Mexican restaurant brand that made its highly anticipated return last year, is continuing its comeback with the launch of a new lunch menu and the return of three of its most-requested legacy items: the Twice Grilled BBQ Burrito , Seafood Nachos , and Margarita Chicken Tacos using its beloved margarita marinade. The additions come as the brand looks to continue reintroducing itself to longtime fans and a new generation of diners. Since reopening in Minneapolis last fall , Chi-Chi’s has welcomed guests from across the country, many of whom have traveled specifically to relive memories associated with the iconic restaurant. Anchored by a new lunch menu designed for today’s diners, the latest offerings blend nostalgic guest favorites with fresh new flavors, showcasing the scratch-made recipes and vibrant Mexican dishes that have defined the Chi-Chi’s experience for generations. Featured menu items include: Twice Grilled BBQ Burrito: Chi-Chi’s takes burritos to the next level with a grilled entrée featuring a citrus-chipotle barbecue sauce, roasted peppers and onions, and a blend of melted asadero and Manchego cheeses. Available with chicken, ground beef or carne asada. Seafood Nachos: Crisp tortilla chips are loaded with crab, shrimp, creamy seafood sauce, cheddar cheese, sour cream and black olives for a shareable appetizer packed with coastal flavor. Margarita Chicken Tacos: Fresh and vibrant, these tacos combine seasoned chicken with avocado, Pico de Gallo, cheese and a cilantro-lime sauce for a bright, citrus-forward bite. The new lunch lineup also features a mini chimichanga, Margarita Chicken Sandwich, and soup-and-salad combinations, with all lunch offerings ranging from $10 to $15. For CEO Michael McDermott, the brand’s resurgence is also personal. As the son of Chi-Chi’s co-founder, Marno McDermott, he is leading the company’s return with a focus on honoring the legacy his father built while introducing the beloved brand to a new generation of guests. “Guests have been asking us for these menu items since the day we reopened,” said McDermott. “Bringing back the Twice Grilled BBQ Burrito, Margarita Chicken Tacos and Seafood Nachos was an easy decision, and the new lunch menu gives guests even more reasons to visit throughout the week. We’re focused on delivering the quality, value, hospitality and fun atmosphere that people remember from Chi-Chi’s while introducing the brand to a new generation of guests.” Known for its vibrant atmosphere, made-from-scratch recipes and strong value proposition, Chi-Chi’s prepares nearly everything in-house, from its salsas and dressings to its flour tortillas. The restaurant’s energetic dining room, popular happy hour offerings and commitment to quality ingredients continue to distinguish it in the Mexican dining category. Looking ahead, Chi-Chi’s is exploring additional growth opportunities and evaluating future locations as interest in the brand continues to grow. articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Clementine’s Ice Cr eam, the St. Louis-born ice cream brand known for its handcrafted, small-batch Nice, Non-Dairy and Naughty creations, is serving up its next phase of growth with the launch of its franchise opportunity. The announcement comes as Clementine’s prepares to open two new parlors in the Kansas City, Missouri area this October and November, as well as celebrating five consecutive years of being recognized on the 2026 Inc. 5000 list. These milestones mark a sweet spot in Clementine’s growth journey as the brand looks to introduce its distinct ice cream experience to new communities through franchising. Founded in 2015 by Tamara Keefe, Clementine’s has built a following around its innovative flavors, high-quality ingredients and memorable guest experience. Its menu spans both classic and unexpected creations, including its signature lineup of “Nice” elevated, chef-driven ice cream flavors, “Non-Dairy” flavors that are also vegan, and “ * Naughty” alcohol-infused flavors. As Clementine’s looks ahead, the brand is seeking franchise partners who share the brand’s passion for hospitality, community and, of course, really good ice cream. “Clementine’s has always been about creating something memorable, from the flavors we imagine to the experience we create,” said Tamara Keefe, founder and CEO of Clementine’s Ice Cream. “Being named to the Inc. 5000 for the fifth year in a row as we prepare to expand into Kansas City with two locations is an incredible testament to the hard work that we’ve put in. Opening our franchise opportunity to dedicated entrepreneurs represents where we’re headed next. We’ve built Clementine’s with a lot of heart and a commitment to quality, and I’m excited to find franchise partners who believe in our vision and want to help bring it to new communities.” The brand’s next phase of expansion will soon unveil two new parlors in the Kansas City market, with the first located at 1438 E Riverfront Dr in Kansas City, Missouri, opening in November and the second at 17165 W 87th St Parkway in Lenexa, Kansas, opening in late October. Clementine’s newest locations will introduce Kansas City guests to the full Clementine’s experience, from decadent, handcrafted flavors to a brand atmosphere designed to make a trip for ice cream feel like an event. Clementine’s upcoming parlors and recent inclusion on the 2026 Inc. 5000, ranking No. 4,312, represent the brand’s tremendous expansion trajectory, having grown 48% in the last three years, providing further validation as the company prepares to scale through franchising. To help propel the brand’s upward momentum, now is the perfect time to open its franchise opportunity to entrepreneurs, giving them the chance to bring an established premium ice cream concept to their own communities. Clementine’s franchisees will benefit from the brand’s vertically integrated production model, one-of-a-kind products, operating systems and support developed by the standout leadership team with years of expertise behind them. “Our goal is to grow Clementine’s thoughtfully, with franchise partners who understand that what makes this brand special goes far beyond the ice cream,” continued Keefe. “Success for us isn’t about growing as quickly as possible, it’s about finding the right partners, entering the right communities and building a brand that people are excited to be part of for years to come.” As the company continues to broaden its footprint, Clementine’s is seeking qualified franchise partners in Missouri, Kansas, Arkansas, Indiana, Kentucky, Tennessee, Iowa, and Illinois. Ideal franchisees will be community-minded and enthusiastic about building a local business, delivering standout guest experiences and growing alongside an emerging brand with unlimited potential. articles.title: The Gyro Project Opening 10th Location on October 15 in Hell’s Kitchen
articles.titleKo: The Gyro Project Opening 10th Location on October 15 in Hell’s Kitchen
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . The Gyro Project, a fast-fine Greek restaurant bringing authentic street food flavors to a modern setting, will open its 10th overall location at 600 9th Avenue in Manhattan’s Hell’s Kitchen on Thursday, October 15, continuing the brand’s rapid expansion throughout New York City and the Tri-State area. The approximately 1,200-square-foot restaurant will feature 14 indoor seats, including window and counter-style seating, and will offer The Gyro Project’s lunch and dinner menus for dine-in, takeout and delivery. Designed with an aesthetic similar to the brand’s newest location on the Upper East Side, the new restaurant will bring The Gyro Project’s contemporary Greek atmosphere to one of Manhattan’s most vibrant neighborhoods. The Hell’s Kitchen location will feature fan-favorite items including classic gyro pita wraps featuring chicken, pork and lamb & beef; hearty platters served with rice, salad and pita; traditional dips such as tzatziki and hummus; loaded Greek fries; and the brand’s signature Greek frozen yogurt. The location will also become the first in New York City to offer The Gyro Project’s Dubai Chocolate Froyo, adding a popular modern flavor to the brand’s Greek frozen yogurt lineup. The opening of 600 9th Avenue follows the June debut of The Gyro Project’s ninth overall location at 1260 Lexington Avenue on Manhattan’s Upper East Side. That location also marked the New York City debut of the brand’s popular Feta-Brined Rotisserie Chicken, a family-style offering that serves approximately three to four people and has become a customer favorite at The Gyro Project’s flagship New Jersey location(s). Founded by childhood friends and restaurateurs George Tenedios and Spiro Kokkosis, The Gyro Project was created to fill a void for high-quality Greek cuisine in New York and New Jersey. Since debuting its first location in Fort Lee, New Jersey, in July 2023, the brand has built a loyal following for its signature pita wraps, mixed grill platters, mezedes, specialty fries, and Greek froyo – all rooted in authentic recipes and bold Mediterranean flavors. “We’re thrilled to reach this milestone with the opening of our 10th location at 600 9th Avenue,” said George Tenedios, co-owner of The Gyro Project. “Hell’s Kitchen is such an energetic and diverse neighborhood, and we’re excited to bring our authentic Greek flavors and fast-fine approach to the community. We’re also especially excited to introduce Dubai Chocolate Froyo to New York City for the first time and continue finding new ways to give our guests something to look forward to.” As part of The Gyro Project’s commitment to supporting the next generation of culinary and hospitality professionals, students from Food and Finance High School in Hell’s Kitchen will be invited to a “Building a Brand” session the day before opening on October 14, followed by an entrepreneurship Q&A with George Tenedios. He will share insights from his experience building and growing a successful restaurant brand. The program will give students an opportunity to learn firsthand about entrepreneurship, branding, leadership and the business of hospitality, while connecting classroom learning with real-world experience. The Gyro Project’s expansion reflects the growing demand for its fast-fine approach to Greek cuisine, combining the speed and accessibility of a fast-casual restaurant with high-quality ingredients, generous portions and authentic Greek flavors. With the opening of Hell’s Kitchen, the brand will have 10 locations across New York and New Jersey, including seven locations throughout New York City and three in New Jersey. articles.title: Starbucks Weighing $3 Billion Japan Deal: Reports
articles.titleKo: Starbucks Weighing $3 Billion Japan Deal: Reports
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . The company’s global same-store sales climbed 7.9 percent last quarter. Starbucks could be on the verge of another significant overseas deal. The company , per a report from Reuters , is considering offloading a majority stake in its Japan business. It would potentially value Starbucks’ largest overseas company-operated market at about $3 billion, two sources informed the publication. Starbucks’ Japan operations cover 1,883 stores and account for nearly 9 percent of the chain’s entire global footprint (September 2025 data). Reuters said Starbucks collected pitches from “several financial advisers” on options for the business and remains open to selling a majority stake. While Starbucks’ Japan valuation is not public, sources suggested it was worth about $3 billion, as noted. Still, the level of stake or any sale has not yet been determined. And what valuation Starbucks ultimately seeks remains subject to negotiations. In an emailed response to Reuters, Starbucks said it’s continually assessing the best structure “to be the most meaningful to customers and create value for shareholders” in Japan. This isn’t the first time news of a potential deal surfaced. Bloomberg in June also reported Starbucks was weighing options for its Japan division, include a stake sale. Sources said Starbucks’ Japan business is expected to attract interest from global and local buyout firms, and a formal process could ignite as early as Q4. Starbucks has held full control of the Japan arm since 2014, when it bought out Sazaby League for roughly $914 million, which valued the operation those days at $1.5 billion. Starbucks had purchased the remaining 60.5 percent share of Starbucks Coffee Japan Ltd in a two-step deal. Starbucks Japan operated as a joint venture between the company and Sazaby League dating to 1995. That summer, Sazaby approach Starbucks about selling its stake. There were about 1,050 cafes in Japan (meaning it’s added more than 800 since). Japan, according to reports, has among the highest profit margin locations globally. The purchase price for Sazaby’s 39.5 percent stake was $505 million. Shortly after the deal, Starbucks began buying the remaining 21 percent held by public and option shareholders of Starbucks Japan’s common stock for $408.5 million. TD Securities analysts in June said monetizing Starbucks’ Japan unit would make strategic sense, Reuters reported, because the market is not central to Starbucks’ brand. And it could further allow management under CEO Brian Niccol to sharpen focus on reviving the core U.S. business. International same-store sales grew 5.7 percent in Q3, with Niccol spotlighting “continued strength in Japan and the U.K.” during Starbucks’ earnings call. The company’s global same-store sales climbed 7.9 percent in the quarter for a two-year stack of 5.9 percent. Traffic increased 4.2 percent (2.2 percent two year). Starbucks’ U.S. comps rose 7.9 percent as well (two-year view of 5.9 percent) on traffic of 4.2 percent (0.2 percent two year). Ticket hiked 3.6 percent and was 5.6 percent higher over two years. Food attachment set Q3 records at U.S. company-run restaurants, with the strongest gains in the afternoon. Pricing contributed less than a point of ticket growth. Starbucks opened 175 net new stores in Q3, exiting at 41,304. The U.S. had 16,933 of those. Overall, Starbucks ended Q3 with 18,371 restaurants in North America, a 2 percent decline year-over-year from 18,734. Starbucks last year entered an agreement to form a joint venture with Boyu Capital, an alternative investment firm with more than 200 portfolio companies, to operate Starbucks retail in China. Under the deal, which closed in April, Boyu held an up to 60 percent interest in Starbucks’ area business. articles.title: Are Restaurants Sabotaging Their Own Staffing?
articles.titleKo: Are Restaurants Sabotaging Their Own Staffing?
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . A restaurant should know what it is looking for before it starts looking. Restaurant hiring has never been especially simple. Managers are balancing callouts, service rushes, food costs, guest issues, and all the other fires that come with running a dining room. Recruiting often gets pushed down the list—until a restaurant is suddenly short-staffed and needs someone, anyone, on the schedule. That is where Karen Browne sees operators get themselves into trouble. “Desperate hiring managers will do desperate things,” says Browne, CEO of Chicago’s One Off Hospitality, the powerhouse group behind Windy City staples like avec, The Publican, Big Star, and Publican Quality Bread. “When they’re understaffed, they’re hiring bodies. They’re not pre-screening for the successful attributes you need for the job.” RELATED: How an Industry Outsider Rewired an Iconic Restaurant Empire It is a familiar cycle in restaurants: A staffing need becomes urgent, standards slip, and the new hire is expected to figure things out in an environment that may already be stretched thin. Turnover follows, the team gets frustrated, and managers are right back where they started. Browne’s answer is not particularly flashy. It is to slow down, get clear about what a role actually requires, and build a process that does not disappear the second service gets busy. That perspective comes from an unusual intersection. At One Off, Browne helms a nine-time James Beard Award-winning collective responsible for some of Chicago’s most iconic dining destinations. But before stepping in as CEO in 2019, she built her career far outside dining rooms, leading massive human-capital organizations and helping major companies design hiring systems at scale. At One Off, she has applied some of that same thinking to a business where the people side can often feel more reactive than strategic. Start with the person, not the open shift The first mistake, Browne says, is hiring around immediate availability rather than the traits that make someone successful in a specific job. A restaurant should know what it is looking for before it starts looking. That might mean warmth and confidence at the host stand, composure on a busy line, attention to detail behind the bar, or the ability to keep a team steady during a difficult shift. Whatever the role calls for, operators need a way to identify it before the interview turns into a simple question of whether the candidate can start Friday. “You need to really take the pill and just slow down and design a system, and then work to the system,” Browne says. That does not mean every hiring decision needs to become a drawn-out corporate exercise. In fact, Browne believes speed matters. The point is to be intentional before urgency takes over. Get out from behind the inbox For Browne, restaurant recruiting is still a decidedly human process. Job boards and applicant tracking systems have a role, but she does not believe an email chain is enough to win over strong candidates. “This is hospitality,” she says. “If you’re sending emails, you’re not going to get the best candidates.” Browne still goes into One Off’s candidate pipeline and calls applicants herself, particularly when a part of the business needs people. That hands-on approach is partly about filling roles, but it is also about setting a tone: Talent matters, and outreach should feel personal. Restaurants spend plenty of time thinking about how to make guests feel welcomed and seen. Browne says candidates deserve a version of that same consideration. A quick phone conversation can reveal more than a resume ever will, while also giving a prospective employee a sense of the people and culture behind the job posting. articles.title: The Hidden Tax Reporting Trap That Could Cost Your Restaurant Thousands
articles.titleKo: The Hidden Tax Reporting Trap That Could Cost Your Restaurant Thousands
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . The key to avoiding penalties for these penalties isn’t complicated. Running a restaurant means juggling a hundred things at once—food costs, staffing, customer experience, and keeping the lights on. Tax forms are probably the last thing on a restaurant operator’s mind. But here’s something most restaurant owners don’t realize: a simple typo on a Form W-2 or Form 1099 can trigger IRS penalties that add up fast. In an industry with high employee turnover, it is critical that restaurant owners, managers, and their advisors verify new employee information before sending that first paycheck. Picture this: a restaurant hires 50 new employees in 2026. A rushed manager transposes two digits in a Social Security Number (SSN) during onboarding. In January 2027, the restaurant files the W-2s with the IRS and issue copies to the employees—and a year later, an IRS penalty notice arrives. At $340 per each W-2 filed with the IRS and the same amount for each W-2 issued to an employee, those small mistakes can snowball into serious money. The good news? There’s a little-known protective strategy that can help restaurant owners avoid these penalties—and it doesn’t require a CPA or in-house legal team to implement. Why This Matters More for Restaurants The restaurant industry has one of the highest turnover rates of any employment sector—often exceeding 70 percent annually . That means more W-2s, more 1099s for delivery drivers or contractors, and more opportunities for SSN/TIN mismatches. Every incorrect SSN or TIN on those forms is a potential IRS penalty. The IRS assesses penalties per return and per payee statement. For 2026 filings (due in January 2027), the penalty is $340 for each W-2 or 1099 with an incorrect or missing SSN/TIN—and for small businesses with gross receipts under $5 million, penalties can reach up to $1,366,000 ($4,098,500 for larger businesses). If the IRS decides a restaurant “intentionally disregarded” the SSN/TIN rules, penalties jump to $680 per return with no cap at all on the penalty amount. And the cherry on top is that interest accrues on those penalties. Before imposing penalties, the IRS typically sends a notice (called a CP2100 or CP2100A) flagging the problem. But here’s the trap: sometimes they skip the warning and go straight to issuing a penalty notice. Either way, the restaurant generally has a limited window—usually 45 days—to respond. There’s another wrinkle: if a restaurant receives one of these notices and continues paying an employee or contractor without fixing the issue, the business may be required to withhold 24 percent of each payment to that employee or contractor and send it to the IRS. That’s an awkward conversation to have with a food supplier or bookkeeper. The Three-Step Protection Strategy Most Restaurant Owners Don’t Know About The key to avoiding penalties for these penalties isn’t complicated, but it does require building verification into the hiring processand the best part is that a restaurant owner or manager can use them year-round. Step 1: Restaurant operators should collect the right paperwork before the first shift. Generally, this means giving each new employee a Form W-4 , and independent contractors (like some delivery drivers or consultants), a Form W-9 . Before any payments go out the door, an owner or manager should obtain a completed Form W-4 or Form W-9 with copies of any identification (like a Social Security card) used to verify the forms. This sounds basic, but in the fast-paced restaurant world, it’s often skipped or done sloppily. Step 2: Restaurant operators should verify SSNs immediately, don’t wait until tax season . Here’s the part most restaurant owners don’t know: the IRS and Social Security Administration (SSA) offer tools to check whether a name and SSN match. articles.title: Restaurant sales lead hospitality growth in August
articles.titleKo: Restaurant sales lead hospitality growth in August
articles.originalSummary: Restaurant sales rose 2.4% year-on-year in August as Britain’s hospitality sector recorded its fourth consecutive month of growth, according to the latest NIQ RSM Hospitality Business Tracker. Like-for-like sales across leading managed hospitality groups increased 0.8% compared with August 2025, although growth slowed from the 1.4% recorded in July, which NIQ says was boosted by the men’s football World Cup. The latest result was the third strongest monthly performance of 2026 so far but remained below the current rate of consumer price inflation. According to the tracker, hospitality has now failed to record real-terms monthly growth for 16 consecutive months.

articles.title: How Danny Grant Built a $35M Powerhouse by Reimagining the Modern Steakhouse Experience
articles.titleKo: How Danny Grant Built a $35M Powerhouse by Reimagining the Modern Steakhouse Experience
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . When Danny Grant set out to open a steakhouse concept in Chicago in 2015, he describes the general feeling as, “Chicago has plenty of steakhouses—why do we need another one?” But he saw an invisible gap in the market that others missed. An underlying mission started to take shape as Grant and his team realized they wanted to disrupt the “masculine” steakhouse narrative that was pervasive in the early 2010s. And thus, a new concept was born from the ashes of steakhouses past: Maple & Ash. “We wanted to use our pedigree and our team and our culture to disrupt what that narrative was at the time. If you look back around that time, everything was always very masculine in a steakhouse,” Grant says. “When we initially started this, it was to appeal to foodies and to be a bit more feminine and sexy and less masculine, and we’ve been playing that game for a while now.” The growing steakhouse concept from the two-Michelin-star chef Grant and Maple Hospitality Group has become a standout in Chicago, where it became the city’s highest-grossing independent restaurant in 2024, with sales of more than $35 million and an average check of $160. It has since expanded to other cities including Miami, Scottsdale, and Boston, and is headed to New York City next. For Grant, the ability to create a concept that pushes the boundaries of what a steakhouse can be—with an unapologetically indulgent experience that diners find worth the higher cost—comes down to building trust. HQ: Chicago Cuisine: Wood-fired steakhouse Units: 4 Year founded: 2015 Maple & Ash blends an upscale wood-fired steakhouse and seafood destination with high-energy hospitality and high-end design elements. A moody interior design created by Studio K mixes mid-century modern style with chic textured mirrored glass walls, clad in custom Benheim glass. The dinner menu features dry-aged steaks, wagyu, fire-roasted seafood towers, caviar, wood-fired specialties, and other specialty entrées like Pillows of Love, a signature hand-folded ricotta agnolotti pasta dish bathed in brown butter and topped with shaved winter truffle. The team leans into more cutesy names, with a section of the menu dubbed “Arm Candy” offering luxury steak toppers and sauces like Alaskan King Crab Oscar, roasted bone marrow, and beefed-up butter. Guests can also opt for the tasting menu option, labeled “I Don’t Give a F*ck”—a signature, multi-course chef’s tasting experience featuring the steakhouse’s most popular and extravagant dishes, with a collection of fire-roasted shellfish, boutique farm steaks, freshly caught seafood, and seasonal delicacies. It’s priced around $225 per person depending on the location, with optional wine pairings available at an extra cost. Then there’s the beverage menu, which follows the same maximalist, luxury-forward approach. Signature cocktails sport names like Reckless Jorge, Good Trouble, Shady Lady, and Unnecessary Attention, alongside elevated takes on classics such as a Maple & Ash Old Fashioned made with the restaurant’s Blanton’s barrel selection, Amaro Montenegro, sherry, Japanese maple sugar, and house bitters. The spirits list is similarly expansive, stretching from rare bourbons, Japanese whiskies, and high-end Scotch to prestige tequila, mezcal, cognac, and caviar-studded martinis, while a “No F*@king Alcohol” section keeps the energy going for sober-curious guests with zero-proof cocktails built around Seedlip, Pathfinder, fruit, botanicals, and spice. articles.title: El Pollo Loco Announces Grand Opening for Second Albuquerque Restaurant
articles.titleKo: El Pollo Loco Announces Grand Opening for Second Albuquerque Restaurant
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . El Pollo Loco, the nation’s leading restaurant for citrus-marinated, fire-grilled chicken, announced a community grand opening celebration for its second Albuquerque restaurant, located at 3811 Ellison Dr NW, Albuquerque, NM 87114. While the restaurant officially opens today, September 16, El Pollo Loco is inviting the community to celebrate the new restaurant with a special grand opening event on Friday, September 25. The celebration begins at 11:00 a.m. with a ribbon-cutting ceremony alongside the Albuquerque Chamber of Commerce, followed by music from a local radio from 11:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. to keep the energy and excitement going. To celebrate, the first 50 guests will receive a FREE* Pollo Bowl, chips, and a large fountain drink. Guests also may enter for the chance to win $250 cash from the restaurant’s builder, Archmill House. The party continues later in the day from 5:00 p.m. to 7:00 p.m. when the restaurant will offer a FREE 2-Piece Chicken Leg & Thigh Meal for in-store guests**, with no purchase necessary, while supplies last. El Pollo Loco’s 2-Piece Chicken Leg & Thigh Meal features two pieces of the company’s legendary fire-grilled chicken, a leg and thigh, grilled low over an open flame. The meal includes a side of seasoned rice, made in-house using enriched long-grain rice with a savory blend of tomatoes and spices, along with Pinto Beans simmered with chopped serrano peppers for a subtle kick. Operated by Ashim Chopra, CEO of CB Pollo NM 1, the new Albuquerque restaurant marks the franchise group’s fourth El Pollo Loco location, and second in the region. “We’ve been truly encouraged by the response El Pollo Loco has received in Albuquerque, and we’re proud to continue investing in this community,” said Chopra. “Our newest restaurant gives us another opportunity to share the bold flavors, warm hospitality and fire-grilled meals our guests love, while creating a place where neighbors can gather, celebrate and make new memories together.” The restaurant will be open daily from 10:00 a.m. until 10:00 p.m., offering dine-in, drive-thru and takeout service. Known for its signature citrus-marinated, fire-grilled chicken, El Pollo Loco prepares its food daily using quality ingredients. From its classic chicken meals to burritos, bowls and handcrafted sides, the brand continues to deliver bold, flavorful options that appeal to a wide range of guests. Available now through Oct. 12 at all 12 Polly’s Pies locations, the seasonal lineup puts a Polly’s spin on classic German-inspired comfort food. Fall is making its way to Polly’s Pies, and that means it’s time for pumpkin, warm spices and a little Oktoberfest flavor. This season, the Southern California legacy restaurant is bringing back a lineup of fall favorites alongside a selection of German-inspired dishes made for cool-weather cravings, available now through Oct. 12. Back by popular demand are four bakery favorites: Pumpkin Pie , Pumpkin Dream Pie , Pumpkin Maple Crunch Pie and Pumpkin Maple Crunch Muffin . Guests can also get into the spirit with Pumpkin Spice Drip Coffee , available throughout the month of November. For those looking for something savory, Polly’s Pies is serving up a full Oktoberfest menu with classic flavors and a few Polly’s twists. The seasonal lineup includes: Brat & Eggs — $14.99: A Mattern Nuerenberg brat served with two large eggs and Polly’s potato pancakes, garnished with sour cream and green onions. The plate comes with pub mustard sauce and a daily bakery item of choice. Guests can upgrade to a Pumpkin Maple Crunch Muffin for an additional 99¢. Pumpkin Pancakes — $14.99: Two buttermilk pumpkin pancakes made with Coach’s Oats and topped with house-made cinnamon whipped cream, served with two large eggs and a choice of Jones Dairy Farms smoked sausage or applewood smoked bacon. Pretzel Bites — $7.99: Warm, soft pretzel bites served with rich and creamy beer cheese for dipping. Mattern Sausage Platter — $16.99: A traditional Nuerenberg brat and smoked cheddar brat served over braised red cabbage with apples and finished with a pub mustard drizzle. Served with Polly’s famous potato pancakes, sour cream and green onions. Pretzel Burger — $15.99: A juicy 6 oz. beef patty topped with applewood smoked bacon, grilled onions, pickles and pub mustard, tucked into a toasted pretzel bun and drenched in beer cheese. Served with french fries. “Our guests wait all year for favorites like pumpkin pancakes and Pumpkin Pie, and Oktoberfest gives us a fun way to add something different to the season,” said Meghan Meadors, advertising and public relations manager at Polly’s Pies. “It’s comfort food, fall flavors and a good reason to gather around the table.” The Oktoberfest menu and seasonal pumpkin offerings are available for a limited time at all 12 Polly’s Pies locations. articles.title: Fuku and Peter Luger Partner on Limited-Edition Sando
articles.titleKo: Fuku and Peter Luger Partner on Limited-Edition Sando
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Fuku, the quick, chef-driven eatery from chef and cultural icon David Chang known for its signature spicy fried chicken sandwich and growing lineup of unexpected collaborations, is teaming up with legendary Peter Luger Steak House for a limited-edition sando. Launching Friday, Oct. 9, the Fuku x Peter Luger Sando will be available for dine-in at Fuku’s Coral Gables and West Palm Beach locations, as well as for takeout and delivery. Served on a Martin’s potato roll, the Fuku x Peter Luger Sando features a choice of Fuku’s spicy or mild fried chicken topped with Peter Luger Extra Thick-Cut Bacon, white onion, and “Luger Jam” made from Peter Luger’s iconic steak sauce and shallots. The combination brings smoky bacon, savory crunch and the signature tang of Peter Luger Steak Sauce to Fuku’s craveable, hand-breaded fried chicken. Guests can also pair the sando with Luger Lager, Peter Luger’s collaborative beer with Threes Brewing of Brooklyn. “This collaboration grew out of a casual lunch at Fuku that quickly turned into a conversation with our culinary team about what we could create together,” said Fuku Chief Brand Officer, Kaitlin Weinman. “We started exploring how Peter Luger’s iconic flavors could work with our fried chicken, and the idea took off from there. The finished sando is unexpected, craveable and a great celebration of the New York roots our brands share.” “Fuku took two of our classics and made something really special,” said Daniel Turtel, VP of Peter Luger Steak House. “It’s a fun, unexpected crossover that we can’t wait to see in South Florida.” Both born in New York City, Fuku and Peter Luger have built loyal followings by creating unmistakable flavors that stand the test of time. The collaboration reimagines some of Peter Luger’s most recognizable elements, including its thick-cut bacon and signature steak sauce (both available in grocery stores nationwide), through Fuku’s bold, chef-driven approach to fried chicken. articles.title: Haraz Coffee Opens Latest Location in College Station
articles.titleKo: Haraz Coffee Opens Latest Location in College Station
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Haraz Coffee, a fast-growing specialty coffee brand, opened its newest location at 2711 Texas Ave. S., Suite 400, College Station. The opening marks the brand’s continued expansion across the United States and its first location near the Texas A&M University campus. The new College Station shop officially opened its doors Sept. 16 and operates 8 a.m. to 11 p.m., seven days a week. The location seats 70 guests inside and out, employs 18 people and offers Haraz’s full menu of specialty coffee drinks and fresh pastries in a space designed for both quick visits and longer stays. With Texas A&M students as a core part of its customer base, the shop was built to be a welcoming study and gathering spot close to campus. Known for blending rich hospitality traditions with modern cafe design, Haraz has built its presence across North America by creating an elevated “third place” — a welcoming space outside of home and work where people gather, connect and build community. The brand sources high-quality beans and delivers rich, aromatic brews with distinctive, carefully crafted flavor profiles, built on a hospitality-first approach designed to outlast any single trend. The College Station location features Haraz’s full menu of specialty coffee and espresso drinks, including lattes, cappuccinos, macchiatos, cold brew, frappes and signature Haraz drinks, along with ceremonial matcha, iced refreshers, teas, smoothies, pastries, desserts and light cafe offerings. The menu also includes traditional drinks such as Adeni chai and Sana’ani-style coffee. With extended hours and a warm, welcoming cafe environment, Haraz is designed as a place where guests can linger, work, study, gather with friends or simply enjoy a quality drink at their own pace. “As a College Station local, I have watched this community grow, and I wanted to build a coffee shop that gives students and neighbors alike a place that feels like home. We encourage people to stay a while, and we have made sure there are plenty of outlets for laptops and phones, which matters so much for students. Haraz is about specialty coffee done right, and I cannot wait for people to try our fresh drinks and pastries and make this their new favorite spot in Aggieland,” said Ali Kareem, owner of the College Station location. The College Station opening adds to Haraz Coffee’s growing national footprint, which now includes more than 60 locations nationwide, with 250 more in development. Texas has emerged as one of the brand’s most active markets, with locations now open in Arlington, Katy, College Station, Sugar Land, Pearland, Cypress and two San Antonio locations, alongside recent openings in the Piedmont Triad region of North Carolina, Pleasanton and Mountain View, California, and Minneapolis, Minnesota. “Texas has been an incredible market for Haraz. From Arlington to San Antonio, and now College Station, communities across the state have embraced what we do, and that means everything to us. We are proud to keep growing here and grateful for how warmly Texas has welcomed Haraz every step of the way,” said Hamzah Nasser, founder and CEO, Haraz Coffee. Slutty Vegan, the world-famous, woman-owned plant-based burger brand founded by entrepreneur, author and reality-television star Pinky Cole Hayes, has officially signed a franchise agreement to bring the rapidly growing concept to Cincinnati, marking the brand’s third market in the state of Ohio. The agreement was signed by Soul Republic Hospitality Group, led by founder Akin Affrica, the same operator behind Slutty Vegan’s Columbus and Cleveland locations. This reinvestment into an additional location builds on the strength of the partnership and rising demand for the brand across the state. As the company continues to scale with experienced operators, Slutty Vegan has prioritized franchise partners who understand both the business fundamentals and the culture behind the brand. “Cincinnati was always part of the plan for us,” said Akin Affrica, Founder of Soul Republic Hospitality Group. “After signing on for Cleveland and Columbus, we saw firsthand how much demand there is for this brand in Ohio. Adding Cincinnati was an easy decision. We know the market, we know the guest, and we are ready to bring that same energy here.” Slutty Vegan’s Columbus and Cleveland locations are anticipated to open in the fall of 2026. Additional details on the Cincinnati location, including its address and opening timeline, will be made public as the buildout progresses. “When a franchise partner comes back to invest in a third market, that further compounds the fact that our brand is valuable and in demand,” said Pinky Cole Hayes, Founder and CEO of Slutty Vegan. “Ohio is primed for a concept like Slutty vegan, and Cincinnati rounds out the top three markets in the state.” Since launching in Atlanta in 2018, Slutty Vegan has grown from a viral burger concept into a nationally recognized brand known for bold flavors, high-energy customer experiences, and community impact. The brand’s founder, Pinky Cole Hayes, is a best-selling author and philanthropist who built the brand from a single food truck into a cultural phenomenon. Cole Hayes has continued her rise to stardom this year as a cast member of Bravo’s The Real Housewives of Atlanta, bringing her boldness and business savvy to one of television’s most-watched franchises and introducing Slutty Vegan to millions of new fans. articles.titleKo: Crunchtime Launches Industry’s First Truly Connected Kitchen in Unified Suite
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Crunchtime, the market leader in restaurant operations management software, announced the launch of the industry’s first connected operations management suite, centralizing common workflows on the kitchen display system (KDS) and delivering the most comprehensive cross-system insights in one place. The launch delivers on the promise of cross-product connections stemming from the company’s 2025 merger with QSR Automations. By connecting Crunchtime Kitchen, Crunchtime Ops Execution, and Crunchtime Inventory, the KDS screen transforms into a unified operational command center, enabling critical workflows — such as viewing prep instructions, logging waste, and completing operational tasks — to happen directly on the line where teams are already working. Customers will improve profitability by reducing waste and will drive efficiency by eliminating common back-of-house friction points. “In modern multi-unit restaurant environments, operational friction often stems from fragmented software that requires teams to interact with multiple disparate devices throughout the shift,” said Brian Herr, SVP of Product at Crunchtime. “The connections we’re announcing today eliminate these silos, ensuring that daily execution is managed on the KDS, where front-line teams are already working on a familiar system they use every shift.” Supercharging the Restaurant Operations Lifecycle on the KDS Enabling key workflows across core products keeps the front line in the flow and gives GMs assurance that the back of house is operating efficiently: Seamless Task Execution: Tasks built in Crunchtime Ops Execution can display directly on KDS screens alongside incoming orders and get bumped without breaking stride or logging into another application. Prep Instructions: Prep recommendations, driven by AI forecasting from Crunchtime Inventory, surface directly on the KDS, guiding kitchen teams and preventing over- and under-prepping. Waste Logging: Team members can now log food waste directly on the KDS screen, which automatically updates Crunchtime Inventory, giving operators more accurate inventory data and reducing missed waste entries. Unified Intelligence Reveals New Insights By connecting Crunchtime Kitchen to Crunchtime Insights, critical service and reservation data is added to the unified intelligence layer that powers the Crunchtime suite and guides data-driven decisions. Speed-of-service metrics, ticket times, cook-time variance, and reservation data now sit alongside inventory, labor, POS, and execution data, giving operations leaders a single, comprehensive view of performance and helping them identify blind spots they might otherwise miss. “By bringing all of this data together in a single view along with AI-driven analysis, we’re changing the landscape of modern restaurant decision-making,” said John Raguin, CEO of Crunchtime. “With a single source of truth, GMs and above-store leaders can make more proactive decisions and uncover new insights, driving even greater efficiency, consistency, and profitability.” See Crunchtime Products Working Together Like Never Before For a deep dive into these new cross-product connections, join the live launch event today, September 16, to hear directly from Crunchtime product experts on how these updates can supercharge your operations. Crunchtime will also be showcasing these powerful new capabilities at upcoming industry events, including FS/TEC in Grapevine, TX (Booth #404) and the Hospitality Tech Expo in London, England (Stand #HT1200). To learn more, visit https://www.crunchtime.com/connected-ops . The post Crunchtime Launches Industry’s First Truly Connected Kitchen in Unified Suite appeared first on QSR Magazine .
