As CMO, Dougher will oversee Mountain Mike’s comprehensive suite of integrated marketing strategies and activations. Mountain Mike’s Pizza, a leading family-style pizza chain for nearly 50 years, and home of the legendary crispy, curly pepperoni, massive 20-inch Mountain-sized pizzas and dough made fresh daily, has appointed Sheena Dougher as Chief Marketing Officer. Dougher brings more than 15 years of multidimensional restaurant marketing experience to the role. Her impressive professional portfolio spans brand strategy, integrated marketing, media, advertising, public relations and social media. She most recently served as Vice President of Brand Marketing at Jack in the Box. “Sheena’s track record is highlighted by her ability to translate brand strategy into tangible business results, and her numerous attributes as a seasoned marketer will further strengthen our brand position, drive traffic and sales, deepen our connections in the communities we serve and help introduce Mountain Mike’s to new guests and new regions across the country,” said Jim Metevier, Chief Executive Officer of Mountain Mike’s Pizza. “For nearly a half-century, our chain has built a strong foundation underpinned by product quality, category differentiation and systemwide passion among our valued franchise partners, and with Sheena’s acute understanding of how effective national marketing and local restaurant successes intersect to impact brand performance, we expect to accelerate our climb to the top of the segment.” As CMO, Dougher will oversee Mountain Mike’s comprehensive suite of integrated marketing strategies and activations, while creating new avenues to build on the brand’s many core strengths that showcase what distinguishes Mountain Mike’s from other pizza concepts. She’s expected to implement an array of thoughtful marketing initiatives that reinforce the brand’s product quality and distinctive identity. Dougher’s multifaceted areas of focus will include increasing brand awareness in new and existing markets, strengthening connections with local communities and driving sales. She also will support franchisee growth and restaurant-level performance, while developing opportunities across emerging channels, including B2B and catering. In her previous role, Dougher oversaw brand strategy across public relations and social media, brand content, paid media and regional marketing. She held several marketing leadership positions with the organization and led award-winning and high-profile brand initiatives, including the Effie Award-winning “The Return of Mark Hamill” campaign in 2023. She has been recognized as a Business Insider Brand Marketing Rising Star, and she has received a Brand Innovators Women in Marketing Industry Innovation Award. Last year, she was named one of Reuters’ Trailblazing Women. Before Jack in the Box, Dougher held marketing roles with Rubio’s Restaurants, Garden Fresh Restaurants and Sammy’s Woodfired Pizza, managing brand marketing, product launches, digital strategy and field marketing. At Mountain Mike’s, she succeeds Carol DeNembo, who previously served as CMO. “What stands out most about Mountain Mike’s Pizza is the strength of the brand, the quality of the product and the genuine commitment from the people behind both,” said Dougher. “There’s a significant opportunity to deepen the foundation and amplify the Mountain Mike’s narrative by sharpening what makes the brand unique, bringing a truly remarkable brand story to more people and creating stronger guest connections in the communities we serve, and I am eager to help turn the opportunity into meaningful brand and business growth.” The post Mountain Mike’s Pizza Appoints Sheena Dougher Chief Marketing Officer appeared first on QSR Magazine .

The World Food Championships announced a new partnership with Sysco, the global leader in selling, marketing, and distributing food and related products to customers who prepare meals away from home. Sysco will join WFC2026 as an Official Platform Partner, bringing together its extensive foodservice network, culinary expertise, and portfolio of leading brands for an expanded presence throughout the World Food Championships in Indianapolis. The partnership will make Sysco the exclusive partner in the Foodservice segment and will provide the company with significant presence throughout the WFC experience. As part of the agreement, the Taste of Indiana stage will be named the Sysco Demo Stage, with the Sysco name incorporated throughout event materials, signage, schedules, and stage callouts. Sysco culinary experts will conduct a variety of live demonstrations throughout the event, creating opportunities to connect professional chefs, competitors, and consumers through food and culinary education. “Sysco brings an incredible combination of scale, culinary expertise, local market relationships, and a deep understanding of the foodservice industry to the World Food Championships,” said Mike McCloud, Founder and CEO of the World Food Championships. “This partnership goes well beyond putting a logo on a wall. Sysco is becoming part of the platform that connects our competitors, chefs, brands, consumers, and the broader foodservice community. Their commitment to supporting culinary professionals and their ability to activate across so many areas of WFC makes this a tremendous addition to our 2026 championship.” Sysco will also serve as the Presenting Partner of the WFC Chef Category , one of the championship’s ten core competition categories. The partnership will put Sysco products directly into the hands of WFC’s elite culinary competitors, including White Marble Farms Pork Loin , which will serve as the required ingredient for the Chef Category Final Round. Competitors will be challenged to showcase their culinary creativity and technical skill while transforming the featured ingredient into a championship-worthy dish. A significant Sysco presence will also anchor the festival floor, with a 1,600-square-foot activation space showcasing the breadth of Sysco’s foodservice capabilities and the specialized expertise of its participating partners. Sysco Indianapolis will serve as the local hub for the activation, while each participating company will play a distinct role across the WFC2026 experience. Certified Angus Beef will support the inaugural Burger Battle , bringing its premium beef expertise to one of WFC’s newest consumer-facing competitions. FreshPoint will highlight the importance of fresh produce and support produce-focused elements throughout the event, while Superior Fresh will bring its premium salmon to the outdoor live-fire consumer tasting, expanding its role from the Culinary Combine into an opportunity for attendees to experience the product firsthand. European Imports will help support the established Sysco Dessert Pantry while also integrating into Dessert Smash , connecting its specialty ingredients and products to WFC’s sweet-focused programming. In addition, Buckhead Meat & Seafood will represent Sysco’s specialty protein capabilities, with its products and expertise incorporated across multiple competition elements. Together, the participating companies will help create an interactive destination where attendees can sample products, discover new ingredients, connect with culinary professionals, and see firsthand how Sysco and its family of specialty businesses support chefs and foodservice operators. Daily sampling, demonstrations, and additional consumer engagement will make the Sysco activation a destination throughout WFC2026. The partnership will also extend into the WFC judging experience

articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . The new brand transformation, created in partnership with global branding agency JKR, will support the company's next phase of growth. Tropical Smoothie Cafe today unveiled a full-scale brand transformation bringing its “Eat Some Good!” philosophy to life through a new brand identity and guest experience. It all starts with a fresh way of defining tropical, as a state of mind that shows up everywhere guests engage with the brand across digital and in-cafe touchpoints. “What makes Tropical Smoothie Cafe special is our ability to bring together great-tasting smoothies, freshly prepared food and an uplifting experience that helps guests fuel their day,” said Max Wetzel, Chief Executive Officer, Tropical Smoothie Cafe. “This evolution reflects the brand we’ve become, sharpens how we communicate our distinct position in the market and creates an even stronger foundation for future growth.” Over the last two years, Tropical Smoothie Cafe has made significant investments in its operations and menu innovation. As a result, it has surpassed $1.6 billion in system sales as of July 2026, grown its loyalty program to 13 million members—a 25 percent increase in a single year—and opened its 1,700ᵗʰ cafe in April 2026, putting it on track to reach more than 1,800 cafes by year-end. The new brand transformation, created in partnership with global branding agency JKR, will support the company’s next phase of growth. With a robust pipeline across 44 states, Tropical Smoothie Cafe is engaging with multi-unit, multi-brand operators and expanding its footprint across non-traditional locations such as airports and military bases. The brand also has plans underway for international expansion. “When you step into a Tropical Smoothie Cafe, you feel it before you can name it — the sights, the smells, the sounds,” said JB Hartford, Executive Creative Director, JKR. “We saw a chance to treat ‘tropical’ less as a place and more as a feeling, one guests could carry with them everywhere, matching the energy and craveability that’s always defined the food itself.” Now, the brand feels instantly recognizable wherever guests interact with it, from a redesigned logo brought to life with the same vibrancy and character found in the cafes themselves, to a playful ‘Palm T’ icon that works as a tropical shorthand on its own. Color, illustration, photography and motion all carry that same energy forward, with a palette of Palm Frond Green and Sunset Orange, and photography that feels sun-kissed and warm in every frame. That momentum is fueling investment in a smarter, more intuitive way for guests to interact with Tropical Smoothie Cafe. Over the next several months, a redesigned, more unified web and app experience will roll out, built to reflect the spirit of the brand itself. Guests can look forward to browsing the menu, customizing their favorites, accessing loyalty benefits and checking out in one seamless journey — whether on the app, online or in-cafe. “This goes beyond how the brand looks,” said Deborah von Kutzleben, Chief Marketing Officer, Tropical Smoothie Cafe. “It’s about creating a stronger, more consistent brand experience across every touchpoint, one that guests will feel the next time they order, true to the energy, quality and optimism that have always driven our business.” The changes will begin rolling out across Tropical Smoothie Cafe locations and digital platforms in the coming weeks. Cofounders and childhood best friends Mohammad Farraj and Omar Al-Massalkhi. Talkin’ Tacos—a concept that’s surged to nearly 40 locations and over $80 million in sales in just six years—spawned from a card game. Around June 2020, cofounders and childhood best friends Mohammad Farraj and Omar Al-Massalkhi landed on the idea for a new Mexican concept. The vision wasn’t far-fetched. Al-Massalkhi had previous experience in the restaurant industry and had an extra food truck that he wasn’t using amid the COVID outbreak. The plan came to life by September 10 in Miami, with the initial hope of earning an extra $500 per month, which wasn’t a small figure for either of them, considering both were married and had children. Farraj was still in school pursuing dentistry at this point, too. Founders : Mohammad Farraj and Omar Al-Massalkhi Headquarters : Broward County Annual Sales : $82 Million Total Units : 37 The food truck opened every day at 6 p.m. because the duo spent the mornings prepping ingredients. The first few months were uneventful. Talkin’ Tacos sold about 10 meals per day until a TikTok video went viral. It wasn’t from an influencer; just a regular customer with a couple hundred followers who posted about a food truck serving birria tacos in Miami on Biscayne Boulevard. Overnight, tens of thousands of people viewed the video. “We had customers that were driving five hours from Orlando. We had a customer who came and said she was from Guatemala. She flew in after she saw the video,” Farraj says. “… The lines just kept coming. And we would just tell them, ‘We’re so sorry. We don’t have enough food. We’ll be ready tomorrow for you guys.’ We thought it was a fluke, it wasn’t going to continue, and then the day after and the day after and, genuinely, it was like a blessing that came, and it just never stopped.” With lines wrapped around the block, Talkin’ Tacos used that momentum to close the food truck and open its first brick-and-mortar store in May 2021. The chain prides itself on birria tacos, in addition to a full lineup of other tacos, burritos, quesadillas, bowls, and specialties, such as a Crispy Stack Wrap, Birria Ramen, Tomato Basil Ramen, and Birria Grilled Cheese. As of mid-July, the company had 37 locations in Florida, North Carolina, Georgia, New York, Texas, and Washington, D.C., growth that occurred without any outside investment. The first location was entirely bootstrapped; Farraj and Al-Massalkhi painted the walls and tables and renovated the kitchen and bathrooms. “This lasted for probably the first two years,” Farraj says. “It really allowed us to have a very low startup cost for the restaurant from start to finish, and it allowed us to expand debt free.” In the first two years, Talkin’ Tacos debuted three locations. The rest of the footprint came online over the past three and a half years. By 2022, the chain was getting hounded by countless franchising inquiries. The demand was so high that Farraj and Al-Massalkhi signed three franchise locations in New York, Jacksonville, Florida, and Orlando. While those units have done well, the rest of expansion—including plans to double in size over the next 16 months—will be all corporately owned restaurants. Stores are based in inline or endcap locations, with the average square footage between 1,800 and 2,200. However, some are as low as 1,500, and others are as big as 3,500 square feet—the point being, the chain works with what it gets and takes a plug-and-play approach, according to Al-Massalkhi. The brand opened its first standalone drive-thru late last year near Miami International Airport. All of it has been done purely through cash flow. “We have a very healthy business,” Farraj says. “Our AUVs are relatively high compared to industry average for Mexican restaurants. We’ve done a very good job at controlling costs, whether it’s labor costs

articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . PURA VIDA MIAMI, the lifestyle-driven wellness café brand known for its elevated all-day dining experience, is welcoming the fall season with six new menu items: the Pumpkin Spice Cloud, Miami Vice Smoothie, Steak & Eggs, Scallion & Feta Omelette, Breakfast Burrito and Fennel Pistachio salad. For guests ready to embrace fall flavors, Pura Vida Miami is introducing the Pumpkin Spice Cloud, a seasonal addition to its coffee and tea category. Available hot or iced, the drink combines double espresso and the guest’s choice of milk with a creamy pumpkin topper featuring Pura Vida Miami’s first-of-its-kind seasonal foam, putting the brand’s signature spin on the quintessential fall flavor. Beyond breakfast, Pura Vida Miami is introducing the Miami Vice Smoothie, created in partnership with Inter Miami CF and inspired by the electric energy of Miami. The smoothie blends strawberry, banana, date, maple syrup, coconut yogurt, coconut water, chia seeds and collagen protein for a vibrant combination delivering 20 grams of protein and 12 grams of fiber. The new Steak & Eggs is a gluten-friendly all-day breakfast plate featuring 100% grass-fed and finished steak, soft-boiled eggs, fresh seasonal fruit and avocado topped with black pepper, sea salt and a lemon oil drizzle. With 39 grams of protein and 6 grams of fiber, the dish offers a protein-forward addition to the brand’s all-day breakfast lineup. Guests may also choose an over-easy egg or a mozzarella omelette at no additional charge. Continuing Pura Vida Miami’s focus on fresh, high-quality ingredients and thoughtfully prepared dishes, the new Breakfast Burrito offers a satisfying new option for breakfast at any time of day. Wrapped in a whole wheat tortilla, the burrito features an egg omelette with scallion and feta, roasted sweet pepper, avocado, olive oil and Pura Vida Miami’s new signature spice blend, delivering 34 grams of protein and 11 grams of fiber. Each order is served with complimentary picante sauce for an added kick. Also part of the all-day breakfast lineup is the Scallion & Feta Omelette, featuring scallion and feta finished with olive oil and served alongside smashed avocado, arugula and toasted sourdough. The dish offers up to 30 grams of protein and nearly 8 grams of fiber, rounding out the new breakfast offerings with another satisfying option for any time of day. In addition to the breakfast and beverage offerings, Pura Vida Miami is introducing the Fennel Pistachio, a fresh, herb-forward salad featuring mixed greens, arugula, dill, basil, fennel, shaved parmesan and toasted pistachio crumbles tossed in a bright sumac vinaigrette. The new salad brings a crisp, seasonal option to Pura Vida Miami’s chef-driven salad lineup. “At Pura Vida Miami, we’re always looking for ways to evolve our menu while staying true to the seasonality, fresh ingredients, quality and flavors our guests have come to expect from us,” said Omer Horev, Co-Founder and CEO of Pura Vida Miami. “These new dishes give our guests even more ways to enjoy breakfast throughout the day, while bringing a fun seasonal element to our coffee menu. We’re excited to introduce these new offerings as we head into fall.” The new menu items build on Pura Vida Miami’s expansive all-day menu, which includes avocado toasts, pasture-raised egg dishes, wraps, bowls, chef-driven salads, high-protein plates, smoothies, açaí bowls, cold-pressed juices, coffee, matcha and fresh-baked goods. The fall menu launch comes as Pura Vida Miami continues to grow its national footprint, now spanning more than 50 locations across Florida, New York, California, Maryland, Virginia and New Jersey. Duck Wings, tossed in teriyaki sauce and topped with toasted sesame seeds, Fresno peppers and scallions. P.F. Chang’s is welcoming fall with Autumn in Kyoto, a limited-time dining experience inspired by one of Japan’s most celebrated seasons. Beginning today, September 16, guests can gather around the table for a new lineup of rich seasonal dishes, including new duck offerings and Wagyu Egg Rolls, alongside handcrafted cocktails and shareable favorites inspired by the warmth and beauty of autumn in Kyoto. The fall season in Kyoto becomes a time for friends and family to slow down, gather and enjoy comforting flavors and meaningful moments. Inspired by this timeless tradition, P.F. Chang’s brings the spirit of the season to the table through its own lens, balancing familiar favorites with new ingredients, techniques, and bold flavors. “Autumn is a season that naturally brings people together, and we wanted to capture that sense of connection through the P.F. Chang’s experience,” said Jim Mazany, Chief Executive Officer of P.F. Chang’s. “With Autumn in Kyoto, we’ve designed a warm, rich, and highly unique, limited-time menu to give guests something new to discover and enjoy together.” For its latest menu launch, P.F. Chang’s introduces two new duck dishes to participating locations nationwide: Duck Wings, tossed in teriyaki sauce and topped with toasted sesame seeds, Fresno peppers and scallions, and Duck Fried Rice, a premium take on a familiar favorite featuring shredded duck, julienned vegetables, edamame, fried shallots, kimchi, chili jam, chili-spiced butter and a fried egg. The seasonal lineup also introduces new Wagyu Egg Rolls, crispy rolls filled with Wagyu beef, black pepper, garlic, ginger and julienned vegetables, finished with black garlic aioli. Also returning is the Sushi Boat, building on its popularity as a shareable centerpiece and giving guests even more reason to gather around the table and experience the season together. “Autumn gives us the opportunity to work with deeper, richer flavors and ingredients that feel especially craveable this time of year,” said Steve Solis, VP of Culinary at P.F. Chang’s. “We challenged ourselves to reimagine familiar P.F. Chang’s favorites through unexpected seasonal pairings. The result is a menu that feels comforting and approachable but still delivers the bold flavor and sense of discovery our guests come to us for.” The new menu extends to the bar through a new partnership with YOSHI Matcha Liqueur, the first matcha liqueur to market, crafted with ceremonial-grade matcha. P.F. Chang’s is among the first national restaurant brands to bring the innovative spirit to guests and introduce the liqueur to restaurant menus nationwide. Together, P.F. Chang’s and YOSHI invite guests to enjoy the Matcha Martini, blending RumChata, YOSHI Matcha Liqueur, cream of coconut and a hint of cinnamon. The seasonal cocktail lineup also includes the new Kyoto Cabin, made with Woodford Reserve Bourbon, black tea, maple and lemon, and finished with a nutmeg aroma. The spirit of sharing extends beyond the table this fall through P.F. Chang’s Spirit of the Zodiac: Spirit of Strength campaign benefiting Starlight Children’s Foundation. Guests can support Starlight by rounding up their check through Round It Up America® or purchasing Bao, P.F. Chang’s limited-edition Spirit of Strength horse plush, for $10; through the Buy One, Give One program, every Bao purchased helps provide another plush to a child through Starlight. Autumn in Kyoto will be available beginning September 16, 2026, through November 3, 2026, at participating P.F. Chang’s locations nationwide, while supplies last. The post P.F. articles.title: Denny’s Opens Nominations for ‘Denny’s Heroes’
articles.titleKo: Denny’s Opens Nominations for ‘Denny’s Heroes’
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Today, America’s Diner opened nominations for Denny’s Heroes: A Grand Slam Thank You, a nationwide search for stories of generosity, resilience, leadership and service that have changed lives or made communities stronger. Every town has a hero who never stops showing up. The teacher who keeps snacks in her desk because she knows which kids come to school hungry. The coach who always finds room for one more child who needs somewhere to belong. The volunteer who keep coming back every Saturday because they know their neighbors are counting on them. If someone immediately came to mind, Denny’s wants to hear their story and celebrate it. “Every day in our restaurants, we see what it means when someone remembers your name, notices when you need something or makes room for you,” said Chris Bode, president and chief executive officer of Denny’s. “A Grand Slam Thank You carries that same care beyond our doors. Together with our franchise owners, we’ll bring the diner to 30 hometown celebrations honoring individuals who keep showing up for others. Denny’s was built one hometown at a time, and we want to bring communities together to celebrate the people who make those hometowns stronger.” A nomination may recognize one individual. Nominees may include educators, caregivers, first responders, coaches, veterans, volunteers, community supporters or anyone who is always the first to step forward when something needs to be done. From the stories submitted, Denny’s will select 30 heroes to receive a “Grand Slam Thank You,” a Denny’s-catered hometown celebration for up to 50 guests hosted by a local franchise owner. The celebration also looks ahead to an important milestone for America’s Diner. In May 2027, Denny’s will mark 50 years since the Grand Slam was first added to the menu in several Atlanta, Ga restaurants in celebration of baseball legend Hank Aaron. As that anniversary approaches, Denny’s Heroes: A Grand Slam Thank You carries the spirit of an iconic meal created to honor a hometown hero forward by recognizing a new generation of people making a difference in communities across the country. “The people we hope to honor will never call themselves heroes. They are too busy making sure someone is fed, safe, seen or given another chance,” said Fasika Melaku, chief people, enterprise communications and social impact officer of Denny’s. “We’re asking people to stop for a moment and think about someone who has made a difference in their life, their family’s life or their community, and then tell us their story. No one should have to become famous to hear the words, ‘We see you. We see the need you noticed, the care you gave and the people who are stronger because you showed up. What you did mattered.'” The post Denny’s Opens Nominations for ‘Denny’s Heroes’ appeared first on FSR magazine .

articles.title: Bob Sambol’s Charlie’s to Open in Dallas
articles.titleKo: Bob Sambol’s Charlie’s to Open in Dallas
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . A noteworthy addition to the Dallas dining scene is taking shape with Charlie’s, a small new restaurant from acclaimed and longtime Dallas restaurant operator Bob Sambol, in partnership with Hunter Pond and Rick Dunlap of Vandelay Companies. The restaurant is slated to open Spring/Summer 2027 in the former Adelmo’s space in Dallas at 5450 W Lovers Ln #225. For Sambol, Charlie’s represents a return to the kind of restaurant that first made him fall in love with the business: personal, understated elegance, and built around relationships. At the heart of Charlie’s will be just 30 tables. Drawing inspiration from the famously intimate culture surrounding restaurants such as Rao’s in New York City, Charlie’s is being conceived as a place where regulars are known, relationships matter and a table can feel almost like an extension of home. There will be no online reservations, and the tables are owned by friends and family of Bob & Vandelay. It will be open to the public by landline phone only for reservation requests. After more than 30 years in the restaurant industry, Sambol has become one of Dallas’ most recognized and well-loved operators. Charlie’s will be deliberately different from the large-scale, highly produced and over designed restaurants. Instead, the restaurant will embrace an understated, old-school elegance inspired by the great neighborhood dining rooms of the East Coast – from New York and the Bronx to classic establishments such as his father’s restaurant The Continental in Mountain Lakes, New Jersey. “This is a very personal restaurant for me,” says Bob Sambol. “After 30 years, I wanted to create something that feels humble and familiar with great hospitality, a beautiful room, people you know and a restaurant you want to return to again and again. Nothing overly complicated. Just a really special place for the neighborhood.” The partnership also brings together two generations of Dallas operators as well as a longtime friendship, pairing Sambol’s decades of hospitality experience with Vandelay Companies, one of the country’s most active restaurant development groups. “I’ve known Hunter and Rick since they were in grade school, and seeing what they have built is truly remarkable. It’s a surreal moment to partner with them on such a personal project” says Bob Sambol. “The memories that Bob and us all have together goes for decades, and it’s special to be doing such a fun and unique project together that no one in Dallas has done in quite some time,” says Hunter Pond. “Charlie’s isn’t about trying to make the biggest restaurant or the loudest statement. It’s about creating a timeless one. That restraint is what makes the project so exciting to us.” The design will follow the same philosophy: low-key, intimate and quietly sophisticated, with a warm palette and subtle touches of vintage yellow hues woven throughout the restaurant. articles.title: Under New CEO, Dave & Buster’s Wants to Win the Experience Game

articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Dave & Buster's believes it can capture more demand with watching experiences. Dave & Buster’s has long occupied a unique lane. It’s an occasion-based business, but one with lofty awareness for its relative size (184 units but 90 percent plus) and the fact customers, on average, visit less than twice a year. For CEO Darin Harper, who stepped in last month following the retirement of Tarun Lal after less than a year at the post, elevating from CFO, it’s a point with a few realities. One is Dave & Buster’s doesn’t have as much margin for getting it right with guests as some. And in recent years, it’s not “consistently been the obvious answer,” he said, when customers plan an excursion only an eatertainment concept can fill. Also, value and experience have not been dependable enough when they do show up to get them back. Dave & Buster’s customers, Harper explained, plan in advance. The brand is not a spot you generally walk by on your way to somewhere else and decide to spend a couple of hours. “When we’re the obvious answer,” he said Monday during his first earnings call as CEO, “we win decisively.” So, the task ahead for Dave & Buster’s, as the company tries to reignite sales after years of tepid performance , falls to three areas around this larger premise. Before unpacking, the brand saw its stock tumble double-digits after reporting a Q2 top- and bottom-line miss. Adjusted EBITDA was 18 percent short of consensus estimates at $98.9 million and same-store sales declined 2.9 percent (negative 5.9 percent two-year stack). That marked an improvement from Q1’s drop of 5.4 percent. However, revenue came in roughly 2 percent short of Wall Street projections as the company lapped $10 million in deferred revenue from a year ago (total figure of $544.1 million, down 2.4 percent, year-over-year). Dave & Buster’s said trends progressed in July, with same-store sales of negative 1.6 percent versus –5 percent in June. And Q3 was gaining still. F&B comps ran positive for the fifth consecutive quarter as well, up 7.6 percent. Special events hiked for the seventh straight period. Dave & Buster’s entertainment business continued to struggle, down an imputed high-single-digit comp. It was low-double-digit red the prior two quarters. Harper believes the path forward is within Dave & Buster’s control. No. 1, regarding occasions, he said the brand will focus on capturing existing demand within personal, seasonal, and cultural calendars (more on this shortly). Next, it’s going to stress “relevance,” meaning ensuring Dave & Buster’s entertainment and F&B offerings are “unmistakably appealing for that occasion.” And lastly, Dave & Buster’s has to promote consistent value and execution with a singular and stable message that customers can recall when they’re making their choice of where to go. In other terms, when they think of heading to Dave & Buster’s (or elsewhere), they know what value awaits. It’s been too cluttered in the past, Harper said. Marketing, in particular, is where the clearest evidence of improvement surfaced in Q2 and where Harper feels the largest opportunity lies. Jeremy Tucker in Q2 joined as CMO. He came over from the same position at AutoNation, leading marketing across north of 300 locations. Tucker previously served as CMO of Planet Fitness and has directed platforms at brands from Doritos to The Walt Disney Company to Spin Master. articles.title: In the Age of New Restaurant Technology, Two-Way Radios Remain an Old-Tech Staple
articles.titleKo: In the Age of New Restaurant Technology, Two-Way Radios Remain an Old-Tech Staple
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Communication matters because restaurant operations remain physical, fast-moving, and unpredictable. Restaurants have embraced new technology over the last five years. Restaurant operators now have AI tools, integrated CRM platforms, advanced POS reporting, and kitchen automation, and they can access all of the new tech with relative ease. This new-age tech promises improved efficiency, better visibility, and tighter control over the guest experience. The promise of new technology often delivers. These new restaurant innovations are amazing, but they often overshadow one of the most effective and longstanding tools in restaurant operations: Two-way radios. Walkie-talkies and headsets don’t get the same attention as AI-powered analytics or guest-facing digital tools, but they remain among the best ways to improve communication, which is one of the biggest issues hurting restaurants. Establishments that succeed do so because they can communicate quickly and clearly in real time. Communication matters because restaurant operations remain physical, fast-moving, and unpredictable. So many things can happen at once. A server needs water for a table. A host needs a manager. A larger party’s order is ready. A guest has a menu question, or a spill needs attention. These scenarios are commonplace in a busy restaurant and addressing them too slowly will kill service. For restaurant operators, especially those still working with leaner teams than they had pre-COVID, that real-time communication is even more critical, according to Richard Stark, former restaurant executive and now Senior Business Consultant at Waters Business Consulting Group in Scottsdale, Arizona. “The communication challenges have worsened since COVID, largely due to a diminished workforce,” Stark said. “Restaurant owners now have to do more with less.” That constant pressure has pushed many operators to adopt new systems across their businesses. However, digital dashboards aren’t very effective at addressing immediate coordination issues. “Reducing workforces means operations struggle to provide the level of hospitality or guest service that is required,” Stark said. “This means teams need to be more efficient in their communication, and two-way radios have been essential because they allow restaurants to take care of guests despite smaller staff.” This idea explains why this technology has remained so resilient. Restaurants can use the most advanced software, but that technology overlooks the fact that the industry still largely depends on people responding to each other as quickly as possible. Radios close that gap faster than any other tool, despite being decades older. Two-way radios don’t require you to unlock a screen, open an app, or type a message. They require you to push a button and speak. They eliminate the need to search across the dining room or back of house to find someone. One quick push of a button can redirect labor, solve a problem, and keep service moving. Stark said the value of radios increases with the size and complexity of the restaurant. “Two-way communication becomes more important as the property size and operational complexity increase,” Stark said. “Smaller restaurants may not need radios, but a moderately sized property, 4,000 square feet, will definitely need a two-way radio system.” As restaurants become more layered, communication becomes increasingly necessary. “Communication is foundational to restaurant success,” Stark said. “Real-time communication is an advantage. Customers want to go to a restaurant where staff can respond more quickly and effectively to their needs.” That has been the experience at La Buena Vida, a Mexican restaurant in Fort Collins, Colorado. articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . L Catterton, the largest global consumer-focused investment firm, announced that it has entered into a definitive agreement to invest in Nandhana Foods, a leading restaurant group specializing in South Indian cuisine. The investment will support Nandhana Foods’ next phase of growth and enable the group to achieve greater scale by leveraging L Catterton’s industry expertise and operating capabilities. South Indian cuisine is one of the largest segments of India’s burgeoning food services market. Propelled by secular trends such as the rising per capita expenditure on dining out and food delivery services, as well as the increasing number of consumption occasions, the segment is expected to witness strong growth led by iconic brands like Nandhana Foods. Nandhana Foods has been offering authentic South Indian cuisine for more than three decades, with a keen focus on taste, authenticity, food quality, freshness, and menu variety. Together with its unique and customizable spice profile, this dedication has enabled it to cultivate a loyal customer base. L Catterton partner Vikram Kumaraswamy commented, “Nandhana Foods’ founding family has built a distinctive and scalable business with a strong consumer proposition and attractive unit economics. It has expanded the business in a disciplined manner and ensured that its restaurants remain anchored in high quality and consistency. We believe there is significant headroom for additional growth by further deepening and broadening its presence in South India and penetrating other markets. There is a clear path for prudently ramping up expansion, and we look forward to working closely with the founding family to drive continued growth.” Nandhana Foods founder and managing director Dr R. Ravichandar added, “We are pleased to partner with L Catterton, which has a track record of creating value for its portfolio companies across the world. The firm has a profound grasp of our organizational DNA and an intricate understanding of the restaurant industry. We are excited about tapping into its astute insights and proven know-how to strengthen our operations in line with our commitment to providing high-quality food and service to our customers.” L Catterton has significant experience in building restaurant brands across the world. The firm has invested in around 30 restaurant businesses till date, with current and past portfolio companies in the space including Dishoom, P.F. Chang’s, Velvet Taco, Baja Fresh, Cheddar’s Scratch Kitchen, Cigierre, HUGE, Impresario, and Mendocino Farms. The post L Catterton Invests in Nandhana Foods appeared first on FSR magazine .

articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Park Slope is NAYA's 32nd restaurant in New York City and its fourth in Brooklyn. NAYA, the Middle Eastern fast casual brand offering fresh, customizable meals and vibrant flavors rooted in Lebanese tradition since 2008, opens its 50th restaurant at 311 7th Avenue in Park Slope, Brooklyn. The opening is NAYA’s ninth of 2026, with four more slated before year end, bringing the brand to 13 openings in a single year. This year’s restaurants span New York, New Jersey, Connecticut and Massachusetts, and the Conshohocken opening later this month will be NAYA’s second in Pennsylvania. Founder and CEO Hady Kfoury is targeting 200 locations nationwide by 2030. Park Slope is NAYA’s 32nd restaurant in New York City and its fourth in Brooklyn, keeping the majority of the brand’s footprint in the city where Kfoury opened the first NAYA in 2008 as a fine dining Lebanese restaurant, later converting it to a build-your-own fast casual model years before Middle Eastern fast casual became a growth category. To mark the milestone, NAYA is offering 50 percent off online orders for pickup and delivery at locations nationwide, from 3PM to close on opening day. In Park Slope, the first 100 guests receive a free bowl, roll or salad, and the restaurant becomes the first NAYA in Brooklyn to carry the brand’s Kids Meal, available seven days a week. “Fifty locations in, I still judge every opening the same way, by whether the food tastes like what we served on day one,” said Hady Kfoury, Founder and CEO of NAYA. The Apple Harvest lineup is designed to fit seamlessly into the everyday moments that define the season. Fall is synonymous with apple, spice and caramel, and Clean Juice is bringing those familiar flavors to the menu its own way. Known for cold-pressed juices, scratch-blended smoothies, and bowls, the brand is unveiling its new Apple Harvest menu, with two limited-time additions pouring nationwide from Sept. 16 through Nov. 10. As the weather cools and seasonal cravings shift, Clean Juice is leaning into fall’s most recognizable flavors without letting them overshadow the fresh ingredients at the heart of its menu. The Apple Harvest lineup puts its own spin on two familiar favorites: Apple Cider Juice: A bright blend of apple, lemon and pumpkin spice. Caramel Apple Smoothie: A creamy blend of apple, banana, almond milk, Greek yogurt, Chia seeds, vanilla, maple and dates, finished with a date-based caramel drizzle. “Seasonal menus have become a meaningful part of how people experience a brand, and we wanted to give our guests something that feels distinctly fall without asking them to step outside the way they already enjoy Clean Juice,” said Erik Jensen, vice president of marketing for BRIX Holdings. “Apple Harvest gives us an opportunity to participate in that while staying aligned with the choices our guests make throughout the rest of the year. With one option that is bright and refreshing and another that is creamy and satisfying, the lineup gives guests two distinct ways to usher in fall. articles.title: The Digital Friction Costing Restaurants Orders Before the First Bite
articles.titleKo: The Digital Friction Costing Restaurants Orders Before the First Bite
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Accurate information keeps a restaurant under consideration, but reviews often provide the confidence to place the order. Restaurant operators spend most of their time focused on what happens inside the business: preparing great food, supporting employees, serving guests, handling costs, and solving the problems that come with a busy shift. But many restaurant decisions are made before a guest ever walks through the door or tastes the food. When people are deciding where to eat, they often start online—browsing menus, checking hours, and reading reviews to see if a restaurant feels like a good fit. If they can’t easily find what they’re looking for, most won’t bother reaching out for more details. They’ll just move on to another place. Menufy research found that 59 percent of consumers have decided not to order from a restaurant because they could not find basic information online. Among Gen Z consumers, that number rises to 71 percent. A restaurant’s digital presence isn’t just a marketing asset. It is part of the guest experience, and small points of friction can cost an order before the restaurant has an opportunity to compete. Missing Information Creates an Invisible Walkout Inside a restaurant, it is usually easy to recognize when a guest walks out. The digital version is much harder to see. A potential customer may struggle to find a current menu, notice conflicting hours, or fail to locate a clear ordering option. That person leaves the page, but the restaurant may never know an order was lost. It’s easy for restaurant staff to overlook small issues like an old holiday schedule or a menu link that doesn’t work well on a phone. They might seem like things that can be fixed later. But for someone choosing where to eat, those little problems can be a big deal. Diners just want to know the basics: What’s on the menu? Are they open? How much will it cost? Can I order quickly? If the answers aren’t clear, it’s easy to move on. When those answers are difficult to find, the customer is not necessarily rejecting the food, value, or brand. Another restaurant simply made the decision easier. Menufy found that 74 percent of consumers say a restaurant’s online presence influences whether they order, increasing to 80 percent among millennials. For younger diners in particular, missing information can make a business appear less current or dependable. Recent Reviews Build Confidence Accurate information keeps a restaurant under consideration, but reviews often provide the confidence to place the order. According to Menufy’s survey, 35 percent of consumers identify positive online reviews as the most important trust factor when trying a new restaurant. Reviews ranked ahead of personal recommendations, a professional website, and social media. Word of mouth still matters. Menufy found that 27 percent of consumers discover restaurants through friends and family, second only to Google search at 34 percent. But a recommendation is often only the beginning. The consumer still searches for the restaurant, checks the menu, and reads what recent guests have said. It’s great to see a restaurant with a high rating, but people also care about the most recent reviews. Diners want to know what things are like these days, not just a year ago. They’ll scan for fresh feedback about the food, the service, how fast orders come out, and whether the staff responds when something isn’t right. If the latest reviews are outdated or nobody replies, it’s easy to wonder if the place is still living up to its reputation. For independent restaurants, this creates a meaningful opportunity to compete locally without a large marketing budget. articles.title: DoorDash to Acquire Wonder’s Grubhub Campus Dining Business, Invest $125M in Company
articles.titleKo: DoorDash to Acquire Wonder’s Grubhub Campus Dining Business, Invest $125M in Company
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . DoorDash, and Wonder announced a strategic partnership. Under the agreement, DoorDash will acquire Wonder’s Grubhub Campus Dining business. In addition, DoorDash made a long-term investment in Wonder as part of its Series D round. Grubhub Campus Dining, formerly known as Tapingo, enables millions of students to order a meal from campus dining facilities and on-campus restaurants using its mobile app or kiosks, pay for the meal with the convenience of campus dining dollars and schedule the pickup. Grubhub Campus Dining is live at more than 450 colleges and universities, serving a significant portion of U.S. higher education students. Following the close of the transaction, DoorDash intends to continue expanding Grubhub Campus Dining in the U.S., enhance the selection and convenience available to students and bring Tapingo’s vertically integrated technology stack beyond college campuses to stadiums, hotels and other similar venues. The transaction is anticipated to close by the first half of 2027, subject to customary closing conditions and regulatory review. Additionally, DoorDash’s $125 million investment adds to Wonder’s $650 million Series D round announced in July, fueling Wonder’s continued physical expansion and investments in technology, robotics and AI. Wonder offers more than 25 different in-house and chef-created concepts under one roof, using hardware and software to translate the craft of Michelin-starred chefs and iconic restaurants into a repeatable, machine-readable process. With 157 locations across the Northeast and Mid-Atlantic regions, Wonder’s footprint has more than quadrupled since the start of 2025. Wonder will expand beyond the East Coast in 2027, opening its first Texas locations in January. “Wonder was founded to make great food more accessible. To us, that means higher-quality food at lower prices, with more choice and convenience, in more communities,” Marc Lore, founder and CEO of Wonder, said in a statement. “Our partnership with DoorDash lets us continue investing in the technology, robotics and infrastructure that mission requires. Grubhub Campus Dining is a thriving business built by a great team, and DoorDash is well positioned to take it further. The partnership also allows Wonder to focus on our long-term ambition: a fully autonomous food system that can plan, produce and deliver personalized meals at scale, serving all 21 meals people eat each week.” “Our mission at DoorDash is to grow and empower local economies,” added Tony Xu, cofounder and CEO of DoorDash. “Adding Grubhub Campus Dining to our platform will enable us to bring greater choice and convenience to college students while streamlining operations and reducing friction for universities. In addition, we’re pleased to be investing in Wonder as they continue to expand access to world-class food for communities across the nation.” Latham & Watkins LLP and Fenwick & West LLP served as legal counsel and J.P. Morgan Securities LLC acted as exclusive financial advisor to Wonder. Wilson Sonsini Goodrich & Rosati P.C. served as legal counsel and RBC Capital Markets served as a financial advisor to DoorDash. articles.title: Elysium Retreats Unveils Major UK Expansion Strategy with up to 12 New Retreat Destinations Under Consideration
articles.titleKo: Elysium Retreats Unveils Major UK Expansion Strategy with up to 12 New Retreat Destinations Under Consideration
articles.originalSummary: UK retreat operator, Elysium Retreats , has unveiled plans for a major UK expansion programme, targeting up to 12 new destinations over the next two years as demand for high-quality nature-led escapes continues to grow. Part of the Sight Acre Group, Elysium Retreats brings together distinctive countryside and waterside stays designed around nature, comfort and memorable time away. The brand is already established through two UK destinations: Fairwood Lakes in Wiltshire, home to waterside lodges, woodland lodges and a unique floating lodge, and Benview Lodges in Stirlingshire, where guests can enjoy peaceful lodge stays surrounded by rolling Scottish hills, close to Aberfoyle and on the edge of Loch Lomond & The Trossachs National Park. With demand for premium UK staycations remaining strong and travellers increasingly seeking nature-focused experiences, Elysium Retreats is accelerating plans to build a nationwide collection of distinctive retreat destinations. The expansion will be delivered through a combination of acquisitions, the refurbishment of existing holiday and leisure parks, and the development of new retreat destinations in carefully selected locations across the UK. The growth programme forms part of the brand’s wider ambition to become one of the UK’s leading retreat operators, creating a collection of locations that each have their own character and sense of place, while sharing the same focus on comfort, nature, warm hospitality and meaningful guest experiences. Matt Pressman, Operations Director at Elysium Retreats, said: “We’re seeing a clear shift in what guests want from their leisure time. People are looking for experiences that combine comfort, nature and genuine opportunities to disconnect from busy everyday lives. “Our expansion strategy reflects that demand. By investing in existing leisure destinations and creating new retreat experiences, we’re building a collection of locations that offer something more distinctive while remaining true to the Elysium Retreats ethos.” The expansion represents one of the most significant growth initiatives undertaken by the Sight Acre Group within the UK leisure and hospitality sector.

articles.title: Hospitality Apprenticeship Showcase 2027
articles.titleKo: Hospitality Apprenticeship Showcase 2027
articles.originalSummary: Hospitality businesses from across the UK are being invited to bring along their outstanding apprentices to the annual Hospitality Apprenticeship Showcase (HAS), taking place at the House of Commons during National Apprenticeship Week. The event, to be held on Wednesday 10 February 2027, from 12.30pm–3.30pm in the Terrace Pavilion, House of Commons, will bring together around 120 hospitality apprentices from many of the UK’s leading operators for an afternoon celebrating the talent, ambition and professionalism of the industry’s future leaders. Over the past decade, more than 1,800 hospitality apprentices have attended the Showcase, making it one of the sector’s most prestigious events dedicated to recognising apprentice achievement. The Showcase provides apprentices with a rare opportunity to meet their local MPs, demonstrate their skills, share their personal career journeys and hear from leading figures from both the hospitality industry and Government. It also gives Parliamentarians the opportunity to see first-hand the contribution apprentices make to one of the UK’s most important sectors and the vital role hospitality plays in supporting employment, skills and economic growth. Hospitality is one of the UK’s largest employers, offering careers across hotels, restaurants, pubs, contract catering, visitor attractions and events. Apprenticeships continue to provide an essential pathway in the industry, helping employers develop skilled, motivated teams while creating rewarding long-term careers for thousands of people every year. The HAS event celebrates not only the achievements of individual apprentices but also the commitment employers make to developing future talent. Every apprentice attending has a story to tell, whether they have progressed from entry-level roles into management, discovered a passion for professional cookery, or built confidence and skills through workplace learning. The event has become one of the highlights of National Apprenticeship Week, shining a spotlight on the diverse and rewarding careers hospitality offers and challenging outdated perceptions of the industry. Hospitality businesses of every size, from independent operators to national brands, are encouraged to bring along their apprentices who have demonstrated commitment, enthusiasm and a passion for the industry. Whether they are just beginning their careers or have already achieved significant milestones, the Showcase offers a unique opportunity to recognise their success on a national stage.

articles.title: Brook & Green Opens on Chiswick High Road, Bringing an 89-Cover All-Day Neighbourhood Concept and Wine Room to W4
articles.titleKo: Brook & Green Opens on Chiswick High Road, Bringing an 89-Cover All-Day Neighbourhood Concept and Wine Room to W4
articles.originalSummary: Brook & Green , a new all-day restaurant and wine room, will open at 142 Chiswick High Road at the end of September 2026 , bringing an ingredient-led dining concept and a dedicated wine room to one of West London’s most established neighbourhood dining streets. The opening lands at a pivotal moment for the site. Chiswick High Road has long been one of the capital’s most reliable neighbourhood catchments – affluent, residential, and driven by repeat local use rather than destination trade – and Brook & Green has been conceived to serve that demand directly, built for regular, all-day use rather than a single occasion. The concept occupies 89 covers across three distinct spaces: 49 at ground floor, 14 on the terrace, and 26 in a newly developed wine room downstairs, built around the restaurant’s own working wine collection. The all-day format has been designed to evolve through the day, from breakfast and lunch through to evening dining and drinks, with the wine room offering a separate, slower-paced destination for pre-dinner drinks, wine discovery and private dining. The kitchen’s output is food-first and ingredient-led, drawing on Mediterranean, Asian and British influences across an all-day menu built for consistency and repeat use rather than occasion-only dining. Breakfast runs from 8am until 11:30am on weekdays and 12:30pm at weekends. The all-day à la carte menu takes over from midday, running until 11pm Monday to Thursday and midnight on Fridays and Saturdays; Sundays are restricted to brunch and lunch, closing at 6pm. The wine room opens from 5pm. Interiors have been reworked around a warmer, more craft-led identity: a softened bar as the room’s social anchor, new booth seating, linen drapery and layered lighting, and a communal table dressed with large-scale artwork. Downstairs, the wine room’s exposed brickwork, integrated bottle display and warm joinery shelving give it a distinct character from the room above. The refit has been led by B3 Designers , the hospitality-focused design studio whose mission is to help ambitious operators turn bold ideas into enduring hospitality brands through strategy and story-driven design. The wider turnaround and redevelopment has been directed by Savvy IQ , the hospitality consultancy that led the project from initial market and feasibility study through to concept finalisation. Tim Price, Owner-Operator of Brook & Green, said: “This isn’t about building a name around one person or one kitchen – it’s about building a restaurant Chiswick will use every week, for years. That’s a different discipline to running a destination restaurant, and it’s exactly what we set out to do here.” Brook & Green’s launch adds to a run of openings and reinvestment along Chiswick High Road, reflecting a broader shift among neighbourhood restaurants towards all-day, multi-daypart formats that maximise use of a single site rather than committing to one service period. The opening will create 18-19 new roles.

articles.title: Applebee’s and IHOP’s Latest Dual-Branded Restaurant Opens in San Antonio
articles.titleKo: Applebee’s and IHOP’s Latest Dual-Branded Restaurant Opens in San Antonio
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Dine Brands approaches 50 dual-branded Applebee’s | IHOP restaurants nationwide with newest opening. Dine Brands Global, Inc., the parent company of Applebee’s Neighborhood Grill + Bar and IHOP, celebrated the rapid expansion of its dual-branded restaurant concept with the opening of a new location in San Antonio, Texas. Less than two years after launching the first standalone U.S. dual-branded restaurant in nearby Seguin, Texas, the two iconic brands are approaching 50 dual-branded locations nationwide, reflecting growing guest demand for greater variety, convenience, and value under one roof. Located at 2607 W. Loop 1604 S., the new restaurant is the eighth dual-branded Applebee’s | IHOP location in the greater San Antonio market, underscoring the region’s strong embrace of the concept. To celebrate the opening and the community, The Hakim Group, an Applebee’s and IHOP franchisee and location owner, hosted a special ribbon-cutting event where 100 guests received free pancakes for a year. The franchisee also presented a $1,000 donation to Stay Strong Foundation, a San Antonio-based nonprofit, reinforcing its commitment to supporting the local community. “We are excited for guests to experience this newest Applebee’s | IHOP location, which reflects the continued evolution of the dual-branded concept,” said Danny Hakim, Vice President of The Hakim Group. “Our restaurants are only as strong as the communities they serve and we’re proud to continue investing in San Antonio and to support organizations that are making a difference locally.” The dual-branded restaurant offers guests the best of both brands under one roof, allowing them to mix and match signature Applebee’s and IHOP items from a single menu any time of day, from morning to late night. Within the space, guests enjoy the unique identity and atmosphere of both brands, connected by shared spaces that create a seamless experience and complemented by specialty cocktails* and exclusive menu innovations available only at dual-branded locations, including the Loaded Buffalo Chicken Omelette and Ultimate Breakfast Burger. “What began as a bold idea has evolved into a meaningful complement to our development and growth strategies,” said John Peyton, CEO of Dine Brands Global. “In under two years, we’ve gone from one dual-branded U.S. location to nearly 50 nationwide, and the momentum continues. By bringing Applebee’s and IHOP together under one roof, we’re creating a more flexible operating model, giving guests more reasons to visit, and offering franchisees an additional pathway to strengthen their businesses over time.” As Dine Brands advances its development and growth strategies, the dual-branded model is emerging as a valuable addition to its portfolio. The company remains on track to open approximately 80 domestic dual-branded restaurants by the end of 2026. articles.title: Taco Bell Foundation Achieves Biggest Community Grants Year Yet
articles.titleKo: Taco Bell Foundation Achieves Biggest Community Grants Year Yet
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . That impact is taking shape in communities nationwide. Today, small acts of generosity are adding up to the Taco Bell Foundation’s biggest Community Grants year yet: a record $32 million supporting 700 nonprofits nationwide, representing a 40% increase in nonprofit partners from last year. Fueled by fans who Round Up their Taco Bell order totals, the investment is creating more opportunities for young people through education, career readiness, mentorship, and youth empowerment. The Community Grants program is investing more than twice what it did just three years ago, while supporting 200+ more nonprofit partners than last year — turning one record investment into thousands of opportunities for young people. “When you think about how this started, with fans giving a little extra at checkout, it’s incredible to see that generosity grow into $32 million for organizations serving young people across the country,” said Morgan Tabor, Executive Director of the Taco Bell Foundation. “What I love most about Community Grants is how local they are. Taco Bell franchisees know these organizations, they believe in their work, and together we’re helping more young people see just how much is possible for their futures.” Behind the record investment is a network of 700 organizations supporting young people on the path to what’s next. That includes national partners like Junior Achievement , City Year , and College Advising Corps alongside local nonprofits like Easterseals DuPage & Fox Valley near Chicago and Mana de Albuquerque . That impact is taking shape in communities nationwide. In California’s Central Valley, the Foundation awarded a $100,000 Community Grant to Boys & Girls Clubs of Fresno County while celebrating acclaimed designer, Huron native, and longtime Taco Bell fan Willy Chavarria. The grant will fuel education, teen programming, and career readiness across eight Club sites, opening more doors for young people throughout the region. Other Community Grant celebrations are bringing that impact to life across the country: In Minneapolis, Foundation Scholars and partners from Taco Bell franchisee Border Foods and Kaleidoscope volunteered with Boys & Girls Club of the Twin Cities, engaging with local youth and assembling school-supply backpacks before presenting a $177,000 grant; In Chicago, Taco Bell Foundation, Easterseals DuPage & Fox Valley, Shamrock Company and McLane celebrated with a facility tour highlighting the Foundation-funded internship program, and a visit from the Taco Bell Truck; In New Mexico, the Taco Bell Foundation team joined Four Corners and Boys & Girls Club of San Juan County in Farmington to celebrate a $100,000 grant, connect with a three-time Live Más Scholar, and experience the Club’s hands-on career readiness programming. Just 43 cents can make a difference. That’s how much fans donate, on average, when they choose to Round Up their Taco Bell orders. In 2025 alone, those contributions added up to over $51 million raised through Round Up, helping fuel the Foundation’s record Community Grants investment. The impact stays close to home. Taco Bell franchisees nominate organizations in their communities to receive the grants, helping direct funding to nonprofits already creating opportunities for young people in their communities. This week, as part of Community Grants Celebration Week, many Taco Bell corporate employees are assembling literacy kits and creating bookmarks with Orange County United Way , and providing food prep and kitchen support alongside Bracken’s Kitchen . Fans across the country can choose to Round Up their total in restaurant or through the Taco Bell app or website, helping fuel the Taco Bell Foundation’s continued support of young people nationwide. articles.title: Friendly’s Introduces ‘The Conehead Crew’ for Kids
articles.titleKo: Friendly’s Introduces ‘The Conehead Crew’ for Kids
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Every kids' meal now comes with a sealed Conehead Crew trading card pack. Friendly’s is giving kids something parents and grown-ups will wish they’d had at that age. Rolling out systemwide on Sept. 16, the new kids’ experience pairs a redesigned menu with sealed packs of collectible trading cards, engaging activity sheets, and five familiar ice cream sundae characters with newfound personalities and a built-in fan base. Say hello to the Conehead Crew. The Crew guides the program and pops up everywhere from the menu cover to the standees by the front door: Conehead, the friendly and adventurous captain who welcomes everybody aboard Vanilla ice cream with signature cone ‘hat’, whipped cream, Reese’s Pieces (contains peanuts). Rock the Star, cool, confident and built for the spotlight Forbidden Chocolate ice cream with chocolate sprinkles, whipped cream, cherry, and Reese’s® Peanut Butter Cup, Reese’s Pieces (contains peanuts). Puddles the Pig, sweet and playful Strawberry ice cream with real banana, whipped topping and M&M’s®. (May contain peanuts). Monster Mash, fun-loving with energy to burn Mint chocolate chip ice cream with M&M’s® and Reese’s® Peanut Butter Cup (contains peanuts). Spot the Dog, loyal and lovable Cookies ‘N Cream ice cream with hot fudge, cherry, Reese’s® Peanut Butter Cup, Reese’s® Pieces (contains peanuts). Every kids’ meal now comes with a sealed Conehead Crew trading card pack featuring two surprise cards from the Character, Crew or Adventure collection, plus a bounceback coupon to use on a future visit. With 18 unique designs to discover, including rare and unique cards randomly tucked into select packs, kids can collect, trade and keep building their Conehead Crew with every visit. But it might take kiddos a minute to collect them all – with the premium and legendary cards being rather rare and more difficult to find. Kids get a reimagined menu across breakfast, lunch and dinner. Each menu also contains mazes, word searches and landmark matching to work through while the magic happens in the kitchen. And the fun doesn’t stop there. Now through Oct. 13, kids eat for $5 with the purchase of an adult entrée. The back-to-school stretch brings one more reason to pull into the parking lot, with a Back-to-School Cheeseburger, fries and a Happy Ending Sundae for only $9.99. The excitement continues on Oct. 1, when Crew standees turn dining rooms into photo stops and temporary tattoos send some joy home with every kid. October has plenty of surprises in store; families may want to keep an eye on the calendar as the weather cools. “Most people can still describe the toy that came with a meal when they were seven, right down to the details,” said Erik Jenson, vice president of marketing for BRIX Holdings. “That kind of memory comes from acquiring something worth keeping and worth showing a friend at school the next morning. We built this program around that instinct, because a kid who walks out with an unfinished collection has already picked where the family is going back to next.” It’s a season of smiles at Friendly’s. Whether stopping in for a quick bite or rounding out a family meal, Friendly’s makes it easy to enjoy the classics without stretching the budget. Guests can also make the most of the new offerings by joining the Friendly’s Fan Club rewards program, which provides exclusive offers, alongside specialty promotions and updates. articles.title: Solmar Hotels & Resorts Names New CEO and COO
articles.titleKo: Solmar Hotels & Resorts Names New CEO and COO
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Solmar Hotels & Resorts, a pioneer of Baja California Sur hospitality since 1974, has appointed Mauricio Salicrup as Chief Executive Officer and Michel Albahari as Chief Operating Officer. The new structure strengthens the company’s corporate governance model and supports the growth strategy the group is building for the years ahead. Together the two executives bring the legacy of one of the founding families of tourism in Los Cabos alongside broad experience across the hospitality industry. The appointments come as Solmar Hotels & Resorts advances a long-term investment strategy focused on the guest experience and sustainable growth. Earlier this year, the company announced a US$6 million investment across its Los Cabos portfolio, spanning new accommodations, guest room renovations and energy-efficient infrastructure upgrades. At Grand Solmar Pacific Dunes, an expansion set for completion in 2027 will add new five-bedroom villas and penthouse-style suites, while improvements across Playa Grande Resort and Grand Solmar Land’s End include renovated rooms, refreshed public spaces, upgraded amenities and energy optimization systems. More than three decades leading tourism operations As CEO, Salicrup leads the group’s overall strategy, backed by more than 35 years in the tourism industry and more than three decades in executive roles at Mexican and international companies. “It is an honor to take on the leadership of a company that has helped shape the history of tourism in Los Cabos,” said Mauricio Salicrup. “Our commitment is to build on a legacy more than five decades in the making, with an operation that keeps growing more efficient, more innovative and more sustainable, so we can continue delivering exceptional experiences for our guests and creating value for our team members, our business partners and the community.” His work extends beyond hotel operations, and he has become one of the leading voices for the tourism sector in Baja California Sur. He served on the board of the Los Cabos Hotel Association for eight years and currently advises its presidency. He is Technical Secretary of the Los Cabos Tourism Board (FITURCA) and a member of the Baja California Sur State Tourism Board (FITUES), and he represents Los Cabos on Mexico’s National Tourism Business Council (CNET). Operational excellence for a new chapter As Chief Operating Officer, Albahari is responsible for service standards and operating efficiency across every property in the group, leading a culture built on innovation, continuous improvement and guest satisfaction. “Our main goal is to keep raising the service standards that define Solmar Hotels & Resorts,” said Michel Albahari. “We will work to optimize every operating process, bring in best practices and build a culture of continuous improvement that delivers memorable experiences for our guests, while maintaining the quality, the warmth and the excellence that characterize the brand.” Solmar Hotels & Resorts operates a portfolio of six hotels: Grand Solmar Land’s End Resort & Spa, Grand Solmar Pacific Dunes Resort Golf & Spa, home to Solmar Golf Links, Playa Grande Resort & Grand Spa, The Ridge at Playa Grande, Solmar Resort and Grand Solmar The Residences, along with a culinary program of four fine dining restaurants. With this structure in place, Solmar Hotels & Resorts begins a chapter focused on accelerating growth, strengthening its standing as one of Mexico’s leading hotel groups and continuing to contribute to the economic and social development of Los Cabos. articles.title: La Vaquita Expanding to Foodservice Business Nationally
articles.titleKo: La Vaquita Expanding to Foodservice Business Nationally
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . As demand for Hispanic cuisine continues to grow, La Vaquita, the award-winning Hispanic cheese brand, is expanding its foodservice business nationally. The move brings La Vaquita’s authentic cheeses to operators throughout the United States to meet consumers’ demand for traditional Hispanic ingredients. La Vaquita’s foodservice portfolio helps restaurants bring Hispanic flavor to a wide range of dishes, just as it has done for homes across Texas for five decades. La Vaquita cheeses combine authenticity, quality, and a broad portfolio of offerings in one trusted brand, supporting applications from crumbled toppings and bold garnishes to melted, seared, and fried cheeses, including enchiladas, tacos, quesadillas, and bowls. La Vaquita’s varieties crafted for restaurant operators include: · Queso Fresco · Queso Cotija · Queso Blanco · Queso Freir · Queso Panela · Queso Quesadilla La Vaquita’s Expansion Fulfills Restaurant Needs The expansion comes as Hispanic cuisine continues to gain momentum across U.S. menus, with the U.S. Mexican restaurant industry valued at approximately $105 billion in 2026 with roughly 52,000 businesses operating nationally. Today, Mexican cuisine represents about 1 in 10 U.S. restaurants and is present in nearly every county in the country. At the same time, the Hispanic cheese category continues to deliver double-digit growth, fueled by consumer demand for authentic flavors and menu innovation. “As more people continue to seek Hispanic foods, operators are looking for traditional, high-quality cheeses to help create differentiated dining experiences,” said David Garascia, Vice President of Sales, Foodservice at DFA. “For over 50 years, La Vaquita has been helping bring families and friends together around delicious, authentic recipes. We are excited to deepen the relationships with consumers and restaurant operators by delivering La Vaquita’s award-winning cheeses to foodservice through authentic craftsmanship, quality, and consistency.” In addition to offering authentic flavor, the portfolio supports back-of-house efficiency with foodservice-ready packaging and formats designed for consistent prep, easier handling, and dependable performance. Operators can source a broad range of Hispanic cheese varieties from a single trusted brand known for its quality, safety, and unparalleled service levels. “La Vaquita brings authentic flavor to every plate,” said Nico Ramos, Chef and Owner, Antigua Latin Inspired Kitchen. “The cheeses remind me of the flavors I grew up with, and they deliver the consistency and performance I need in a professional kitchen. Whether I’m crumbling Queso Fresco, creating a creamy sauce with Queso Blanco, or adding the bold finish of Cotija, I know I’m working with a product that brings the best to every dish.” Founded in 1971 by Maria Castro, who began making Queso Fresco in her Houston home, today La Vaquita is available at retailers in Texas and beyond. La Vaquita products, from fresh cheeses to butter to cremas, have earned recognition at national and international cheese competitions, including Best of Class honors at the 2026 World Championship Cheese Contest. articles.titleKo: Marble Slab Creamery Adds Location in Oxford
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Marble Slab Creamery, known for its small-batch fresh ice cream and owned by FAT Brands, has officially opened a new location in Oxford, Miss. Located at the Evergreen Travel Center, this marks the fifth Marble Slab Creamery in the state. “Just like there are endless ice cream combinations at Marble Slab Creamery, the future is bright for our growth,” said Allison Lauenstein, President of Marble Slab Creamery. “We are proud to now have five locations in Mississippi, reflecting the strong support of our loyal guests and our dedication to delivering our premium small-batch ice cream and exceptional guest experience.” For over 40 years, Marble Slab Creamery has been an innovator in the ice cream space, dreaming up the frozen slab technique and offering homemade, small-batch Ice Cream with always free Mix-Ins and Shakes in a variety of flavors. The new Marble Slab Creamery is located at the Evergreen Travel Center, 3800 McAlexander Drive, Oxford, MS 38655, and is open Monday through Sunday, 11:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. The post Marble Slab Creamery Adds Location in Oxford appeared first on QSR Magazine .
