articles.title: Steak ‘n Shake is Getting Political as it Keeps Driving Sales
articles.titleKo: Steak ‘n Shake is Getting Political as it Keeps Driving Sales
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . After a years-long spell of tepid sales , Steak ‘n Shake has landed on a formula that’s infusing performance and buzz into the legacy chain. Same-store sales in Q2 lifted 11.9 percent and are up 14 percent across the first half of the year. According to the Wall Street Journal , average visits per location bumped 5.8 percent over that span as well. This after the 1934-founded brand began fiscal 2026 with comps of 10 percent and posted its best calendar run in 2025 since 1992 . On a two-year stack for Q2, Steak ‘n Shake reported 22.6 percent higher. Pretax earnings in the quarter increased 31 percent, year-over-year, to $8.5 million, and net revenue (inclusive of frees from franchise partners) rose 4.1 percent. Better results have come as the footprint retracts, however, although the pace has settled somewhat of late. It ended Q2 with 126 company-operated units, 183 franchise-partner ( the single-store model introduced in 2018 ), and 90 traditional franchises for a total of 399. That compares to a year-ago measure of 143, 174, 100, and 417, respectively. Additionally, eight of Steak ‘n Shake’s 126 company-operated locations were closed as of June 30. Of those, two should reopen and six are slated to be sold or leased. The brand is down about 17 percent from this point in 2023. And further: Q2 revenue at Steak ‘n Shake was $72 million compared to roughly $69 million a year ago. Over the first half of the year, it’s $135.8 million compared to $131.1 million. More recently, per its X account , franchise-partner same-store sales gained 19 percent through Q3. The brand said it’s achieved double-digit same-store sales since making the call in May 2025 to take Bitcoin. Steak ‘n Shake’s franchise-partner comp was 14.5 percent this past quarter. Returning to the larger formula at work, Steak ‘n Shake continues to lean into two outward levers as it strips underperformers from the system and adjusts to a kiosk-forward QSR model. One is a MAHA-inspired ingredient push. The second, becoming increasingly political. The brand on September 9, in a rare spin for restaurant chains, endorsed Sen. Jon Husted (R-Ohio), praising him as a champion of the MAHA movement. It also criticized Democratic opponent Sherrod Brown for supporting federal spending “that fueled the inflation crisis.” Previously, Steak ‘n Shake endorsed Republican challenger Derek Merrin against Marcy Kaptur and republican Zach Lahn, who is aiming to become Iowa’s governor. Per The Washington Post, Steak ‘n Shake’s April-appointed “Chief MAHA Officer,” Michael Boes, who previously advised Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., said the brand “supports candidates who are committed to improving people’s health” and would endorse Democrats as well as Republicans if the person fit the bill. On Saturday, it added an endorsement of retired U.S. Army Colonel and Republican Laura Buckhout for North Carolina’s 1 st Congressional District, saying “we stand behind her mission to cut unnecessary regulations, relieve the burden on small businesses, and improve Americans’ access to healthy, natural, high-quality food at a price they can afford.” Buckhout posted a video on X stopping by a location in Dallas. Boes told The Post he wasn’t concerned about alienating customers, noting Steak ‘n Shake would prioritize “doing the right thing, even if it hurts our short-term profits.” Steak ‘n Shake has waved this MAHA banner for years now, really taking off when RFK Jr. visited a store last March. That remains Steak ‘n Shake’s pinned X post, collecting more than 155,000 likes, 4,300 comments, and 10,000-plus retweets. articles.title: Burger King UK ventures further into the chicken category with chicken tenders
articles.titleKo: Burger King UK ventures further into the chicken category with chicken tenders
articles.originalSummary: Burger King UK is launching chicken tenders nationwide from 15 September as it looks to capitalise on increasing demand for poultry products. Chicken has emerged as a key growth area for QSR and restaurant operators with specialist chicken brands including Popeyes, Wingstop and Slim Chickens expanding at pace and Pizza Express expanding into chicken with Mac & Wings and Domino’s launching CHICK ’N’ DIP. Burger King’s new product is made with 100% chicken breast and coated in a seasoned breadcrumb coating. It will be available in three-, five- and eight-piece portions, priced from £5.99. The launch is supported by three new sauces exclusive to Burger King: BK flame-grilled mayo, spicy smokehouse ketchup and BBQ mayo. Burger King will also offer the tenders as part of a meal, with three- and five-piece options served with medium fries, a medium drink and a core dip, from £8.49. A chicken sharebox will also be available, comprising four tenders, 12 nuggets, two premium dips and two core dips, from £10.49. The chicken tenders will be available at participating Burger King restaurants nationwide, as well as through the brand’s app and delivery platforms.

articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . White Castle is kicking off a new year of value beginning Sept. 15 with the launch of Craver Nation Rewards Season 3. This follows a winning Season 2 — spanning Sept. 2025 to Sept. 2026 — which delivered $5.1 million in savings to members through exclusive deals and offers. Season 3 of Craver Nation Rewards, White Castle’s free-to-join customer loyalty program, brings new Quests, rewards and opportunities to level up, along with special offers throughout the year. To celebrate the launch, members can unlock 25% off one mobile order and earn double points on their first purchase between Sept. 15 and Sept. 30. Members will also receive 10% off purchases at HouseofCrave.com, White Castle’s exclusive online storefront, through Sept. 30. “White Castle has been committed to real value since day one,” said Jamie Richardson, chief marketing officer at White Castle. “As we kick off Season 3 of Craver Nation Rewards, we’re giving Cravers even more ways to unlock deals, rewards and memorable moments, because feeding the Crave should never break the bank.” Cravers saved big in Season 2 Craver Nation Rewards members made the most of their membership during Season 2, saving a combined $5.1 million through rewards, deals and exclusive offers. Over the past year: Craver Nation Rewards members earned 32 million points. Members redeemed more than 1.2 million offers. Chicago was home to the largest population of Craver Nation Rewards members. Friday at 2 a.m. was the peak ordering time for Craver Nation Rewards members. A fresh season of rewards Season 3 launches Sept. 15, giving every Craver Nation Rewards member a fresh opportunity to climb from Adventurer to Champion and ultimately Legend status while taking on new Quests and earning rewards along the way. Every badge members earn is theirs to keep. New members can also start their Craver Nation Rewards journey with $5 off their first Mobile Order of $8 or more. The welcome offer is valid for 30 days after joining. Beyond the Season 3 kickoff offers, Craver Nation Rewards members can look forward to exclusive deals throughout the fall. “To the Cravers who have been on this journey through Season 1 and Season 2, we thank you,” said Richardson. “And whether you’ve been with us from the beginning or are joining Craver Nation for the first time, Season 3 brings even more ways to save, earn and feed your Crave.” The post White Castle Launching Craver National Rewards Season 3 appeared first on QSR Magazine .

articles.title: How Sydney Grims Learned to Lead at Fearless Restaurants
articles.titleKo: How Sydney Grims Learned to Lead at Fearless Restaurants
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Sydney Grims likes to say she stands on the shoulders of giants. Lacking opportunity, her great-grandparents left behind their lives in Poland and Italy and settled in the suburbs of Philadelphia, opening Central Tavern, a bar that both her grandfather and father would spend countless hours working in. Her father would go on to open The Fountain Restaurant at the Four Seasons Hotel, then La Fourchette, Taquet, Passerelle, Bravo, and more. These restaurants became a daycare for Grims; she’d spend every weekend there, baking cookies with pastry chefs and catching lizards in the creek out front. She grew up watching her parents dedicate their lives to their business: early mornings, late nights, odd hours. Except her father never asked her to go into the family business. If anything, he tried to talk her out of it. “My parents never pressured me to follow in their footsteps because they knew that the lifestyle is very challenging. My dad would always tell me I would have to really, genuinely love what I do if I wanted to go into restaurants.” Register today to join women leaders at FSR and QSR’s WiRL Summit! She set out to build her own voice in hospitality, leaving Philadelphia for New York, where she’d spend her early career rising through the ranks at Hillstone Restaurant Group’s rigorous hospitality management training program and serving as director of hospitality for MacAndrews & Forbes. Moving back home at age 26 to join as a general partner for her family’s 14-location, $80 million hospitality group, Fearless Restaurants, she didn’t realize how much she had to unlearn. “It’s very intimidating to be in the workplace as the only woman, also being young and feeling like you need to prove yourself, especially when you are constantly just referred to as ‘the boss’s daughter,'” Grims says. “I felt the pressure to have a strong skill set at a young age to be respected.” Helping lead roughly 1,500 employees across brands like Moshulu, White Dog Cafe, Tuckers Tavern, Rosalie, Autograph Brasserie, and Louie Louie, Grims found it difficult to find her footing in those initial months. She had come from an environment where she was taught to be tough, to “grin and bear it,” to discipline rather than manage—and she very quickly found out that wouldn’t work here. “To me, a good leader is someone who isn’t going to use a hammer on their employees; they’ll use a wrench, tools to get the job done rather than just disciplining people. When I first moved back home, I think I was very hard-headed,” Grims says. “I felt like I had to be really tough, stronger than everybody in the room, and I had to really dig deep to learn where strength and good leadership come from.” It took time, and a fair share of costly missteps, before Grims found her footing. Once she did, her focus shifted from proving herself to building something lasting. “When I came on board, I saw this as something I’m going to be doing for the rest of my life, and at the time, there wasn’t a master plan for growth. I wanted to build a strategy for long-term longevity, and the starting point is making everybody’s lives easier. Efficiency is the name of the game,” Grims says. She’s currently spearheading a 14-location POS migration, consolidating systems and weighing every financial decision against the brand’s future goals. Grims has also leveraged artificial intelligence to assist her with day-to-day decisions—like scheduling and sending follow-ups— freeing up the kind of time the generations of restaurateurs before her rarely got. “People in the restaurant business are not your average worker. Salespeople are good at sales. articles.title: Giving Kitchen Names Carmen Jackson Chief Operating Officer
articles.titleKo: Giving Kitchen Names Carmen Jackson Chief Operating Officer
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Giving Kitchen, the nonprofit that provides emergency assistance to food service workers through unanticipated crisis, has named Carmen Jackson as its Chief Operating Officer. Jackson begins in the role on September 14. Jackson brings more than 18 years of operational and strategic leadership across Fortune 100 enterprises, mission-driven organizations, and independent consulting. She began her career in food service and retail — an experience that gave her an early and enduring appreciation for the people who show up every day to keep the industry running. “Carmen understands both sides of this work — what it takes to run an organization well, and what it feels like to work a closing shift. That combination is rare, and it is exactly what this moment calls for. As our community grows, Carmen will make sure our ability to show up for it grows right alongside,” said Allison Padilla-Goodman Chief Executive Officer of Giving Kitchen. In 2025, a food service worker in crisis reached out to Giving Kitchen every 36 minutes. Behind each of those moments is a case manager who picked up the phone, a system that routed the request, and a process that moved support out the door quickly. Jackson’s role is to strengthen and scale that operational backbone as demand for the organization’s services continues to grow. “The mission here is personal, the team is exceptional, and the work ahead is exactly the kind I was built to do. The best outcomes happen when people are brought around a table and invited to build something side by side — that is how I intend to lead here.” said Jackson. Jackson’s career spans enterprise consulting at IBM, KPMG, and McKinsey, where she led post-acquisition integrations, built global centers of excellence, and delivered double- to triple-digit performance outcomes across financial services, technology, travel and hospitality, and energy. She has also led from inside mission-driven organizations, serving as Fractional Innovation Director for a national financial education nonprofit and as Executive Director of a community development corporation, where she rebuilt operational and financial infrastructure from the ground up and forged partnerships that generated measurable community impact. Through Metric Strategy Partners, her independent consulting practice, Jackson has spent recent years helping nonprofits build the governance frameworks, technology infrastructure, and operating models they need to sustain growth and serve their communities well. Jackson succeeds Brooke Kamke, Giving Kitchen’s first-ever Chief Operating Officer, who established the systems, processes, and team structure the organization operates on today. Kamke departs for a new opportunity with the organization’s deep gratitude. A graduate of the Georgia Institute of Technology with a Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering, Jackson also completed engineering coursework at Georgia Tech Lorraine in France. She is an alumna of Leadership Long Beach and a member of the Junior League. She has run six marathons in support of cancer research with Team in Training for the Leukemia & Lymphoma Society and several half marathons benefiting St. Jude. Pal's holds the distinction as the first restaurant company to earn the Malcolm Baldrige National Quality Award in 2001 and has twice won the Tennessee Quality Award. Pal’s Sudden Service, one of America’s leading regional fast food chains, has earned the prestigious Great Places To Work Certification for 2026-2027. The certification is based on Great Place to Work proprietary process which includes GPTW employee Trust Index Survey of more than 1,400 Pal’s team members. “The certification verifies our commitment to offering a great work environment aligned with our mission: to delight customers in a way that creates loyalty,” says Adam Crosby, President. “Our team takes pride in being the best at excellent customer service, providing high-quality, fresh, and consistently sudden made to order meals quickly and the empowerment of thorough one-on-one training across our service model promising ‘Great Food in a Flash®” to our customers. The Great Place To Work Certification® criteria are the global standard for quantifying and benchmarking the employee experience. Certification evaluates workplace culture and trust from the perspective that matters the most, the employee. It offers the most comprehensive picture on the market of the internal health of an organization. Pal’s holds the distinction as the first restaurant company to earn the Malcolm Baldrige National Quality Award in 2001 and has twice won the Tennessee Quality Award. The new Great Places To Work Certification is a result of continuing to follow the Baldrige criteria for excellence to become an ever-stronger company. “The Baldrige framework is how we continue to benchmark ourselves.” says Crosby. “Our focus today is to continuously improve our systems to optimize efficiencies and grow the skills of our team members.” “I want to thank our employees for their hard work in executing our mission daily and their trust in our organization and congratulations for sharing in this important designation,” Crosby concludes. The certification comes during Pal’s 70th anniversary year. Founded in Kingsport in 1956, Pal’s has grown to more than 30 locations throughout Northeast Tennessee and Southwest Virginia with more locations actively in development while remaining true to its commitment to quality and customer satisfaction. IHOP announced the nationwide return of Stuffed French Toast. Today, IHOP announced the nationwide return of Stuffed French Toast, bringing back one of the brand’s most popular and requested breakfast menu items. After years of guest requests across social media , the return of this breakfast classic marks the latest example of IHOP responding directly to guest feedback while expanding the brand’s portfolio of signature breakfast offerings. IHOP announced the nationwide return of Stuffed French Toast, bringing back one of the brand’s most popular and requested breakfast menu items. Since its debut in 2003, Stuffed French Toast has been a guest favorite, earning a permanent spot on IHOP’s menu after launching as a limited-time offering. Over the years, the brand has continued to evolve the platform through new flavors, premium ingredients, and elevated preparation techniques, including the introduction of Thick ‘N Fluffy French Toast in 2022 and reclaiming ownership of the category with a complete platform refresh in 2024. Now, after more than two decades of guest love and innovation, IHOP is bringing Stuffed French Toast back as a dedicated menu category, reaffirming its place as one of the brand’s most beloved breakfast offerings. “The return of Stuffed French Toast reflects our commitment to growing the IHOP brand by leaning into what guests love most,” said Lawrence Kim, President of IHOP. “We saw years of demand across social media and beyond, and we knew this was the right moment to bring back a fan favorite in a way that feels relevant for today. By pairing a beloved classic with new flavor innovation and a fresh marketing approach, we’re creating excitement for longtime fans while introducing a new generation of guests to one of IHOP’s most iconic breakfast experiences.” With 75 percent of orders centered around breakfast at any time of day, IHOP continues to innovate through differentiated menu verticals. The new Strawberry Vanilla and Blueberry Vanilla varieties build on the beloved Stuffed French Toast legacy while introducing exciting new flavor experiences. It’s a truly pastry-level, nostalgic experience that evokes cherished breakfast memories with a preparation and quality that stands apart in the category. Strawberry Vanilla & Blueberry Vanilla Stuffed French Toast: 2 triangles filled with sweet cream, dipped and griddled in our vanilla, cinnamon French toast batter. Topped with choice of glazed strawberries or blueberry topping and vanilla sauce. The return coincides with IHOP’s new “Fancy a French Toast?” campaign, a playful, over-the-top creative platform that transforms an everyday breakfast into a moment of accessible luxury. Inspired by the extravagance of the Rococo-era, the campaign embraces the growing “treat yourself” mindset, pairing indulgent visuals with a modern pop sensibility. Through bold, unexpected storytelling, IHOP positions Stuffed French Toast as a crave-worthy indulgence that delivers a luxurious experience without the luxury price tag, proving that guests don’t have to spend big to savor something special. By combining a beloved breakfast favorite with new flavor offerings and a modern marketing campaign, IHOP continues to evolve its menu while staying true to the breakfast experiences guests know and love. The return of Stuffed French Toast reinforces the brand’s commitment to building on its breakfast heritage while introducing distinctive offerings that set IHOP apart. articles.title: How Restaurants Can Reduce Risks and Protect Staff Through Workers’ Comp
articles.titleKo: How Restaurants Can Reduce Risks and Protect Staff Through Workers’ Comp
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Preventing injuries can help restaurant owners avoid indirect costs that often accompany workplace incidents. Restaurants are powered by people, from line cooks and servers to dishwashers and delivery staff. Foodies are routinely served by a person performing a physical role in a fast-paced environment, which comes with certain risks. Kitchens are rife with hot surfaces, sharp tools and wet floors. Dining rooms are bustling with customers, which challenges workers to navigate crowded areas while carrying heavy trays. Long shifts, repetitive motions and frequent lifting are further increasing the potential for worker injuries and business interruption. Those realities make workplace injuries and disruptions more common in restaurants than in many other industries, placing workers’ compensation insurance at the center of restaurant risk management. While often viewed as a legal requirement, workers’ compensation serves a vital role for restaurants, by providing protection for employees, offering a way to manage unexpected disruptions, and offering a level of stability when injuries occur. Some common workers’ compensation claims in the restaurant industry include: Slips and falls on wet or greasy surfaces Burns from grills, fryers or hot liquids Cuts from knives and food prep equipment Back and shoulder injuries from lifting supplies Repetitive strain injuries from food preparation or dishwashing With many restaurants experiencing high turnover and regularly onboarding new employees, maintaining consistent safety awareness can be an ongoing challenge. Why Workplace Safety Is Good for Business For many restaurant owners, workplace safety is viewed primarily through a compliance lens. However, a strong safety culture can deliver meaningful business benefits beyond reducing injuries. Preventing injuries can help restaurant owners avoid indirect costs that often accompany workplace incidents. For example, an employee injury may result in disruptions, overtime expenses, temporary staffing needs, training costs for replacement workers and decreased productivity while teams adjust to staff shortages. By focusing on prevention, restaurant owners can create a safer work environment while helping protect customer service standards and business continuity. Protecting the People Behind the Business Workers’ compensation insurance plays a vital role in helping restaurants protect the employees who keep their operations running. By understanding workplace risks and taking steps to manage them, restaurant owners can support their teams while building resilience in their business. In a restaurant, workers’ compensation may help cover: Medical care related to workplace injuries Partial wage replacement during recovery Rehabilitation or physical-therapy services Legal defense costs that arise from employee injury lawsuits For example, if a server slips while carrying a tray, or a cook burns their hand during food preparation, workers’ compensation can help ensure medical needs are addressed, while supporting the business through the disruption. Workers’ compensation is often misunderstood in restaurants, particularly where part-time or seasonal employees are common. Coverage generally applies regardless of hours worked, and even minor injuries may be covered if they occur on the job. Practical Steps Restaurants Can Take To Reduce Risk While insurance provides essential protection, prevention remains a critical component of managing workplace injuries. Restaurants can take proactive steps, such as: Providing consistent safety training during onboarding Addressing spills and hazards promptly Encouraging slip-resistant footwear Clearly marking hot surfaces and high-risk areas Promoting prompt injury reporting Offering light-duty options for employees returning from an injury-related leave These measures can help reduce the freque

The award recognises excellence across the UK hospitality industry, with winners selected by a panel of more than 100 leading industry professionals. Ross receives the accolade in the inaugural year of the Pastry Chef of the Year category, recognising his outstanding contribution to the craft of pastry, innovation and mentorship across the industry. As Executive Pastry Chef, Ross leads the patisserie, bakery and confectionery teams at both The Balmoral in Edinburgh, and Brown’s Hotel in London, overseeing the development of exceptional pastry programmes while continually raising standards across two flagship Rocco Forte Hotels properties. Alongside his culinary achievements, Ross has built a reputation as an inspiring mentor, supporting the development of young pastry chefs throughout his career. Many of those he has trained have gone on to successful roles in some of the UK’s and the world’s leading hotels and restaurants, reflecting his commitment to nurturing the next generation of hospitality talent. Commenting on Ross’s achievement, Richard Cooke, Managing Director, United Kingdom & Northern Europe, Rocco Forte Hotels, said: “ Ross has been back at The Balmoral as Executive Pastry Chef since 2015, and for the past three years has been Executive Pastry Chef overseeing both The Balmoral and Brown’s in London. The focused devotion to his craft and his knowledge is underpinned by a curiosity which takes his creativity to an exceptional level, which he keeps building upon. Ross consistently elevates the product in our properties in the UK and beyond. “

articles.originalSummary: Hakkasan Group are pleased to announce the appointment of Fai Choi as Research and Development Chef in the UK, marking a significant step in the Group’s continued investment in culinary innovation and the evolution of its UK food strategy Chef Fai joins the business with over a decade of Michelin-starred experience spanning London and Hong Kong. Most recently, he served as Head Chef at Mora in Hong Kong, where he secured and retained both a Michelin Star and a Michelin Green Star within his first year. His work there was recognised for its pioneering approach to sustainability, embedded within a refined, soy-focused fine dining concept. His career includes key roles within Simon Rogan’s restaurant group, including Aulis Hong Kong, as well as experience at Michelin-starred HIDE in London. In 2024, he received the Michelin Young Chef Award for his precision, creativity, and disciplined execution. In his new UK-based role, Chef Fai will lead the next phase of culinary development across Hakkasan and Yauatcha, working closely with CEO Yavuz Pehlivanlar, who was appointed in October 2025. His appointment reflects a clear strategic focus on innovation, sustainability, seasonality, and a more ingredient-driven approach to modern Cantonese cuisine, with an emphasis on refined, health-conscious dining. This year also marks a significant milestone, as Hakkasan celebrates its 25th anniversary this year. “I’m excited to be joining Hakkasan Group at such an important moment for the brand. Having spent time working across both Hong Kong and London, this opportunity feels especially meaningful to me. articles.title: New Cocktail Bar Coming to Raleigh’s North Hills Innovation District
articles.titleKo: New Cocktail Bar Coming to Raleigh’s North Hills Innovation District
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Patrick Shanahan — the hospitality visionary who has brought cinematic design to Raleigh’s most talked-about bars and restaurants this year — is bringing his signature creative sensibility to North Hills for the first time with co-owner Robby Opperman. Slated to open in 2027, Little Saint Cocktail Co. will mark Shanahan’s fifth project in two years, and North Hills’ first true standalone cocktail bar. Follow along at @LittleSaintRaleigh. Shanahan’s track record speaks for itself. Peregrine earned a James Beard Foundation nomination for “Best New Restaurant”; Capulet Cocktail Club at The Exchange was spotlighted in F orbes and Wine Enthusiast for its maximalist design; and Rosebud Cocktail Lounge in downtown Raleigh landed the cover of Raleigh Magazine’s Best Bars issue. This month, the all-day Café Royale will open at The Exchange, introducing a coffee-to-cocktail French café culture. With Little Saint, he’s bringing that same design-forward, hands-on approach to a part of the city that’s never had a dedicated craft cocktail destination of its own. “North Hills Innovation District (NHID) is a special place with a strong community of locals who come here to work, live, dine and spend time together,” said Mary Ehrenberger, Retail Leasing and Multi-Site Manager for Kane Realty Corporation. “Little Saint is a great addition to the lineup we’re building in NHID. Bringing a true cocktail bar to North Hills gives our guests another reason to linger and enjoy the neighborhood, and Patrick and his team have the creativity and hospitality experience to make this space a natural fit for the district.” Little Saint will occupy 3,865 square feet on the ground floor of the St. Albans Lofts building at 600 St Albans Drive, on the corner of St. Albans Street and Hardimont (directly across from Standard). The space will include outdoor seating along the street, adding to North Hills’ growing patio scene. As both designer and co-owner, Shanahan continues his hands-on approach to hospitality design. Little Saint will be completed by Mauer Architecture and JCI Builders, the same team behind his prior four projects. Little Saint Cocktail Co. will offer an elevated, upscale cocktail experience, filling a longstanding gap in North Hills for a dedicated craft cocktail destination. Follow along at @littlesaintraleigh for updates as the 2027 opening approaches. But first: Café Royale opens late September 2026 at The Exchange in Raleigh’s Midtown. Follow @CafeRoyaleRaleigh for opening updates. The post New Cocktail Bar Coming to Raleigh’s North Hills Innovation District appeared first on FSR magazine .

articles.title: Vicious Biscuit Signs Lease in Greenville, North Carolina
articles.titleKo: Vicious Biscuit Signs Lease in Greenville, North Carolina
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Vicious Biscuit, the original home of unapologetically bold biscuits, is adding an experienced multi-brand restaurant group to its growing franchise system. Operating as Gravy Crew, LLC, Chris Carnes, Ben Fields and operating partner Jonah Greenup, whose portfolio includes 11 Zaxby’s and six Chicken Salad Chick restaurants, have signed a lease for their first Vicious Biscuit in Greenville, North Carolina. The 3,000-square-foot restaurant will be located at 3030 S. Evans St. in University Commons and is expected to open late 2026. It will be Vicious Biscuit’s first franchise location in North Carolina, joining corporate-owned restaurants in Boone, Charlotte and Wilmington. The partnership brings together three operators who have worked alongside one another for nearly two decades. Carnes entered the restaurant business with Zaxby’s in 2001. Fields, who previously worked on the corporate side of Zaxby’s, joined Carnes in 2008. Greenup began with the group that same year, working his way from team member through management and eventually becoming a partner when the group added Chicken Salad Chick to its portfolio. While Carnes wasn’t looking to add another restaurant concept, Vicious Biscuit had been on his radar for some time. He first learned about Vicious Biscuit after seeing it featured on national television. Years later, while traveling to visit his son at Appalachian State University, he repeatedly passed Vicious Biscuit in Boone and noticed the crowds waiting outside. When he finally visited, what he found was different from the biscuit restaurant he expected. “I had probably passed it a dozen times and there were always people standing outside,” said Carnes. “We finally caught it without a line, went in and ordered a little bit of everything. I was expecting more of a mom-and-pop biscuit place, but as soon as I walked in, I realized this was a real concept. The food, the atmosphere and the personality of the brand were fun and edgy.” That experience prompted Carnes to take a closer look at Vicious Biscuit as a potential addition to the group’s restaurant portfolio. Carnes saw parallels to his early experience with Zaxby’s while the concept was still relatively young. “When I got into Zaxby’s more than 20 years ago, it was still early, and I saw what that could become,” Carnes said. “I told myself years ago that if I ever came across another opportunity I really believed in, I wasn’t going to let it pass me by. I like where Vicious Biscuit is today and the opportunity to grow with it.” Beyond the food and concept, Vicious Biscuit’s leadership team was an important factor in the group’s decision. After spending time with co-founder and CEO George McLaughlin and the team, Carnes saw an emerging concept with the infrastructure and experience his group wanted from a franchisor. “For an emerging brand, it feels very established,” Carnes said. “They’ve already built the infrastructure and support you’d expect from a much larger franchise system, and there are experienced people behind it. You have to love the product first, but just as important is knowing you can pick up the phone and call the people leading the company. When I met George and the team, it felt like a group of people we could work and grow with.” The group was also drawn to Vicious Biscuit’s operating model. Its single-shift schedule and 2:30 p.m. closing time offer a different operating environment from traditional full-day restaurant concepts, giving teams their afternoons and evenings back. The three partners initially signed for one restaurant, giving them an opportunity to operate within the Vicious Biscuit system before determining their next phase of growth. If Greenville performs as expected and the partnership proves to be the right long-term fit, the group sees potential for additional Vicious Biscuit restaurants in Eastern North C

articles.title: Lola Beans Signs 5-Unit Deal to Enter Miami Market
articles.titleKo: Lola Beans Signs 5-Unit Deal to Enter Miami Market
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Lola Beans, the fast-growing dual drive-thru beverage concept known for handcrafted coffee, energy drinks, teas, lemonades and its signature Lola Colas (infused sodas), has signed a five-unit development agreement to enter the Miami market. The deal marks another major step in the brand’s expansion, coming just one week after Lola Beans announced a six-unit development agreement for Delaware. The new franchisees, Daniela Gonzalez and Joangel “Joey” Lopez are immigrants from Nicaragua and Cuba who grew up in Miami, where coffee was always about much more than the drink itself. They grew up surrounded by the city’s cafecito and ventanita traditions, where strong, sweet Cuban-style espresso and walk-up coffee windows have long brought people together for a quick coffee, a familiar face and conversation with a neighbor. As they started families and built their careers, Gonzalez and Lopez came to appreciate the need for a coffee experience that could keep pace with modern life without losing that sense of community. “Miami has such a strong coffee culture, but it’s also a city that moves fast,” said Gonzalez and Lopez. “We fell in love with Lola Beans because it feels close to home. It brings the spirit of Miami’s ventanita cafecito culture into a modern dual drive-thru that delivers speed without sacrificing connection. The menu goes far beyond coffee, while still keeping that personal interaction. We’re confident that combination will resonate really well here.” The couple plans to initially develop five Lola Beans locations over the next five years. “We’ve been excited for a long time about building a strong presence for Lola Beans throughout Florida, and this agreement is an important first step in that vision,” said Donny Bradley, founder of Lola Beans. “Joey and Daniela understand the culture, the community and the experience we want Lola Beans to create, and we believe they will be the first of many outstanding franchisees to help establish the brand across Florida.” The Miami agreement adds to significant momentum for Lola Beans since beginning franchising in early 2025. Last week the brand signed a six-unit development agreement for Delaware and a 120-unit Texas agreement led by Kirk and Coleen Jeter through Rise Hospitality Group, Inc. Lola Beans’ founders have hand-picked a team of industry veterans with deep experience in franchise development and operations, marketing, site selection, supply chain and procurement-all focused on giving franchisees the support they need to grow successfully nationwide. “Collectively, our team has never seen this level of interest in a brand or segment before. Our Discovery Days are filling up fast,” said John Moates, Lola Beans’ Development Partner and CDO. The post Lola Beans Signs 5-Unit Deal to Enter Miami Market appeared first on QSR Magazine .

articles.title: Whit’s Frozen Custard Chooses Square as its Unified Commerce Platform
articles.titleKo: Whit’s Frozen Custard Chooses Square as its Unified Commerce Platform
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Square today announced that Whit’s Frozen Custard, the quick-service restaurant (QSR) brand known for its fresh-made frozen custard and loyal fan base, has selected Square as its unified commerce platform powering 100 locations nationwide. The move marks a pivotal step for the fast-growing franchise as it streamlines cross-location visibility, centralizes reporting and menu management, and builds a stronger foundation for continued expansion. Founded in 2003 in Granville, Ohio during one of the region’s coldest winters, Whit’s Frozen Custard began as a bold bet: that customers would fall in love with a product many had never even heard of. More than two decades later, that bet has proven sweet. With 100 locations across 11 states and a fiercely loyal following (including more than 60% repeat customers), Whit’s Frozen Custard has grown into a nationally recognized franchise known for its premium ingredients, daily fresh batches, and ever-changing “flavor of the week.” Now, under the leadership of CEO Bill Aseere – formerly a top-performing Whit’s Frozen Custard franchisee – the company is investing in the commerce platform needed to support its next chapter. “We’ve always believed that if you focus on delivering consistent quality, growth will follow,” said Aseere. “Our products and experiences upheld that standard, but as we scaled, it became clear that our technology needed to evolve alongside us. Too much time was being spent stitching gaps together across locations. We wanted to make life easier for our franchisees – enabling them to operate independently while giving our corporate team better visibility, and ultimately creating a smoother experience for our customers. Square helped us win on all fronts.” Keeping the Focus on the Custard Prior to choosing Square, Whit’s Frozen Custard operated on a combination of fragmented systems that added friction at every level of the business. Menu updates had to be manually managed across stores. Reporting lacked consistency and clarity. Franchisees were left navigating the complexities of payments, disputes, and compliance on their own. And corporate teams had limited visibility into performance and royalty tracking. Square’s franchise capabilities solved these problems in a single destination, giving the corporate team centralized control of its entities. The brand now uses Square Register, Square Kitchen Display System (KDS), Square for Restaurants, and Square for Franchises to power its growing network, removing a significant operational burden from franchisees and returning their attention to the custard that keeps customers coming back for more. In the process, franchisees see an estimated savings of approximately $2,000 annually per location across software and processing costs. “Food & beverage franchises require a delicate balance of independence on the ground and uniformity at the brand level,” said James Schonziet, Head of Food & Beverage at Square. “Square brings the operational infrastructure, reporting, and ease of use needed to scale a consistent experience across every location, while keeping it simple for the people running it day-to-day. Whit’s is a prime example of what we aim to enable on both fronts.” Serving Up the Future of QSR Through the partnership, Whit’s Frozen Custard is leaning into new ways of serving customers, including adopting Square’s emerging drive-thru capabilities to bring added speed and convenience to its operations while maintaining the brand’s signature, happy hospitality. By leveraging Square’s partner ecosystem, Whit’s is also preparing to utilize integrations that enhance online ordering, loyalty, and mobile app experiences, further enhancing how customers engage with the brand both in-store and digitally. As temperatures cool down, Hardee’s is blending summer nostalgia with fall coziness, launching a crave-worthy S’mores Platform and the hearty Bacon Beast Platform beginning September 9, along with the triumphant return of the fan-favorite Cinnamon ‘N’ Raisin Biscuit. A Summer Favorite Hardee’s new S’mores Platform celebrates those last warm moments of summer: • S’mores Iced Coffee: Blends Hardee’s signature cold brew coffee with toasted marshmallow and chocolatey syrups for a smooth, lightly sweet finish, perfect for a morning pick-me-up or an afternoon craving. • S’mores Hand-Scooped Ice Cream Shake: Creamy and decadent, featuring hand-scooped vanilla ice cream blended with toasted marshmallow and chocolate syrups, finished with graham cracker and chocolatey sprinkles for a new take on a classic S’mores favorite. • S’mores Fried Pie: The ultimate seasonal standout is guaranteed to be a new favorite, featuring a golden-brown shell filled with graham crumble, melty marshmallow cream and rich chocolatey filling. A Welcome Return The fan-favorite Cinnamon ‘N’ Raisin Biscuit is back! A sweet biscuit loaded with raisins and cinnamon, topped with a drizzle of icing. articles.title: Potbelly Opens in West McKinney, Texas
articles.titleKo: Potbelly Opens in West McKinney, Texas
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Potbelly, the iconic neighborhood sandwich shop known for its great food and good vibes, announced today the opening of a new shop in the DFW market. The new location brings Potbelly to the Stonebridge Ranch community of McKinney, one of the largest suburbs in the Metroplex. Opening on Saturday, September 5, the new shop is located in the Eldorado Neighborhood Shops near the intersection of Eldorado Parkway and Stonebridge Drive (3200 S. Stonebridge Dr., Suite 108). Situated at the southern edge of Stonebridge Ranch, the well-known master planned community, the shop gives nearby families, students, professionals and businesses a new go-to dining spot, whether grabbing a quick lunch, picking up dinner for the family or bringing Potbelly catering to a school, office or neighborhood gathering. The new shop will serve the oven-toasted sandwiches Potbelly is known for, along with wraps, signature salads, hand-dipped shakes, freshly baked cookies and other craveable menu favorites. Potbelly in West McKinney is owned and operated by father-son duo Barry and Remington Burke of Burke Restaurant Group, who bring decades of combined experience in multi-unit restaurant operations, franchising and entrepreneurship. The Burkes have long seen strong potential for Potbelly in West McKinney, drawn to the area’s growth and neighborhood-driven character. Looking ahead, the Burkes also plan to bring Potbelly to additional neighborhoods across North and East Texas as part of their 15-shop development agreement, furthering their investment in the region. “West McKinney has such a strong sense of community and a lot of energy around its growth, making it a natural fit for Potbelly,” said Remington Burke. “We’re looking forward to opening our doors and bringing residents and the local workforce together over great food and good vibes. Our team is ready to welcome longtime Potbelly fans and first-time guests alike with the craveable food, friendly service and neighborhood-driven atmosphere that define Potbelly.” To celebrate the opening, Potbelly will host a celebration on September 19 from 11 a.m. to 1 p.m. Guests can enjoy a morning of food, fun and prizes with a Spin the Wheel activity featuring opportunities to win Potbelly merchandise and other giveaways, including up to 50 Free Potbelly for a Year prizes. Joining more than 65 locations across Texas and dozens in the DFW market, the West McKinney shop will offer convenient options for lunch, dinner and everything in between. Regular operating hours are 10 a.m. to 9 p.m. daily. Delivery, order ahead and catering are available in-shop, through Potbelly.com and in the Potbelly App, with third-party delivery services also available. For exclusive offers and rewards, Potbelly invites guests to join the Potbelly Perks program, where members can unlock free sandwiches, cookies and special offers throughout the year. To sign up, visit www.potbelly.com/perks. For more information about the new Potbelly location, visit www.potbelly.com. articles.title: Primanti Bros. Parent Authentic Restaurant Brands Captures $325 Million Investment
articles.titleKo: Primanti Bros. Parent Authentic Restaurant Brands Captures $325 Million Investment
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . The portfolio encompasses 225 restaurants that collectively produce more than $1 billion in annual revenue and over $150 million in EBITDA. Authentic Restaurant Brands has secured a $325 million capital package to accelerate restaurant development and pursue additional acquisitions. The infusion came from London-based firm Trimontium. The investment includes debt and equity, with funding available as ARB identifies growth opportunities. It will support expansion across ARB’s existing markets and the selective acquisition of more regional restaurant concepts. Founded in 2021 and headquartered in Austin, Texas, ARB owns Pollo Tropical, Tavern in the Square, P.J. Whelihan’s, Mambo Seafood, and Primanti Bros. The portfolio encompasses 225 restaurants that collectively produce more than $1 billion in annual revenue and over $150 million in EBITDA. ARB has also recorded four consecutive years of positive same-store sales growth. The company, backed by Garnett Station Partners, targets established regional concepts with deep community ties and loyal customer bases. Its model gives acquired brands access to technology, data, analytics, and shared resources intended to support expansion without stripping away their local identities. “Our growth has always been deliberate,” ARB cofounder, chairman, and CEO Alex Macedo said in a statement. “We buy brands people love, we keep the operators who built them and we give them the tools to scale efficiently and thoughtfully. This capital lets us do more of that, faster.” Garnett Station formed ARB in 2021 through the acquisition of Primanti Bros., a Pittsburgh-based concept founded in 1933. The platform added P.J. Whelihan’s in 2022, Houston-based Mambo Seafood and Pollo Tropical parent Fiesta Restaurant Group in 2023, and Tavern in the Square parent Broadway Hospitality Group in 2024. Each of ARB’s five concepts has operated for more than 25 years. The portfolio spans several distinct geographic territories, including Florida, Texas, Pennsylvania, Maryland, Ohio, West Virginia, Massachusetts, Philadelphia, and South Jersey. Trimontium founder and chief investment officer Vlado Spasov described ARB as a high-quality restaurant business with a differentiated platform and a clearly defined expansion strategy. He also pointed to Garnett Station’s operating experience in foodservice as a key component of the transaction. Trimontium manages $1.6 billion in assets and provides flexible capital solutions to companies in Europe and North America. The firm is headquartered in London, maintains a presence in Luxembourg, and plans to expand into New York. Garnett Station, founded in 2013, manages approximately $4.5 billion in assets. Its primary investment categories include consumer and business services, health and wellness, automotive, and food and beverage. Simpson Thacher & Bartlett served as Trimontium’s legal adviser. Houlihan Lokey acted as valuation adviser, and La Presa Partners served as tax adviser. Kirkland & Ellis acted as ARB’s legal adviser, with Evercore serving as financial adviser. “Trimontium understood how we operate from the first conversation and structured their solution around what will support the business today,” Macedo said. “We are excited for this next chapter.” The post Primanti Bros. Parent Authentic Restaurant Brands Captures $325 Million Investment appeared first on FSR magazine .

articles.title: After 10 Years of Sales Growth, The Melt Takes its Biggest Step Yet
articles.titleKo: After 10 Years of Sales Growth, The Melt Takes its Biggest Step Yet
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . The Melt has 24 locations. The Melt spent a decade proving it could transform its restaurants. Now it must prove someone else can run them just as well. The California-based fast casual is moving into franchising after lifting average unit volumes from $700,000 to roughly $3.5 million under CEO Ralph Bower. The growth plan calls for the company to reach 80 corporate restaurants by 2030 across California and Arizona, with franchisees carrying the brand into new states. It is a significant turn for a chain that was primarily known for grilled cheese when Bower arrived 10 years ago. The menu has since evolved into chef-inspired comfort food led by burgers, melts, mac and cheese, and chicken. The operating model has undergone an even larger transformation, producing 10 consecutive years of positive same-store sales and online ratings that have held between 4.7 and 4.8 this year. “I don’t know of another brand that’s ever been able to drive their AUVs from 700 [thousand] to 3.5 [million],” Bower says. His first move was to ask customers and employees what should change and what should stay. An email to the brand’s database drew 1,100 responses. Bower posed the same two questions to restaurant operators, collected the findings in a spreadsheet, and acted on the feedback. The resulting sales climb accelerated during the pandemic. Average unit volumes were near $1.5 million entering 2020 and doubled to $3 million by 2021. They have since gained another $500,000. The Melt’s sales initially fell 80 percent when shelter-in-place orders arrived in San Francisco, recovered to flat by May 2020 and set a record in June. Sales increased 57 percent from July through the end of that year, followed by a 54 percent gain in 2021 against the prior surge. The Melt had spent years preparing its kitchens to withstand high-volume periods. Its speed of service did not change by five seconds when sales doubled, Bower says. Proprietary software alerts restaurant personnel when ticket times breach key thresholds. A nine-minute average over a 15-minute window triggers texts to Bower, the chief operating officer, area manager, and general manager. A 15-minute mark prompts automated calls. Those peaks can arrive late. Forty percent of The Melt’s sales occur after 10 p.m. One San Francisco restaurant recently processed a $4,600 hour from 11 p.m. to midnight, following a $3,000 hour. A La Jolla store that routinely posted weekly sales near $20,000 before the pandemic reached $80,000 per week by the end of 2020. The brand ties employee bonuses to guest feedback and delivery errors instead of sales and profit. Operators join a 9 a.m. call seven days per week to review customer responses, mistakes, and restaurant performance. Teams also hold rallies before lunch and dinner shifts based on the companywide goal of delivering an “I love it here” experience to every guest. “I think sales and profits are what you did yesterday, what you did last week, and what you did last month. It’s history,” Bower says. “The number one indicator of what your success tomorrow is going to be is your guest feedback today.” The Melt’s franchising push will test whether that culture can transfer outside its corporate system. Bower has long been cautious of licensing the concept because he could not know how much of its improvement came from the food and how much came from operational intensity. Greg Vojnovic, head of franchising, began advising the company roughly a year ago. He and Bower previously worked together at Popeyes, and Vojnovic had evaluated two Melt sites years earlier. The initial discussion was not necessarily focused on franchising. It concerned how a successful regional brand should grow and whether its restaurants could succeed in distant markets. articles.title: Tijuana Flats Begins Next Chapter with Ambitious Franchise Push
articles.titleKo: Tijuana Flats Begins Next Chapter with Ambitious Franchise Push
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Tijuana Flats wants to be 80 percent franchised. Tijuana Flats is back in the franchising game. The brand relaunched its franchising program this spring following a turbulent stretch marked by bankruptcy, restaurant closures, and a change in ownership. Now, the 30-year-old chain is emerging from that reset period under the recently formed Latitude Food Group. Latitude was created after &pizza acquired Tijuana Flats last fall, forming a two-brand platform built around shared services and multi-brand franchising. The premise is to preserve the distinct personalities at the core of each concept while combining back-end resources to improve economics and create a more scalable foundation for operators. Tijuana Flats has taken a winding path through franchising. After beginning to franchise in the early 2000s, the brand halted new development in 2007 following a challenging early period and leaned more heavily on company-operated growth. It resumed a selective push in 2019, but that effort was paused a few years later. The company last filed its FDD in 2023, according to Latitude’s chief development officer Brett Willis. Tijuana Flats filed for bankruptcy in 2024 and closed dozens of restaurants. Under then-CEO Jim Greco, the company sought to stabilize operations, sharpen its positioning, improve menu offerings, and tighten restaurant-level costs. It emerged from bankruptcy in early 2025 before becoming part of Latitude later that year and officially relaunching franchising this spring. The immediate plan is twofold: refranchise select company-operated restaurants and pursue new development from both existing and prospective operators. Latitude is offering corporate stores in packages of three to five locations, with opportunities for larger packages, while conversations with existing Tijuana Flats franchisees are also underway. “Right now it’s heavily corporate owned,” Willis says. “We really want to take that more into a traditional franchising equation, meaning that 80 percent of the restaurants will be franchised and 20 percent will be corporate. We’ve kicked off an initiative alongside restarting our franchising program to sell some of our corporate shops to help spur some of that growth.” The company aims to sell about 20 restaurants this year—roughly 20 percent of the existing portfolio—and secure another 20 to 40 development commitments through a mix of new-build agreements and deals tied to refranchised locations. Initial development attention is centered on Florida and the broader Southeast, where Tijuana Flats has its deepest brand recognition and operating base. Latitude does not intend to eliminate its corporate footprint altogether. It expects to retain a core group of company-operated restaurants, particularly around its Orlando headquarters, to test new menu items, technology, and operational initiatives before expanding them throughout the system. For prospective franchisees, Latitude’s main selling point is the platform behind the brand. While &pizza and Tijuana Flats remain separate consumer-facing concepts, their parent company can consolidate purchasing, marketing, technology, training, HR, creative production, and vendor relationships. The goal is to lower recurring costs, strengthen support, and create more dollars for franchisees to either retain or reinvest in growth. “At the core, the shared-services model allows us to really leverage economies of scale, which ultimately result in better unit economics,” says CMO Sergio Perez. That can mean savings on everyday operating expenses or additional resources for revenue-driving initiatives such as loyalty, media, catering, and third-party delivery. articles.title: Mountain Mike’s Pizza Opens in Georgetown, Texas
articles.titleKo: Mountain Mike’s Pizza Opens in Georgetown, Texas
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Mountain Mike’s Pizza, a leading family-style pizza chain for nearly 50 years, and home of the legendary crispy, curly pepperoni, massive 20-inch Mountain-sized pizzas and dough made fresh daily, is now open in Georgetown, Texas, marking the 17th location in the Lone Star State. The Georgetown restaurant is owned and operated by Rajeev Dewan, who owns two existing Mountain Mike’s locations in Manor and Cedar Park, and is actively developing two additional locations across Central Texas. For nearly five decades, Mountain Mike’s Pizza has delighted guests with “Pizza the Way it Oughta Be!” and is rapidly expanding into new markets across the country. Williamson County residents and visitors alike can enjoy the brand’s signature pizza experience at the new Mountain Mike’s in Georgetown, whether dining in, carrying out or via delivery. “As a business owner, I am deeply committed to creating lasting, meaningful connections with the local community, and Mountain Mike’s Pizza gives us the opportunity to bring families together while supporting local schools, first responders and youth programs that make Georgetown thrive,” said Dewan “Georgetown’s historic character, welcoming atmosphere and strong sense of community make it an exciting place to bring Mountain Mike’s, and we’re proud to join the growing local restaurant scene with ‘Pizza the Way It Oughta Be!’” The spacious 2,400-square-foot Mountain Mike’s Pizza in Georgetown features the welcoming, family-friendly atmosphere for which the brand is known. Boasting six big-screen televisions, the Georgetown restaurant is bound to be a go-to destination for sports fans, no matter which team guests root for. The Georgetown restaurant also includes a weekday all-you-can-eat pizza buffet and salad bar, an outdoor patio, kids’ arcade area and complimentary Wi-Fi. There is something for everyone at Mountain Mike’s in Georgetown, making it an ideal spot for guests of all ages, team parties, family get-togethers, office gatherings and group fundraising events alike. One bite into a cheesy slice of pizza from Mountain Mike’s takes you back to childhood, providing a sense of nostalgia for when pizzas were handmade with the freshest and finest ingredients. From its legendary crispy, curly pepperoni, 100% whole milk mozzarella cheese and a variety of fan-favorite specialty pizzas, Mountain Mike’s has something to satisfy every taste. Whether it’s dine-in, carryout or its own in-house delivery, guests can always count on Mountain Mike’s to ensure quality, freshness, flavor and value. Orders may be placed online, through the Mountain Rewards App or through any of the brand’s third-party delivery partners. The new Georgetown Mountain Mike’s is located at 1314 W University Ave., Suite 101, and can be reached by (512) 352-9888. The restaurant is open Sunday through Wednesday from 10:30 a.m. to 10 p.m. and Thursday through Saturday from 10:30 a.m. to 11 p.m. For additional information about Mountain Mike’s Pizza, visit www.mountainmikespizza.com. For additional information about the Georgetown location, visit Mountain Mike’s Georgetown/W. University Dr. or find the restaurant on Google and Yelp. articles.title: Buddy’s bar-b-q Adds Chicken Tenders to Menu
articles.titleKo: Buddy’s bar-b-q Adds Chicken Tenders to Menu
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Buddy’s bar-b-q has spent more than 50 years serving up slow-smoked favorites across East Tennessee, and now the hometown staple is adding a crispy new option to the mix. New chicken tenders are officially on the menu, giving Buddy’s guests another affordable, family-friendly favorite alongside the bar-b-q, Southern sides and signature flavors they already know and love. Fried fresh and served hot, Buddy’s tenders feature juicy chicken hand-coated in a golden, crispy breading. Served plain, tossed in Buddy’s bar-b-q sauce or finished with Buddy’s signature seasoning for an extra kick — the new tenders bring a satisfying crunch and classic Buddy’s flavors to every bite. The tenders can be ordered à la carte in four- or five-piece portions, or as a combo with a drink and guests’ choice of side from Buddy’s classic Southern lineup. Four-piece orders start at $5.59 à la carte or $8.99 as a combo, while five-piece orders start at $6.59 à la carte or $9.99 as a combo. Guests can round out their chicken tender meal with comforting Southern sides, from savory Hushpuppies and Baked Beans to Coleslaw and Potato Salad. Each tender combo also comes with a choice of bar-b-q, ranch or honey mustard dipping sauce, adding an extra boost of flavor to every crispy bite. “Our guests have always trusted us to deliver quality food made simple at a great price, and we think these chicken tenders fit right in at Buddy’s,” said Mark Lemoncelli, CEO of Buddy’s bar-b-q. “Whether it’s an easy family dinner, a quick lunch or something the kids will love, we’re always looking for ways to give our guests more choices while staying true to what they’ve loved about Buddy’s for generations.” The new chicken tenders continue Buddy’s tradition of serving A Smokin’ Good Deal™, bringing an affordable, familiar favorite to the menu alongside the franchise’s signature bar-b-q offerings. With options for a quick bite, family meal or something in between, the tenders give longtime fans and new guests alike another way to enjoy the flavor and value Buddy’s has served for generations. With more than five decades of tradition behind it, Buddy’s continues to evolve its menu while staying rooted in the classic flavors, great value and Southern hospitality that have defined the brand since 1972. Buddy’s new chicken tenders are available now at all locations across East Tennessee. For more information on Buddy’s bar-b-q, please visit Buddysbarbq.com. articles.title: Hyll Appoints David Kelman as Executive Chef
articles.titleKo: Hyll Appoints David Kelman as Executive Chef
articles.originalSummary: Cotswolds boutique hotel HYLL has appointed David Kelman as Executive Chef, bringing one of the region’s most respected culinary talents to lead the food offering at the new 17th century manor house hotel. Kelman joins HYLL following his role at Estelle Manor in Oxfordshire and brings more than two decades of experience across some of the UK’s most acclaimed country house hotels and hospitality destinations. Originally from North Wales, Kelman has built an impressive career spanning Bodysgallen Hall, Lower Slaughter Manor, Wyck Hill House, Ellenborough Park, Cowley Manor, Thyme and Burford Garden Company. He is particularly recognised for his tenure as Executive Head Chef at Ellenborough Park in Cheltenham, where he led the Beaufort Dining Room to three AA Rosettes and received numerous accolades, including Best Chef at the Taste of Gloucestershire Awards and Chef of the Year at the Cotswold Life Food & Drink Awards. A familiar face within the industry, Kelman represented Wales on BBC’s Great British Menu in 2014 and has cooked for members of the Royal Family, including Queen Elizabeth II and the then Prince of Wales. He has also represented Wales internationally as a member of the Welsh National Culinary Team. At HYLL, which opened in September 2025, Kelman will oversee the hotel’s culinary direction, developing menus that celebrate the seasons and the exceptional produce of the Cotswolds and surrounding counties. His approach centres on ingredient-led cooking, strong relationships with local suppliers and creating memorable dining experiences that reflect a genuine sense of place.
koreanSummary: Cotswolds boutique hotel HYLL has appointed David Kelman as Executive Chef, bringing one of the region’s most respected culinary talents to lead the food offering at the new 17th century manor house hotel.

Kelman joins HYLL following his role at Estelle Manor in Oxfordshire and brings more than two decades of experience across some of the UK’s most acclaimed country house hotels and hospitality destinations.

articles.title: Businesswoman Behind £20m+ London Hospitality Group Reveals New French Riviera Hotel and Art-Led Villa
articles.titleKo: Businesswoman Behind £20m+ London Hospitality Group Reveals New French Riviera Hotel and Art-Led Villa
articles.originalSummary: Former investment banking director Elmira Amdiy is expanding beyond her seven-strong London restaurant portfolio and existing French Riviera hotel, with a new hotel development and art-led villa on the Mediterranean coast. The businesswoman behind the Wild Group, the eight-figure hospitality group that includes some of London’s most coveted restaurants, including Belvedere, Wild Tavern, Wild Izakaya, Wild Corner, Wild Notting Hill, Chelsea Grill and Pinna Mayfair, has revealed the next stage of her wider hospitality portfolio, with two major projects underway on the French Riviera. Former investment banking director Elmira Amdiy, formerly of Barclays Capital, Nomura and UBS , is preparing to restore and redevelop a collection of historic buildings into a new hotel, named Hotel Les Chardons, while also creating a private seven-bedroom art villa at her existing luxury hotel, Hostellerie La Farandole. The villa is being created in partnership with renowned artist and sculptor Grishi Giano, who is designing the property in its entirety, from its recycled materials and interiors to original stone sculptures, creating a villa that will be a work of art in its own right . Meanwhile, plans for Hotel Les Chardons are taking shape , with Amdiy currently developing the concept around a potential focus on wellness and longevity . The historic buildings will be carefully restored and redeveloped, with architectural plans revealing landscaped gardens, restaurant terraces overlooking the French Riviera and a large outdoor swimming pool with an expansive poolside lounge area. Amdiy said: “Hotel Les Chardons is a significant project for us. We’re taking a collection of existing buildings and creating something new around them, while also being very conscious of what is already there and what we can restore. If we do take Les Chardons in the wellness and longevity direction, we will make sure there is real substance behind it, and a reason for people to travel specifically to stay with us. ” The projects mark a significant expansion of Amdiy’s hospitality interests beyond London, where she has spent the past five years working alongside her partners and team to build Wild Group from a single restaurant into a £20m+ portfolio spanning seven venues and employing more than 300 Londoners . Her involvement in hospitality began in France. Alongside her career in investment banking, Amdiy was already involved in the ownership of Hostellerie La Farandole before investing in Wild Tavern in 2020 and going on to help build the wider Wild Group portfolio. A SEVEN-BEDROOM VILLA CREATED AS A WORK OF ART The seven-bedroom private villa at Hostellerie La Farandole is on track for completion by the end of 2026, when it will become available to book through the hotel. Set within private grounds, the villa will have its own swimming pool and pétanque area . Amdiy is working closely with renowned artist and sculptor Grishi Giano on the design of the entire villa , with art and design being developed together from the outset. His involvement spans materials, furniture and lighting to original sculptures created specifically for the property and its grounds . Amdiy said : “I didn’t want us to design the villa and then decide what art to put on the walls afterwards. Grishi has been involved from the very beginning, so the art is part of the design rather than something added at the end. We have quite different instincts, which is what makes the collaboration interesting. My taste is far more classical, while Grishi will push things much further. We challenge each other, and that’s often how we get to the best result.” Giano said: “My role goes far beyond creating the artworks. The villa is being created in partnership with renowned artist and sculptor Grishi Giano, who is designing the property in its entirety, from its recycled materials and interiors to original stone sculptures, creating a villa that will be a work of art in its own right .

articles.title: Broadwick Soho in London’s West End joins Small Luxury Hotels of the World’s Finest Collection
articles.titleKo: Broadwick Soho in London’s West End joins Small Luxury Hotels of the World’s Finest Collection
articles.originalSummary: Small Luxury Hotels of the World (SLH) has welcomed Broadwick Soho as the first London hotel to join its Finest Collection, a selection of exceptional, independent properties recognised for their distinctive character, unmistakable sense of place and consistently outstanding guest experiences. Set in the heart of London’s West End, Broadwick Soho brings a bold, bohemian and deeply personal expression of luxury to the collection. The 57-room hotel channels the glamour, eccentricity and creative energy of its neighbourhood through richly layered interiors, characterful dining and an evolving cultural programme spanning art, music, design and performance. It’s a vibrant hub for local creativity, connection and community. Conceived by a group of friends and creatives, the property, located at 20 Broadwick Street, Soho is partly inspired by owner Noel Hayden’s childhood memories of his family’s flamboyant seaside hotel in Bournemouth. Internationally acclaimed interior architect Martin Brudnizki brought the vision to life in his first London hotel project, combining English eccentricity, Jazz Age opulence and disco-era glamour. A dynamic assortment of materials, colours, fabrics and textures have been used to create a whimsical and colourful menagerie, embodying 70s hedonism. Each room and suite has been meticulously designed, featuring bespoke furniture by Brudnizki, antiques and vintage curios. The hotel’s 10 suites and Penthouse are swathed in marbled wallpaper depicting floating elephants, tigers and exotic flora and fauna, complemented by handmade furniture such as custom minibars masquerading as brass elephants, made in Jaipur. The kaleidoscopic hotel is also home to more than 300 original artworks, bringing together internationally recognised names and emerging global artists. Highlights include works by Andy Warhol, Francis Bacon, Bridget Riley, Victor Pasmore, Faye Wei Wei and Casey Moore, alongside specially commissioned pieces created for the guestrooms and suites. A cultural address in the heart of Soho Broadwick Soho’s cultural programme further connects guests with Soho’s creative life. Since opening in November 2023, the hotel has hosted live performances from artists including Sister Sledge, Sheryl Crow, Sophie Ellis-Bextor and Dave Stewart, alongside DJs, emerging talent, talks and events linked to London Fashion Week, Pride in London and Frieze. During Frieze London from 15 to 18 October 2026, Broadwick Soho will host an artist residency centred around Moroccan multidisciplinary artist Rita Alaoui. The programme will combine an artist-led workshop with access to Frieze London, private gallery visits and intimate conversations with artists, collectors, curators and cultural figures. “Broadwick Soho is exactly the kind of hotel Small Luxury hotels of the World was created to celebrate – a small hotel with a big experience” said Richard Hyde, Chief Operating Officer at Small Luxury Hotels of the World. “It is independently minded, deeply personal and inseparable from the character of its location. Every element, from its design and art collection to its cultural programming and hospitality, reflects a confident and original point of view.” He continued, “Finest Collection brings together hotels that are destinations in their own right. Defined by the strength of their identity, the quality and consistency of their guest experience and their ability to offer something genuinely distinctive. It’s the sum of all the small and thought details at Broadwick Soho that gives us an outstanding first Finest address in London.” “We are incredibly proud to be joining SLH’s Finest Collection and to be recognised alongside such an exceptional collection of independently owned hotels from around the globe. articles.title: Tigermilk Brings Hacienda Grandeur to the Heart of East London
articles.titleKo: Tigermilk Brings Hacienda Grandeur to the Heart of East London
articles.originalSummary: Their modern South American inspired interior brings life to their largest site to dat e Following its successful opening in May, Tigermilk Spitalfields’s interior has emerged as one of the defining elements of the new flagship restaurant by Alexis and Nina Melikov, the group’s largest site to date. Designed by Studio Leche, Tigermilk’s in-house design studio, the space brings together hacienda-inspired architecture, layered materials and a warm, transportive atmosphere that has become central to the guest experience. Conceived as an escape in the heart of Spitalfields, the ambition was to build an environment that guests would immediately want to stay in, rather than one designed purely to be photographed. Central patios, generous proportions, fountains, handcrafted materials and lush greenery give the space its structure and soul, evoking the kind of environment that takes decades to settle into its surroundings. Antique furniture sits alongside bespoke pieces, and reclaimed terracotta, natural stone, marble and aged timber are used throughout, materials that carry history and wear it well. “People rarely talk about specific design features. They talk about the atmosphere,” adds Alexis. “If people leave believing the space possesses a history, then we have succeeded in creating something that feels authentic rather than constructed.” A considered selection of suppliers and craftspeople underpins the interior. Sogni and Pooky provide the lighting, Pierre Frey and Morris the fabrics and upholstery, and Mandarin Stone the marble and stone surfaces. Flexhouse – responsible for custom joinery, millwork and bespoke fabrication – also contributed to the furniture alongside vintage pieces and Leta, while Resources delivered the decorative wall finishes. Together they bring a layered quality to the space, as though each element has its own provenance and story. With its new 280-cover restaurant, hacienda-inspired interiors and striking luminescent bar stocked with more than 2700 bottles, Tigermilk Spitalfields invites guests into what feels like the brand’s thirteenth home. Through a considered interior scheme full of texture and attention to detail, the restaurant offers a transportive South American-inspired experience designed to engage every sense.

articles.title: Regency House: Chris McClurg and Alice Stewart on building their dream restaurant
articles.titleKo: Regency House: Chris McClurg and Alice Stewart on building their dream restaurant
articles.originalSummary: The couple have returned to Belfast to take over Regency House hotel - and finally open the restaurant they’ve spent two decades planning. The drizzle is light but persistent as the taxi winds its way through south Belfast, the cooler air a noticeable shift from the late-summer warmth left behind in London. There is an edge to this part of the city, a little roughness around the polish, before a row of Georgian townhouses comes into view. Among them sits Regency House, Belfast’s only Michelin Key hotel. The journey ends just shy of the front door, interrupted by a swarm of television crews setting up cameras outside, an unusual welcome and an early indication of the attention already gathering around the building, which is set to feature in at least two television series. Inside, past reception and into a courtyard-style dining room, is Regency House’s first public-facing restaurant: a compact space centred on an equally compact open kitchen, where Parisian bistro meets Northern Irish produce.
