articles.title: The Flying Biscuit Café Opens in Knoxville, Tennessee
articles.titleKo: The Flying Biscuit Café Opens in Knoxville, Tennessee
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . The Flying Biscuit Café opens its downtown café at 327 W Summit Hill Dr SW in Knoxville, Tenn., on Saturday, Sept. 12, 2026, bringing the Atlanta-born breakfast and brunch brand into the city’s downtown core for the first time. The café is owned and operated by Chris Compton, who opened the brand’s first Tennessee location at 11683 Parkside Dr in the Turkey Creek area in May of 2025. Downtown is his second Flying Biscuit café. The space includes a patio and a full bar and covers 3,428 square feet with seating for 140. Compton expects to employ around 30 people at the location. Compton chose the Summit Hill Drive site for its position in the center of the city and its proximity to the University of Tennessee, where he swam as an 11-time All-American and SEC champion and was ranked among the top 10 swimmers in the world in 1992. He said the blocks around the café draw downtown office workers, state and city employees, and UT students through the week, with few sit-down breakfast options among them. Before moving into hospitality, Compton spent more than 20 years founding and running companies in credit card finance, real estate development and technology consulting. “Turkey Creek has been good to us, and the question we kept hearing was when we were coming downtown,” said Chris Compton, owner of The Flying Biscuit Café Knoxville. “There are a lot of people on these blocks by 8 a.m. and not many places to sit down and eat. Creamy dreamy grits, freshly baked biscuits, a rich pistachio latte and somebody glad to see you walk in — that’s what opens on Summit Hill on Sept. 12.” The Flying Biscuit Café Downtown Knoxville is at 327 W Summit Hill Dr SW, Knoxville, TN 37902, and opens to guests Saturday, Sept. 12. Hours are 7 a.m. to 2 p.m. Monday through Thursday and 7 a.m. to 3 p.m. Friday through Sunday, with dinner service from 5 to 9 p.m. Friday and Saturday. The café serves breakfast and lunch daily and offers full-service catering. Guest inquiries can go to knoxvilledowntown@flyingbiscuit.com and catering requests to knoxvilledowntowncatering@flyingbiscuit.com. The location phone is (865) 427-6748. Menus and location details are at flyingbiscuit.com. Compton’s Turkey Creek café remains open at 11683 Parkside Dr, Knoxville, TN 37934, (865) 288-0513. Compton plans to keep working with Knoxville-area nonprofits through the downtown café, continuing the partnerships he built around Turkey Creek. He plans to keep developing Flying Biscuit cafés in the greater Knoxville area over the next five years. Flying Biscuit Franchising is continuing to award territories across the Southeast and Texas including Tennessee, Kentucky, Florida, Virginia, Arkansas, and Ohio. Prospective operators can review open markets, ownership requirements and how to start a conversation with the development team at flyingbiscuitfranchising.com. articles.title: JOEY Restaurants Opens Second Dallas Location
articles.titleKo: JOEY Restaurants Opens Second Dallas Location
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . JOEY Restaurants, the award-winning, globally inspired hospitality group known for its elevated yet approachable culinary experiences, will open JOEY Maple, its second Dallas location, on Thursday, September 10. Located at 2508 Maple Avenue, the restaurant will offer a dynamic new destination for Uptown Dallas residents and visitors alike, serving lunch, happy hour and dinner. As part of the brand’s continued U.S. growth, JOEY Maple will bring the company’s signature blend of globally inspired cuisine, exceptional service and vibrant atmosphere to the neighborhood. “Uptown Dallas has one of the most energetic dining communities in the country, and expanding in Texas is a significant milestone for our brand, representing an exciting step in our growth strategy,” said Layne Krienke, president of JOEY Restaurants. “We designed JOEY Maple around a menu that gives guests a reason to keep coming back, from approachable favorites to globally inspired dishes and signature JOEY creations. Whether it’s a quick lunch or dinner that turns into drinks, the food is at the heart of the experience.” TOP CHEF TALENT, GLOBAL FLAVORS AND SIGNATURE SIPS At JOEY Maple, Executive Chef Matthew Stowe, a winning Top Chef alumnus and recent guest judge, will lead a menu that blends JOEY signatures with globally inspired flavors, bringing the brand’s distinctive approach to contemporary dining. The beverage program will be overseen by Bar Development Leader Jay Jones, a Restaurant Hall of Fame inductee, alongside Group Sommelier Jason Yamasaki. The menu reflects JOEY’s long-standing philosophy of blending global culinary techniques with high-quality ingredients showcasing a balance of premium steaks, fire-torched sushi, fresh seafood, bowls, handhelds and shareable plates. Guests can soon enjoy iconic cuts such as the Bone-In Prime Ribeye and Tomahawk, served with JOEY’s signature Crispy Mashed Potatoes alongside new dishes including Crispy Nigiri, Caviar, Truffle Udon Carbonara and JOEY Signature Chocolate Cake. The beverage program includes a curated wine list selected by Yamasaki and handcrafted cocktails from the Sarti Spritz and The Good Life Margarita, to the Woodsmoked Old Fashioned and JOEY Martini. Guests can also enjoy the JOEY Supers, a twist on the classic highball with its noteworthy lemon-lime slush. THOUGHTFULLY DESIGNED, INSPIRED TO CONNECT Designed as a modern, dynamic escape, JOEY Maple offers a comfortably elegant retreat in Uptown Dallas. The exterior establishes strong architectural presence through expansive floor-to-ceiling glazing, and sculptural vertical wood screening that softens the building’s profile. With over 7,800 square feet, the design centers around an immersive indoor alfresco environment, anchored by a fully operable skylight and perimeter operable windows, creating the sensation of dining outdoors while enjoying the comfort of the interior. Guests are welcomed by a fire bowl lounge surrounded by lush plantings and greeted by a sculptural curved millwork wine display to establish a strong sense of craftsmanship and hospitality. A signature statement light installation introduces a playful, artistic element that immediately defines the restaurant’s character. Guests will also delight in a gallery wall featuring one-of-a-kind works by America Martin, B Shawn Cox and James Wolanin. The collection is anchored by a custom commissioned piece from artist Mina Eskandari that pays homage to the site’s previous identity as a beloved day lounge and pool destination, celebrating the history of the location while giving it a contemporary new expression. Positioned as a focal point at the back of the restaurant, the open kitchen is celebrated with a dramatic lighting installation where the warm amber glow will draw guests through the space and enrich the dining atmosphere. The Village Dallas announces the appointment of Chef Eduardo Osorio as Culinary Director, expanding his leadership across the iconic Dallas community’s collection of restaurants, bars and entertainment destinations. As Culinary Director, Osorio will collaborate with the culinary teams across The Village to guide menu development, maintain quality and consistency, mentor culinary talent and support the continued evolution of each concept’s culinary program. His leadership will support a cohesive food and beverage vision across the property while allowing each destination to retain their own distinct experience. “The Village is more than a place where people live and work—it is a destination where the Dallas community and visitors can come together to experience a diverse mix of dining, shopping, entertainment and hospitality,” said Osorio. “I’m excited to work alongside the talented teams at each culinary concept and continue raising the bar across the property. Buzz & Bustle , The Village’s neighborhood coffee shop and daytime gathering place serving coffee, breakfast, lunch and grab-and-go selections. “Chef Eduardo has demonstrated an exceptional ability to pair culinary creativity with genuine hospitality and strong leadership,” said Brandy Spence, VP of Food & Beverage for The Village. “He understands that each of our concepts serves a different purpose while contributing to the larger experience of The Village. articles.title: Flame Broiler Launches New Nonprofit Foundation
articles.titleKo: Flame Broiler Launches New Nonprofit Foundation
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Flame Broiler, the family-owned quick-service restaurant brand known for its Korean-inspired rice bowls, announces the launch of the Flame Broiler Foundation , the company’s new philanthropic arm dedicated to supporting and feeding under-resourced youth and communities. The Foundation marks a new chapter in the brand’s legacy on the heels of its 30th anniversary and begins with a new round up campaign. For the month of September, guests can round up their change to the nearest dollar or donate any additional amount at checkout, both online and in-store at participating locations. To make the most impact, Flame Broiler has underwritten all operational overhead costs so that 100% of proceeds will benefit nonprofit organizations dedicated to the Foundation’s mission: to promote food equity and the betterment of communities. Flame Broiler Foundation will provide funding, meal donations and volunteer support to local organizations that deliver after-school programming, community enrichment and healthy meal programs. This work will be defined by three key priorities: promoting youth food equity, empowering community development and transforming food systems. The Foundation has supported around 400 youth through grants and in-kind donations to after-school and summer programs for at-risk students, foster youth, family services, workforce development and more. The Lee family, founders Young and Sarah, along with their sons Daniel, Christian and David, continue to lead the business that now spans two generations. The Foundation represents the family’s continued commitment to breaking down barriers for nutritious food, beyond the four walls of the restaurants. “Feeding communities was why we started Flame Broiler to begin with,” said Christian Lee, president and chief operating officer of Flame Broiler. “Thirty years later, we’re proud to carry on that same spirit, while expanding our impact through the Flame Broiler Foundation, ensuring philanthropy remains at the heart of our business.” The California-born brand continues to collaborate with local organizations such as longtime partners like OC United and new partners like Crece Urban Farms to help meet immediate needs of the community. Previous giveback has included delivering thousands of nutritious school lunches and supporting first responders through meal donations. “We believe that everyone, regardless of their background or location, should have the ability and opportunity to access and consume healthy, affordable and culturally connected foods,” said Asako Lee, executive director, The Flame Broiler Foundation. “We’re committed to advancing food equity and inspiring healthier communities for the next generation and the round up campaign is our first step – giving our guests a simple way to take part in our mission.” In-store and online rounding will run throughout the month of September at all corporate locations in California and participating franchisee locations. Customers across the country can participate when ordering online or through the Flame Broiler Magic Rewards app. To learn more, visit www.flamebroilerfoundation.org. Lou Malnati’s Pizzeria is celebrating football season with the return of its fan-favorite BuffaLou Chicken Pizza and a new Lou’s Rewards promotion rewarding loyalty members with free wings every time they order on game day and their market’s qualifying professional football team wins. The limited-time pizza is topped with Lou’s handcrafted wing sauce, made from a proprietary blend of homemade ranch dressing and Frank’s RedHot Original Cayenne Pepper Sauce. It’s built on Lou Malnati’s signature buttery, flaky crust, finished with Wisconsin mozzarella, premium all-white meat chicken, red onion and fresh parsley. Beginning Sept. 10, BuffaLou is available in both deep dish and thin crust for dine-in, carryout and delivery at all Lou Malnati’s locations, and ships nationwide for a limited-time through TastesofChicago.com. The pizza’s return comes alongside a new way for football fans in two of the company’s markets to celebrate a win. Starting with the season opener on Sept. 13, Lou’s Rewards members are automatically eligible for the promotion when they order on a qualifying game day in their market: games involving Chicago’s professional football team at Chicagoland locations, and games involving Chicago’s or Arizona’s professional football team at Arizona locations. When the qualifying team wins, a reward posts to the member’s account the next day, a free medium order of wings with any $30 purchase, redeemable within seven days. The promotion spans all game days each market’s qualifying teams are scheduled to play, keeping loyalty members engaged with Lou Malnati’s throughout the football season. “Guests have been asking us to bring BuffaLou back, and football season felt like the perfect time,” said Julie Younglove-Webb, CEO of Lou Malnati’s. “Lou’s has always been about bringing people together, whether it’s a family gathering or a game day watch party. Our new limited-time offering and Lou’s Rewards promotion carries that spirit forward, giving fans more reasons to come together and celebrate on game day. Order the BuffaLou to cheer on your team, then come back for free wings when they win.” For more information on BuffaLou Chicken Pizza, visit loumalnatis.com. Applebee’s is bringing back its fan-favorite National Cheeseburger Day deal, offering guests a Classic Burger or Classic Cheeseburger served with Fries for just $8.99 on Sept. 18. Available for dine-in and To Go, the one-day offer gives guests the opportunity to enjoy a Handcrafted Burger and fries for less than $9.* Applebee’s Handcrafted Burgers feature a juicy, all-beef patty topped with lettuce, tomato, onion, and pickles on a Brioche bun. Guests can choose between a Classic Burger or Classic Cheeseburger, topped with two slices of American cheese, both served with Fries as part of the National Cheeseburger Day offer. “A great cheeseburger hits the sweet spot between comfort, craving, and value, which is exactly what guests are looking for right now,” said Michelle Chin, chief marketing officer at Applebee’s. “Burgers remain one of our most-loved menu categories, and National Cheeseburger Day gives us the perfect excuse to come together and celebrate them. Whether guests choose our Classic Cheeseburger and fries for $8.99 or one of our delicious, over-the-top O-M-Cheese creations, we’re serving up something for every burger craving at Applebee’s.” Guests looking for an upgraded cheeseburger experience all month long can also enjoy Applebee’s NEW O-M-Cheese-adilla Burger, the latest addition to Applebee’s viral O-M-Cheese lineup, available on Applebee’s 2 for $25 value menu.** The over-the-top mashup transforms Applebee’s fan-favorite Quesadilla Burger with bacon and Pepper Jack cheese into a cheese-loaded experience served sizzling in a skillet of molten queso and melted Cheddar cheeses with white corn tortilla chips topped with queso, house-made pico and cilantro. Applebee’s 2 for $25 Menu Applebee’s popular 2 for $25 menu lets diners share one appetizer and choose two full-size entrees from a selection of guest favorites. Wings Etc. is adding a new sauce presentation to the menu with a Ranch Flight launching Tuesday, Sept. 15. The limited-time offer introduces two new ranch flavors — for a total of five — and a three-sauce presentation designed to encourage flavor sampling, customization and incremental sales. With the Ranch Flight guests can choose any three dips from the brand’s five house-made ranch flavors, including House Ranch, Ranch Fire, Parmesan Garlic Ranch and the brand-new Buffalo Ranch and Dill Ranch. The menu innovation expands the ways guests can dip, dunk, mix, match and customize their meals with Wings Etc.’s Big Flavor. The promotion also introduces a new presentation format for Wings Etc.’s sauces. Wings Etc. has invested in a new melamine serving tray for dine-in orders designed to enhance the overall in-store presentation compared with serving sauces in individual 2 oz. portion cups. Beyond presentation, the new tray makes it easier for guests to sample and compare three flavors at once and mix flavors for complete personalization. It offers a way for guests to amplify any menu item, from wings to burgers, sandwiches and fries — even pizza. “The Ranch Flight encourages guests to sample, compare and discover their favorite,” said Wings Etc. COO Chuck Moore. “Instead of simply serving dipping sauces, we’re creating an interactive flavor experience that serves up excitement.” The expanded lineup of ranch-inspired flavors and the launch of a Ranch Flight reflects Wings Etc.’s commitment to Big Flavor. In addition to the timeless House Ranch; the bold and adventurous Ranch Fire; and the rich and savory Parmesan Garlic Ranch, Wings Etc. is introducing two new ranch sauces: Dill Ranch starts with fresh dill finely chopped in-house. It’s stirred into classic ranch dressing with a splash of pickle juice for a bright, herb-forward dip that pairs perfectly with wings, wraps and sandwiches. Buffalo Ranch blends the cool creaminess of ranch dressing with the tangy heat of Wings Etc.’s signature Buffalo flavor — another top sauce among Wings Etc. guests — creating a perfectly balanced bit of kick for wings, tenders and fries. “Our objective is simple: When guests think about ranch, we want Wings Etc. to be the first brand that comes to mind,” said Moore. “By establishing our dominance with five ranch flavors and the Ranch Flight, we can create a unique competitive advantage, drive additional attachment sales, strengthen our flavor leadership and deliver an experience that guests can’t find anywhere else.” Wings Etc.’s investment comes as ranch grows in broad consumer appeal. It was one of the most talked about flavors around the globe during the FIFA World Cup, rivaling hydration breaks for online buzz. 1 But it’s been a favorite condiment nationwide for years. 2 According to Datassential, 3 75 percent of Americans like it or love it, more than any other dressing, and 44 percent of consumers have ranch weekly. “We know how much our guests love ranch — it’s our top-selling dip,” said Wings Etc. CEO Rob Hensmann. “As the Ranch Authority, we give fans more of the Big Flavor they crave, with fresh new varieties and the ability to personalize our award-winning wings as well as any menu item.” The Ranch Flight is a limited-time offer available in all markets. It will be served in a melamine tray for dine-in orders; carryout and delivery flights will be served in three 2 oz. cups. Pricing for the add-on is $2.69 to $2.99, depending on market. Now Trending: Savory Pumpkin bellagreen looks beyond lattes and pie, incorporating nutrient-dense pumpkin in healthful, hearty dishes, including: Pumpkin Beef Chili – ground beef simmered with pumpkin puree, onions, bell peppers, carrots and warm spices, topped with sour cream, jalapeño and shredded cheese GF 4.99 / 6.99 Seared Salmon with Pumpkin Sauce – pan-seared salmon topped with a house-made creamy pumpkin sauce, served over rice pilaf with butternut squash and carrots GF 19.99 Nature’s Harvest Salad – spring greens, roasted butternut squash, red roasted beets and quinoa tossed in fig balsamic dressing, finished with goat cheese and toasted pumpkin seeds GF 14.99 Golden Glow Roasted Veggie Bowl – a returning favorite from the Winter Golden Glow menu, with quinoa, kale, roasted sweet potatoes and cauliflower, avocado, pumpkin seeds and a golden tahini-sriracha drizzle. GF 11.99 Add protein: +4.99 grilled or blackened chicken or tofu, +6.99 grilled or blackened shrimp or salmon Golden Glow Chicken Soup – slow-simmered chicken infused with turmeric, ginger, garlic, onions, tender sweet potatoes and carrots, with a touch of cream, finished with fresh herbs. articles.title: Middle Eastern Concept De Babel Opens Second Scottsdale, Arizona

articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . De Babel is opening its second Scottsdale location at The Edge, introducing a distinctive format that brings together made-to-order Middle Eastern food, elevated hospitality and a carefully curated market of essential Middle Eastern products. Located at 8980 N. 90th St., Suite 124, the new restaurant preserves the familiar flavors, quality and consistency established at De Babel’s original Pima Road location. De Babel remains a strictly halal kitchen, with restaurant food preparation and made-to-order menu items following the brand’s halal standards. The Edge location expands the experience beyond the traditional fast-casual model. It offers large patios, comfortable soft seating and an environment designed to encourage guests to relax, gather and experience genuine Middle Eastern hospitality without sacrificing convenience. “We wanted to create a more complete experience while remaining true to who we are,” said De Babel founder Marwan Kandeel. “The food will continue to be made to order, the kitchen will remain strictly halal and our guests will still find the consistent flavors they know. At the same time, we are creating a more comfortable environment and making important Middle Eastern products easier to find.” A carefully curated Middle Eastern market The market features selected Pereg kosher products alongside Halloumi, Bulgarian, Akkawi and Nabulsi cheeses; Tahsildaroglu Goat’s Milk White cheese; tahini; pickles; and a wide assortment of gluten-free packaged products. Although the retail market carries selected kosher-certified packaged products, De Babel itself remains a strictly halal kitchen. The distinction allows the restaurant to maintain its halal menu while making thoughtfully selected packaged products available to guests with different dietary preferences. Organic beverages served differently Guests can sample Tractor beverages from six juice taps and four bubblers serving iced tea and lemonade. De Babel will also offer dairy-free tahini ice cream as part of its expanded range of thoughtful alternatives. The same food, with a more expansive experience Despite the added retail and hospitality elements, the made-to-order menu remains at the center of De Babel. The new restaurant delivers the same Middle Eastern flavors associated with the original location while giving guests more ways to experience the brand – whether stopping for a quick meal, gathering on the patio or purchasing traditional products to take home. “This is not about changing the food or turning De Babel into something unfamiliar,” Kandeel said. “It is about protecting what our guests already love and building a better experience around it.” A quiet and intentional opening De Babel will not hold a traditional grand-opening celebration or introduce promotional discounts. Instead, the restaurant will open quietly and intentionally. The measured opening period will allow the team to strengthen its systems, build consistency under pressure and refine the guest experience before Metro Phoenix enters its high season and welcomes the return of winter visitors. “We are choosing to grow with discipline,” Kandeel said. “Before the busiest season arrives, we want our team to become confident, consistent and fully prepared to deliver outstanding hospitality every day.” The post Middle Eastern Concept De Babel Opens Second Scottsdale, Arizona appeared first on QSR Magazine .

Named in honor of Collin Sewell’s grandmother, Millie Leigh Cruson, the restaurant pays tribute to a cherished family legacy while serving as a gathering place where guests can enjoy approachable, made-from-scratch cooking throughout the day. Together, these details celebrate the warmth, generosity and love that made Millie Leigh so cherished. Chef David brings together his Southern Appalachian roots and the bold, rustic flavors of West Texas, weaving time-honored recipes inspired by Millie Leigh herself into a menu that honors her family traditions through comforting, made-from-scratch dishes. Millie Leigh’s works closely with local and regional farmers, ranchers and specialty producers, including proprietary beef producer 1911 Cattle Co., Broken Arrow Ranch, Midland Meat Company, Tortilleria La Perla, Anderson Farms, Volleman’s Dairy, Harding Hen House and Maribea Cocoa. These partnerships bring trusted Texas ingredients to the menu while supporting producers throughout the Permian Basin and beyond. O’Charley’s has shuttered company-owned restaurants across the country, bringing the once-prominent casual-dining chain closer to disappearing after years of contraction. Employees at multiple restaurants said Wednesday would be their final day, with many locations scheduled to close permanently at 8 p.m. The shutdown came with little warning for workers and without a public explanation from the Nashville-based company. In O’Charley’s home market, Nashville television station WKRN contacted managers at six of the chain’s eight Middle Tennessee restaurants. They said employees at all eight had been informed that their restaurants would close Wednesday at 8 p.m. The company did not respond to the station’s repeated requests for comment. NewsChannel 5 in Nashville reported that employees at multiple restaurants were informed Tuesday that Wednesday would be their last day. The Manchester Times in Manchester, Tennessee , separately spoke with a staff member who said employees received only one day’s notice. The restaurant had operated in the community for nearly 20 years. In Marion, Illinois, the restaurant’s general manager told local television station KFVS that the O’Charley’s would permanently close at 8 p.m. Wednesday. Employees there were informed of the decision Wednesday morning. The restaurant had been part of the Marion community for 24 years. In Kentucky, a staff member at the Hopkinsville restaurant confirmed to local radio station WHOP that the location would permanently close Wednesday at 8 p.m. The employee said nearly all O’Charley’s restaurants were expected to shut down. The two O’Charley’s restaurants in Northern Kentucky, located in Florence and Cold Spring, were also closing. The closures did not immediately include every restaurant. The franchised O’Charley’s in Niles, Ohio, will remain open until September 27 before permanently closing, according to an employee who spoke with the Columbus Dispatch . O’Charley’s Facebook and Instagram accounts were deactivated Wednesday, according to several local outlets. Its website, however, remained operational as of Wednesday evening. At its peak, O’Charley’s grew to nearly 250 restaurants across the U.S. The chain reported 244 locations across 19 states in 2010, including 234 company-owned restaurants and 10 franchised units. Charlie Watkins founded O’Charley’s in 1971 on 21st Avenue near Vanderbilt University in Nashville. The concept is now majority owned by Cannae Holdings. In the hero spot, Baby Spice and Ginger Spice reminisce about their former bandmate, from her pumpkin-inspired hits to her signature choreography and unwavering devotion to the flavor of the season. Years after going their separate ways, the trio reunites over Dunkin’s pumpkin drinks, giving Pumpkin Spice one more chance to pitch a comeback and prove that some passions never go out of season. “I think Pumpkin Spice was just ahead of her time. Getting to bring Pumpkin Spice back with Emma and Geri for Dunkin’ was so much fun. It feels like she’s finally getting the recognition she deserves.” The campaign builds on the Aug. 19 return of pumpkin season at Dunkin’, with a lineup of pumpkin beverages and bakery favorites available for a limited time at participating Dunkin’ restaurants nationwide. articles.title: Joe & The Juice Launches Refreshed Morning Menu
articles.titleKo: Joe & The Juice Launches Refreshed Morning Menu
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . On September 9, JOE & THE JUICE is rolling out a new menu and a global campaign to own the morning. The chain is refreshing and expanding its morning line-up – coffee, functional smoothies and shots, bowls, plus a new hot breakfast menu featuring eggs – bringing it together for the first time as one coordinated push. JOE has sold its iconic juices, coffee and morning products for years, and the name itself is slang for coffee. Yet despite guests already starting their day with JOE, survey data shows that one in four people still don’t think of JOE as a morning destination – a gap the new menu and campaign are now set out to close. The new hot egg products will see their widest rollout in the UK and US, but will also be available in select stores across the Nordics, Europe and in several of JOE’s franchise markets, including the Middle East, while all markets are simultaneously sharpening their focus on the morning experience. “We’ve built our name on juice and coffee, made fresh, at lunch and in the afternoon. Mornings are the one part of the day we haven’t won yet – and that’s the one we’re going after now,” says Thomas Noroxe, CEO of JOE & THE JUICE. Mornings currently make up a smaller share of JOE’s business than lunch and afternoon, and the company sees it as one of the most overlooked growth opportunities. Emphasis will vary by market, but the ambition is the same everywhere: making JOE the natural first stop of the day. “We’ve offered a breakfast range for quite a while, but demand for eggs specifically has grown, and it gives our morning guests more to choose from. This campaign is about making sure people think of JOE the moment they start their day, whether they want juice, coffee, eggs or something else,” Noroxe continues. The launch marks the start of a longer-term push to build morning habits among customers. articles.title: Jersey Mike’s is Chasing More Customers, Not More Pricing
articles.titleKo: Jersey Mike’s is Chasing More Customers, Not More Pricing
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Jersey Mike's has over 1,600 restaurants in its pipeline. Jersey Mike’s has a clear destination for its restaurants. The sandwich giant wants average unit volumes to climb from roughly $1.4 million to $2 million. Its path there is starting with transactions. Same-store sales rose 2.3 percent in the second quarter, accelerating from 1.7 percent in Q1. The increase was driven primarily by transactions, and momentum carried into the third quarter, with comps tracking above 3 percent at the time of Jersey Mike’s inaugural earnings call on Wednesday. The company expects same-store sales growth of 2.5 to 3 percent for the full year, including 3 to 4 percent in the third quarter. Pricing is expected to contribute 1 percentage point or less during the second half. Jersey Mike’s made a deliberate decision in late 2025 to rely less on price and put more energy into traffic. “We made a conscious decision last year in the fourth quarter to reduce the amount of price we took as a brand and focus our efforts on growing transactions for the long term, which we believe is a much healthier way to grow the business,” CEO Charles Morrison said during the brand’s Q2 earnings call. READ MORE : Making the Case for Why Jersey Mike’s is Just Getting Started Jersey Mike’s Raises $1 Billion, but Shares Fall in Public Debut Jersey Mike’s Reported Another Year of Growth in 2025 That pursuit is changing how Jersey Mike’s markets itself. Despite brand awareness of roughly 90 percent, the chain sees room to attract customers who know its name but visit infrequently, particularly Gen Z and Hispanic consumers. Digital marketing accounted for less than 1 percent of spending before climbing above 20 percent in the first half of 2026. Loyalty registrations increased 22 percent year-over-year, and ad awareness among Hispanic guests rose 6 percent. Morrison said Jersey Mike’s had done little call-to-action digital advertising before 2026. The shift gives the chain another tool to convert recognition into visits and eventually move customers into its loyalty ecosystem. The opportunity is substantial. Jersey Mike’s has an estimated 12 million to 13 million loyalty users, including roughly 7 million active members. Those active customers visit approximately once per month. Morrison believes the database can eventually reach 30 million to 50 million users. Digital sales also increased roughly 200 basis points during Q2 and accounted for 43 percent of sales. Jersey Mike’s sees that figure eventually reaching 60 to 70 percent. Delivery represents just under 20 percent of total sales, but first-party delivery accounts for only roughly 3 percent. The company sees first-party delivery eventually reaching 10 percent of sales as more guests order through Jersey Mike’s own digital channels. “We’ve seen that segment grow this year, but it’s from a very low base. But we do know that our marketing efforts are working to drive more customers to that channel and present them with a better value proposition, notably our loyalty program,” Morrison said. The digital push is arriving alongside a more active product calendar, although Jersey Mike’s plans to keep limited-time offers to two or three per year. Chicken salad brought new guests into restaurants and helped drive second-quarter sales acceleration. Mike’s Hot Italian, which first appeared earlier in 2026, returned with a regular sub priced at $8.95. Its food cost is below 20 percent of sales compared with an average food cost near 27 percent across the brand. The company sees its flat grill as another source of menu opportunities. Hot subs and cheesesteaks can reach different occasions and younger customers without forcing restaurants to add an extensive list of new ingredients. The sales opportunity is not confined to menu launches or digital ordering. Catering represents roughly 3 percent of sales today,

articles.title: Inspire Brands CEO Temporarily Steps Away Ahead of Potential IPO
articles.titleKo: Inspire Brands CEO Temporarily Steps Away Ahead of Potential IPO
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Inspire Brands CEO and cofounder Paul Brown is expected to return after his medical leave. Inspire Brands CEO and cofounder Paul Brown is temporarily stepping away from the restaurant giant as it prepares for a potential entrance into the public markets . Brown is taking a medical leave as he recovers from a recent injury, according to the Wall Street Journal , which cited a message sent to employees. Scott Murphy, president of Dunkin’ and chief brand officer of Inspire, will serve as interim CEO. The Journal reported that Murphy told employees he does not expect Inspire’s strategy or direction to change during Brown’s absence. Inspire also expressed confidence that Brown will return after his recovery. The timing comes during a pivotal stretch for one of the world’s largest restaurant companies. In May, Inspire confidentially submitted a draft registration statement with the SEC for a proposed IPO. The Journal previously reported that an IPO could arrive by the end of 2026, although the process could extend into early 2027. Brown became CEO of Arby’s in 2013 and helped oversee the chain’s turnaround before Arby’s Restaurant Group acquired Buffalo Wild Wings for $2.9 billion in 2018. That deal led to the formation of Inspire. The company quickly grew through a string of major acquisitions. Sonic joined the portfolio in 2018 in a deal valued at roughly $2.3 billion, followed by Jimmy John’s in 2019. Inspire then acquired Dunkin’ Brands in 2020 for $11.3 billion, bringing Dunkin’ and Baskin-Robbins into the fold in one of the largest restaurant transactions in industry history. Today, Inspire oversees more than 33,400 restaurants across Dunkin’, Buffalo Wild Wings, Buffalo Wild Wings GO, Arby’s, Jimmy John’s, Sonic, and Baskin-Robbins. The brands combined for $33.4 billion in global system sales in 2025 and are supported by roughly 650,000 company and franchise employees. Inspire is controlled by private equity firm Roark Capital. Murphy brings extensive experience inside the portfolio to the interim CEO position. He has spent more than two decades with Dunkin’ and its predecessor organization, holding positions that included COO of Dunkin’ and president of Dunkin’ Americas before becoming brand president. He was named Inspire’s chief brand officer in 2023. Several of Inspire’s concepts also have histories as public companies. Sonic traded publicly for roughly 27 years before Inspire acquired it, Buffalo Wild Wings spent about 15 years on the public markets, and Dunkin’ Brands was public for nearly a decade before its acquisition. articles.title: The ‘Burger Revolution’ Arrives at Carl’s Jr.
articles.titleKo: The ‘Burger Revolution’ Arrives at Carl’s Jr.
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Carl's Jr. is launching the Angus Maximus to introduce customers to its new cooked-to-order standard. There are a few layers to how Carl’s Jr. plans to talk about one of the most impactful brand changes in some time. But chain president Iwona Alter returns to the obvious. “All in all,” says Alter, a former Habit Burger COO who joined in January, “we call this whole program a ‘Burger Revolution,’ because that’s what it is. We are changing how we are making our burgers.” Naturally, this represents a consequential turn for a brand founded 85 years ago as a hot dog cart (a drive-in model opened four years later in Anaheim, California, with the “Jr.” version arriving in 1956 as a smaller, faster unit). Burgers have been on the menu dating to 1946—the official start of the “Baby Boom” generation. How Carl’s Jr. plans to ignite a “burger revolution” harkens back as well. It’s ditching pre-cooked patties, stepping away from hot-holding stations (Prince Castle), and cooking every burger to order. When Alter was appointed brand president, she brought two-plus decades of burger experience to the title, having spent 13 years at Jack in Box, including two as CMO, before her tenure at Habit. She says Carl’s Jr’s began having conversations under new leadership. The brand’s parent company, CKE Restaurants (along with Hardee’s), tapped Joe Guith as CEO in March 2025, coming over from Church’s Texas Chicken and prior stops at GoTo Foods, McAlister’s Deli, Cinnabon, and Coca-Cola. He was CKE’s third CEO since 2023, following Ned Lyerly and Max Wetzel, the latter of which now directs Tropical Smoothie Café. As is often the case with any redirect of this scope, Alter says, Carl’s Jr. looked at how it could get back to the core of who it was as a brand. That’s felt different over the decades, she says, but one recurring thread was “being bold,” whether it’s flavor, branding, or design. Secondly, though, how do you progress that into the present? “And think of how that boldness looks like?” she says. Carl’s Jr. turned to social listening and survey tools to ask guests. The most-common response wasn’t a complex dilemma: customers wanted hot burgers, consistently. When done correctly, Carl’s Jr.’s char-broiled equity proved clear and its product held ground in the most-crowded QSR field there is. Carl’s Jr. ended 2025 with 992 stores and average-unit volumes of $1.422 million, good for 13 th among the 14 burger brands in this year’s QSR 50 by systemwide sales ($1.425 billion ). Ahead of Carl’s Jr. was Shake Shack ($1.541 billion) and behind, Freddy’s ($1.04 billion). So, what was the path to consistency? There weren’t going to be any shortcuts, Alter says. Carl’s Jr. needed to transform the entire near-1,000-unit system regarding how it delivered a hot patty. While the idea wasn’t convoluted (cook to order), it did present a material shift in production, execution, and mindset. One note, Alter explains, is Carl’s Jr. was already here on other pieces. Stores chop lettuce and slice tomatoes and onions in-restaurant every day. “So, why not the patty?” Alter says. “And knowing the guests are looking for that. Knowing that yeah, the dollar now has to work so much harder because as I’m spending it, I want something that will satisfy the craving.” As Carl’s Jr. explored its brand premise, a mantra kept emerging: “Nobody craves a compromise.” Although processes and equipment factored in, employees were the ones tasked with embracing that and making it happen, Alter says. Carl’s Jr. started by explaining internally why it was pushing toward cooked-to order. Pilots ran late last year and Carl’s Jr. polled team members on their personal takes. Would they want this if they walked in? Then, Carl’s Jr.’s restaurant excellence team devised how back-of-house efforts would change in light of answering the question. articles.title: Speed Wins: The Restaurants That Hire First Are Winning the Talent Race
articles.titleKo: Speed Wins: The Restaurants That Hire First Are Winning the Talent Race
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . An unfilled restaurant position impacts far more than recruiting. For years, restaurant hiring has been treated like a numbers game. Post a job, collect applications, review resumes, schedule interviews, and hope the best candidate is still available when you’re ready to make a decision. Today’s hiring market doesn’t work that way. One of the biggest competitive advantages in restaurant hiring isn’t offering the highest wage or the biggest signing bonus. Increasingly, it’s speed. Great candidates have options, and the restaurant that reaches them first often has the best opportunity to hire them. Great Candidates Don’t Stay on the Market Hourly workers aren’t necessarily spending weeks evaluating opportunities. Many are applying to multiple restaurants at the same time, often directly from their phones and sometimes within minutes of each other. The first employer to acknowledge an application, answer questions, and invite a qualified candidate to an interview immediately stands out. By the time another restaurant reviews applications two or three days later, that same candidate may already have an interview scheduled or have accepted another position. Hiring delays don’t just cost time. They cost talent. Think about two restaurants hiring for the exact same position. The first reviews applications every few days. A manager manually contacts candidates, waits for responses, and goes back and forth trying to schedule interviews. The second responds almost immediately. The candidate gets their questions answered, selects an interview time, and could be sitting across from a manager the following day. Both restaurants might offer similar compensation, culture, and opportunities. The difference is that one created momentum while the candidate was still interested. That’s the advantage of speed. The Cost of Waiting An unfilled restaurant position impacts far more than recruiting. When a restaurant is short staffed, managers spend more time covering shifts, existing employees take on additional responsibilities, and guest service can suffer. Over time, that added pressure can contribute to burnout and even more turnover. This creates a cycle restaurant operators know all too well. You’re short staffed, so your existing team works harder. Your team becomes frustrated, which can lead to more turnover. Suddenly, you’re not trying to fill one position anymore. Every additional day a critical role remains vacant has a cost, which is why reducing the time between application and interview matters so much. Candidates Expect Faster Communication Today’s candidates are accustomed to getting immediate responses in nearly every part of their lives. They can order dinner, book a ride, make a reservation, or schedule an appointment from their phone in minutes. Those expectations are carrying over into hiring. When applicants don’t hear back quickly, many aren’t going to wait. They’re going to keep applying elsewhere. At Swob, we’ve built our platform around this idea. Instant candidate communication, automated interview scheduling, and real time notifications are designed to help restaurant operators engage qualified candidates while their interest is at its highest. Instead of allowing applications to sit untouched for days, technology can help operators move candidates from application to conversation to interview much faster. This doesn’t mean removing the human side of hiring. In fact, I believe it’s the opposite. Technology should remove the administrative work that prevents those human conversations from happening sooner. That’s particularly important in restaurants. Hiring managers aren’t sitting behind a desk waiting for applications to arrive. My career in the restaurant industry began in 1988 as a hostess at Bob Evans Restaurant, where I quickly discovered my passion for hospitality and operations. I was drawn to the structure of the business, the fast-paced environment and the opportunity to make an impact through both guest service and team leadership. Those early experiences taught me the importance of discipline, accountability and building strong relationships, lessons that have guided me throughout my career. After being promoted to server, I entered Bob Evans’ Management-in-Training program at age 20 and became a General Manager by 23. Over the next decade, I developed a strong operational foundation before moving into multi-unit leadership. When Bob Evans acquired Mimi’s Café, I was selected to oversee 15 Florida locations as Director of Operations, gaining valuable experience leading large teams through growth and organizational change. Following the sale of Mimi’s Café, I joined Logan’s Roadhouse, where I continued advancing my leadership career and helped guide teams through significant industry challenges, including the COVID-19 pandemic and the company’s transition to SPB Hospitality. In 2022, I joined the SPB Support Center to lead Operations Services across the company’s restaurant portfolio, broadening my perspective on cross-functional leadership and enterprise-wide strategy. When SPB acquired Krystal, I had already built strong relationships with the brand while supporting its operations. In February 2024, I joined Krystal full time as Senior Vice President of Operations, and more recently, I was honored to be named Chief Operating Officer following G.J. Hart’s appointment as CEO of SPB Hospitality. Today, I have the privilege of partnering with leaders across every department to strengthen operations, elevate the guest experience and support Krystal’s continued growth. My focus is on developing high-performing teams, fostering a culture of accountability and ensuring operational excellence across the system. While my responsibilities have evolved considerably since my first restaurant job, my leadership philosophy remains unchanged: take care of people, stay curious, embrace continuous learning and never lose sight of the fundamentals that create exceptional guest experiences. QUESTIONS What was your first job? My first job was as a hostess at Bob Evans Restaurants. My hire date was June 6, 1988. I was thrilled at the opportunity! We wore floor-length polyester wraparound skirts, high-neck ruffled blouses and string ties. I had to count back change and manually record check times. We accepted checks for payment and had smoking and non-smoking sections of the restaurant. What’s your favorite menu item at Krystal? I absolutely love our Spicy Chik! I request it with no mayo and extra pickles. It features delicious breast meat with a light batter and packs a kick, all served on our steamed Krystal bun. What’s your favorite cuisine aside from what you offer at Krystal? I love to cook and eat Italian food. Eggplant Parmesan is a favorite. I also make meatballs and my own rendition of the family sauce often. Who inspires you as a leader? My husband inspires me as a leader. articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . One way a franchisor can make a healthy impact on new franchisees is by investing in an incentive structure. For aspiring entrepreneurs, it almost feels like there’s an artform to mastering the delicate balance between ambition and risk. In today’s economy, achieving that harmony takes more skill than before as costs rise, and available real estate grows scarce. The path to opening a single profitable franchise location now calls for sharper strategy and data-backed decision-making. For many first-time franchisees, real estate has become one of the biggest obstacles to work through on the way to a grand opening. With the high-risk environment not changing anytime soon, the franchisors best positioned for growth are the ones rethinking how they can best tackle the real estate process for their prospective franchisees. Franchisor and Franchisee Real Estate Relationship When brands rapidly expand, a disconnect can form between franchisee and franchisor during the site-search process, especially as costs climb. Franchisors need to prioritize the relationship with the franchisee prospect by walking them through the brand’s support from day one. Be transparent about what site selection fully entails: data, realistic timelines, and the costs franchisees should expect to encounter in the market they are looking to expand in. For franchisees to succeed, franchisors must stay actively involved when evaluating potential sites. Franchisees are better equipped to make confident decisions when they understand what they’re walking into. Reviewing demographic data, traffic patterns and competitive density helps prevent costly missteps for franchisees before they happen. Having the real estate expertise to notice when a site that looks promising on paper is the wrong fit in reality will benefit franchisees who are new to the industry. Franchisors that invest that time up front see stronger, longer-lasting partnerships as a result. The shift to shared responsibility is an encouraging development for franchising. It suggests that the industry is maturing into a model that values the strength of both the franchisor and franchisee and does not prioritize one over the other. Benefits of Franchisee Incentives One way a franchisor can make a healthy impact on new franchisees is by investing in an incentive structure. Franchisors can’t change interest rates or construction costs, but they can offer equipment packages, phased royalties, and franchise fee incentives to relieve some of that pressure. Done well, these incentives can lower the bar for entry and create greater confidence for aspiring franchisees. Nontraditional Growth With traditional real estate scarce and expensive, more brands are buying into the idea of nontraditional formats like travel plazas, college campuses, or shared spaces that reduce the real estate burden altogether. These locations often come with lower buildout costs, smaller footprints, and a built-in customer base from the existing vendors. For brands open to nontraditional expansion, there’s an opportunity to succeed in markets where a standalone location would be difficult to justify. These formats will never replace traditional development, but they are giving brands additional paths to scale. The brands succeeding with this approach aren’t treating nontraditional locations as a fallback, but are evaluating each opportunity with the same rigor as a traditional site. Used well, nontraditional locations are a complement to a brand’s portfolio rather than a compromise. Available at all participating 34 Glory Days Grill locations across the U.S., the new menu introduces bold new options. Glory Days Grill & Sports House is kicking off football season with an all-new lineup of food and drinks designed to give guests even more reasons to gather, celebrate and enjoy game day. Available at all participating 34 Glory Days Grill locations across the U.S., the new menu introduces bold new options featuring juicy Wagyu beef, crispy breaded chicken wings, fresh cocktails and shareable carafes made specifically for watching the game with friends and family. “Glory Days Grill has been a neighborhood gathering spot for over 30 years, and we pride ourselves on providing a consistent experience for our guests while also giving them reasons to come back for new and exciting food to try,” said Jen Ulmer, Chief Marketing Officer for Glory Days Grill. “Our new menu lineup offers some delicious reasons to get together with friends and family after your big game, or while watching your favorite team play on one of our dozens of flatscreen TVs.” New Plays From the Kitchen Leading the new lineup are two new options featuring Wagyu beef, each bringing its own distinct flavor profile. The SoCal Wagyu Bowl ($18.99) combines juicy Wagyu beef with bacon, Gruyère cheese, avocado, diced tomato, arugula and pickled onions, served on a bed of basmati rice and finished with Glory Days Grill’s signature Homerun Sauce. The Red Zone Wagyu Burger ($17.99) starts with a juicy Wagyu beef burger, topped with creamy cherry pepper aioli, avocado, Pepper Jack cheese and arugula, all stacked on a toasted brioche bun. Pura Vida Miami , the all-day café and lifestyle brand operating 55 locations across six states and Washington D.C., today announced the appointment of Donnie Upshaw as Chief People and Culture Officer . Upshaw joins Co-Founders Omer and Jennifer Horev and the company’s expanding executive leadership team as Pura Vida Miami continues its national expansion. As the company enters its next chapter, Pura Vida is investing not only in new cafés and markets, but in the people, leadership and culture required to build an enduring organization. In his role, Upshaw will lead Pura Vida’s people and culture strategy, with responsibility for attracting and developing exceptional talent, strengthening leadership at every level of the organization, improving employee engagement and retention, and building the systems and infrastructure necessary to support the company as it scales. “As we build the next chapter of Pura Vida, one of my greatest responsibilities as CEO is to make sure we are not simply building a bigger company – we are building a better one,” said Omer Horev, Co-Founder and CEO of Pura Vida Miami. “I believe the strongest companies are built by people who genuinely care – about the guest, about their teammates, about the details, and about what we are building together. Donnie brings a deep understanding of what it takes to build strong teams, develop great leaders and create an environment where people can grow with the company. I think about our organization much like a great sports team,” Horev continued. “We may play different positions and have different responsibilities, but we wear the same jersey and are working toward the same goal. Bringing Donnie into our leadership team is an important investment in the company and culture we intend to build in the longterm.” Donnie Upshaw, Chief People and Culture Officer Upshaw joins Pura Vida Miami following an eight-year tenure with Wingstop, where he held senior leadership roles across people, brand and restaurant operations during a period of significant growth and transformation. He brings expertise spanning leadership development, succession planning, talent acquisition, workforce strategy and organizational effectiveness. At Pura Vida, Upshaw will work closely with executive leadership to strengthen leadership capabilities, develop talent from within and create opportunities for employees to grow into management and leadership roles. Central to his role will be preserving the entrepreneurial culture, hospitality and sense of community that have distinguished the brand as it scales. “Pura Vida Miami has built something truly special—a brand with an incredible culture, passionate people and an ambitious vision for the future,” said Donnie Upshaw, Chief People and Culture Officer of Pura Vida Miami. “I’m excited to help build the leadership, talent and capabilities to support our growth while maintaining the culture and sense of community that makes Pura Vida so special. I want Pura Vida to be a place where exceptional people want to build their careers and where leaders are developed from within.” Upshaw’s appointment further strengthens Pura Vida Miami’s senior leadership team as the company continues to invest in the people, operational capabilities and infrastructure needed to support its national expansion. His appointment follows the company’s recent additions of Andrew McCaughan as Chief Development Officer, Chad Brauze as Chief Culinary Officer, and Bruno Cardinali as Chief Marketing Officer in June 2026. articles.title: Five Guys is Bringing its Word-of-Mouth Formula into the Digital Age
articles.titleKo: Five Guys is Bringing its Word-of-Mouth Formula into the Digital Age
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Five Guys is one of the largest burger chains in the U.S. Five Guys built a restaurant empire without many of the tools that have become standard across the industry. The fast casual is the 10th-largest burger chain in America in terms of systemwide sales; it earned $2.3 billion in 2025. In terms of unit count, it is the seventh-largest, ending last year with 1,511 U.S. restaurants. There is no loyalty program. The menu has stayed remarkably focused. Marketing has never relied on a constant stream of limited-time products. For decades, much of the brand’s reputation traveled through customers telling other customers where to find a good burger and fries. Forty years after Five Guys opened its first restaurant, that foundation isn’t being discarded. But the way people discover restaurants, order food, and communicate with brands has changed enough for Five Guys to rethink how it tells its story. That work is now part of the job for chief commercial officer Navin Sharma, whose responsibilities span marketing, digital, loyalty, e-commerce, analytics and consumer insights. The position gives Five Guys a dedicated commercial operation at a time when the chain continues to add restaurants and sees an opportunity to introduce more consumers to what happens behind the counter. “One of the big drivers of success for the brand historically has changed in today’s environment and that’s the word of mouth aspect of it,” Sharma says. The restaurant walls offer a clue to how Five Guys originally built its reputation. Reviews from newspapers and magazines have long been part of the décor, showcasing outside validation of the food and experience. Much of that conversation now happens through social media, where Five Guys sees an opening to tell stories that consumers may have never heard. Fresh-cut fries are one example. Five Guys makes them from fresh potatoes inside its restaurants, a process Sharma gained a new appreciation for when he trained in a store after joining the company. “There’s a lot of things like that we do that people don’t know,” Sharma says. “So there’s a lot of stories we can share.” The challenge is building a more sophisticated commercial engine without stripping away the simplicity that helped Five Guys grow. Sharma doesn’t see the assignment as a reinvention. He wants new marketing and digital capabilities to serve as an extension of what Five Guys already does. That applies to menu innovation, too. Five Guys isn’t preparing to chase every product trend or stretch into categories far removed from burgers, fries and shakes. “You won’t see us do a chicken sandwich or anything like that,” Sharma says. “It’s still going to be burgers and fries and shakes. We might do a slightly different version of a burger perhaps, or a different version of the shake, but it’ll still be those core items that people love.” One untapped source of innovation already exists inside the menu. Customers can create a huge number of burger and shake combinations from Five Guys’ existing ingredients, giving the chain material it can surface through digital channels without expanding far outside its core. Sharma sees potential to showcase combinations created by employees and customers, introducing guests to orders they may not have considered on their own. Loyalty could eventually become another vehicle for those discoveries. Five Guys is working on a loyalty program after hearing requests for one from customers. Sharma says frequency and customer data are useful benefits, but the initial motivation is rewarding the chain’s most frequent guests. articles.title: Hilton Ramps up Growth Across Ireland with DoubleTree by Hilton Ashbourne Signing
articles.titleKo: Hilton Ramps up Growth Across Ireland with DoubleTree by Hilton Ashbourne Signing
articles.originalSummary: Hilton is expanding its presence in Ireland with a range of signings, openings and brand debuts, marking a significant step in its growth and building on its existing portfolio of eight hotels across six brands. The upcoming openings will create more than 150 jobs and will bring the number of team members working at Hilton hotels in Ireland to nearly 1,000. The growth is boosted by an agreement to bring DoubleTree by Hilton to Ireland with the conversion of a 156-room hotel in Ashbourne, near Dublin. Expected to open as DoubleTree by Hilton Ashbourne in early 2027 , the hotel will undergo a comprehensive refurbishment, including upgrades to guest rooms, public spaces, restaurants and bars. Located 25 minutes from Dublin Airport, the property is well placed for business and leisure demand, further strengthening Hilton’s presence in Greater Dublin. Richard Mc Dermott, proprietor of DoubleTree by Hilton Ashbourne, said: “Partnering with Hilton marks an exciting next step for the hotel. Alongside a refreshed guest experience, it will help create employment opportunities and deliver long-term value for the local area. Backed by Hilton’s commercial strength and global loyalty programme, we’re confident the hotel will become a go-to destination for guests visiting Dublin and beyond.” The signing follows the opening of Home2 Suites by Hilton Dublin City Centre , marking the brand’s European debut. The 290-suite property introduces Hilton’s fast-growing extended-stay concept to the region, offering apartment-style accommodation designed for both short and longer stays. Located just moments from O’Connell Street, the hotel caters to the growing demand for flexible, home-like accommodation among both business and leisure travellers. Paul Blackmore, vice president, development, UK & Ireland, Hilton, said: “Ireland’s enduring appeal makes it an attractive market for Hilton, with strong demand in cities and across the regions. The opening of Home2 Suites, alongside new signings including DoubleTree by Hilton Ashbourne, and continued expansion of brands such as Tapestry Collection by Hilton, underlines our confidence in the country. We remain focused on expanding our footprint and working with owners and partners to bring the right brands to the right locations while supporting tourism and long-term investment.” Alongside these developments, Hilton recently signed Cork City Centre, Tapestry Collection by Hilton . Expected to open in 2027 in partnership with JMK Group, the 103-room hotel will be located on South Terrace in the heart of Cork and will feature a mix of standard guestrooms and extended-stay accommodation, alongside a restaurant, bar and fitness facilities. The signing marks Hilton’s debut in Cork and builds on the growth of its lifestyle portfolio across the UK and Ireland. Hilton is also expanding its presence across Northern Ireland with a number of landmark projects spanning multiple brands. In Portrush, Hilton celebrated the one-year anniversary since the opening of The Marcus Portrush, Tapestry Collection by Hilton , which marked the brand debut of Tapestry Collection in Northern Ireland. It also expanded its DoubleTree portfolio through the signings of DoubleTree by Hilton Belfast City Ten Square and DoubleTree by Hilton Derry ‑ Londonderry. Looking ahead, Hilton is set to debut another brand in Northern Ireland – Tempo by Hilton Belfast City Centre . Expected to be the first Tempo by Hilton opening outside of the United States, the 144-room lifestyle hotel will bring Hilton’s wellness-focused brand to international markets for the first time, representing a significant milestone in the brand’s global growth strategy.
koreanSummary: Hilton is expanding its presence in Ireland with a range of signings, openings and brand debuts, marking a significant step in its growth and building on its existing portfolio of eight hotels across six brands.
The upcoming openings will create more than 150 jobs and will bring the number of team members working at Hilton hotels in Ireland to nearly 1,000.
The growth is boosted by an agreement to bring DoubleTree by Hilton to Ireland with the conversion of a 156-room hotel in Ashbourne, near Dublin.

articles.title: Statement Panels Added to Kinedo’s Kinewall Range
articles.titleKo: Statement Panels Added to Kinedo’s Kinewall Range
articles.originalSummary: Ever fancied a Highland cow in your bathroom? Or perhaps a preening peacock, a glorious lion, or a giraffe with serious design attitude? Now you can. Kinedo has expanded its Kinewall range with a new portfolio of animal-inspired wall panel designs under its Signature collection. The new Highland Cow, Peacock and Lion panels join the distinctive Giraffe design launched last year, creating a bold new line-up for homeowners and designers looking to bring real personality into the bathroom. The Signature collection has been created for those who want to make a lasting impression. Designed to stand out, these eye-catching panels bring colour, character and style to everyday spaces, helping to transform bathrooms, cloakrooms and utility rooms into statement interiors. Whether used as a single feature panel in a shower, a standalone decorative panel in a cloakroom, or as part of a larger feature wall, Kinewall panels offer exceptional flexibility, durability and ease of installation. In addition to the new animal-inspired designs, Kinedo has also expanded several of its existing Kinewall collections with fresh new patterns. Tangram is a new abstract oak-coloured wood-effect design, while Royal Foliage introduces a striking, large gold-leaf pattern to the Nature collection. Also joining Nature are Botanical Beige, Botanical Green and Exotic. The Minerals & Metals collection has been enhanced with Marble Haze and Corten Copper Stone, while the playful Hills design adds a splash of blue and orange in a flowing wave pattern. Hills joins the Patterns & Geometric collection alongside the new Mandala design, which brings a nostalgic decorative feel to the range. The full Kinewall collection can be viewed on the Kinedo website and in the new downloadable brochure.

articles.title: Hotel Café Royal Announces Leadership Appointments
articles.titleKo: Hotel Café Royal Announces Leadership Appointments
articles.originalSummary: Hotel Café Royal, the landmark hotel on Regent Street at the crossroads of Mayfair and Soho, is delighted to announce the appointments of Alex Cooper as Hotel Manager and Jude Rozario as Executive Chef. The appointments further strengthen the hotel’s leadership team as it continues to build on its reputation as one of London’s most distinguished hospitality destinations. Alex Cooper has joined Hotel Café Royal as Hotel Manager, bringing extensive leadership experience from some of London’s most respected luxury hotels. Most recently serving on the Executive Team as Director of Food & Beverage at The Berkeley and The Emory, Cooper played a key role in shaping guest journeys, leading major opening projects, driving sustainability initiatives and overseeing large operational teams. Earlier in his career, he held senior positions at The Trafalgar St. James and within the Firmdale Hotels portfolio, including Haymarket Hotel and Ham Yard Hotel. Alex has been recognised for his contributions to the industry with accolades including Hotel Cateys F&B Manager of the Year in 2019 and UK Rising Star Restaurant Manager in 2016. In his new role, Cooper oversees Hotel Café Royal’s operational divisions, providing strategic leadership across rooms, engineering, food and beverage, security, wellness and events. He has also joined the Executive Committee. Alongside Cooper’s appointment, Hotel Café Royal has welcomed Jude Rozario as Executive Chef. With experience spanning some of London’s most acclaimed culinary institutions, including The Connaught, The Berkeley, Claridge’s, Sea Containers and Broadwick Soho, Rozario has built a reputation for leading complex culinary operations across hotels, restaurants and banqueting. His time in internationally renowned kitchens, including NOMA Copenhagen and Eleven Madison Park, has further shaped his approach to culinary excellence and innovation. As Executive Chef, he will lead the hotel’s culinary direction and day-to-day kitchen operations across its diverse food and beverage portfolio, while working closely with renowned British chef Kevin Gratton , who continues to play a key role in shaping the Café Royal Grill’s distinctive culinary philosophy, rooted in seasonality and heritage.

articles.title: Angelo Cappellini & Opera Contemporary and the Villa Jolanda project in Brunate on Lake Como
articles.titleKo: Angelo Cappellini & Opera Contemporary and the Villa Jolanda project in Brunate on Lake Como
articles.originalSummary: Set on the hills of Brunate overlooking the breathtaking panorama of Lake Como, Villa Jolanda becomes the stage for an interior design project that celebrates the excellence of Italian design and craftsmanship through the intervention of Angelo Cappellini and Opera Contemporary , created in collaboration with Garamonds. Nestled within an architecturally charming setting, the villa has been reinterpreted through an interior design project capable of enhancing its historical identity with an elegant, sophisticated language perfectly in harmony with the atmosphere of the location. Taking center stage in the project are furnishings by Opera Contemporary and Angelo Cappellini, carefully selected to create a harmonious dialogue between historical heritage and contemporary sensibility. The rooms of the residence feature a refined selection of Clarissa, Osiride, and Ivette beds by Opera Contemporary, complemented by furnishings distinguished by soft lines, fine materials, and delicate beige and natural tones. The interiors blend seamlessly into the villa’s original spaces, helping to shape intimate and relaxing environments designed to offer an exclusive and contemporary hospitality experience. The designer beds by Opera Contemporary express a welcoming, warm, and sensual aesthetic, achieved through the use of fine materials, artisanal craftsmanship, and a rich variety of textures that enhance the feeling of comfort and intimacy. The color palettes, dominated by natural tones with occasional accents of color, define refined and contemporary environments in which the bed becomes the absolute centerpiece of the bedroom space. The bedroom, the most personal space in the home, thus transforms into a private retreat away from daily stress: a place dedicated to relaxation, wellbeing, and the restoration of one’s energy. A distinctive element of the project is also the wooden dependency separated from the main villa, conceived as an elegant space dedicated to the traditional “five o’clock tea.” Angelo Cappellini interprets the charm of great Italian decorative tradition through a Louis XV-style living room composed of sofas, armchairs, chairs, and coffee tables with crystal tops. The artisanal craftsmanship, carved details, and fine finishes fully express the brand’s savoir-faire, creating an environment with a refined and timeless character. The intervention at Villa Jolanda highlights the ability of Angelo Cappellini and Opera Contemporary to design environments where aesthetics, comfort, and identity coexist in perfect balance. It is a project that interprets contemporary luxury through manufacturing quality, stylistic research, and the enhancement of Italian heritage, set in one of the most iconic and internationally renowned destinations of the Lake Como area. The collaboration with Garamonds arose naturally, driven by a shared vision of hospitality and the authentic value of Italian lifestyle. Villa Jolanda represents a place capable of attracting an international clientele seeking not only an exclusive destination, but an experience deeply rooted in tradition, elegance, and a culture of beauty. From the very early stages of the project, a strong synergy emerged among the companies involved, united by the desire to enhance the historic character of the villa through furnishings and atmospheres capable of expressing Italian craftsmanship. This is a language made of artisanal details, refined materials, and high-end manufacturing techniques, designed for an international audience that recognizes Italy as a global benchmark for style and quality. In this context, the collaboration between Angelo Cappellini, Opera Contemporary, and Garamonds has helped create environments that are fully consistent with the soul of the villa, where contemporary design and classical tradition coexist in perfect balance, offering guests a sophisticated and timeless experience.

articles.title: Putting on the Ritz: Manchester Hoteliers Association Celebrates 21st Anniversary with ‘Roaring 20s’ Ball
articles.titleKo: Putting on the Ritz: Manchester Hoteliers Association Celebrates 21st Anniversary with ‘Roaring 20s’ Ball
articles.originalSummary: Membership organisation comprising more than 75 of Greater Manchester’s key hotels, the MHA, has announced plans for its 21st annual ball. The popular event is hosted every year to raise money for local charities and celebrate the hospitality industry. Taking place on Thursday 29th October, the ball will return to Emirates Old Trafford for the second year running. Since the organisation’s inception, one of its key pillars has been charitable donations, raising hundreds of thousands of pounds from the annual celebration over two decades. This year’s chosen charities are Barnabus, Greater Manchester Mayor’s Charity, Wood Street Mission and national charity, Hospitality Action. MHA chair, Matt Townley, has set lofty aims to beat last year’s £45,000 raised. The event, which will take a ‘Roaring 20s’ theme, will also play host to the MHA’s annual awards, voted for by a panel of business and industry experts. Following usual proceedings, there will be a total of nine trophies presented on the night, including Unsung Hero, Rising Star, and Outstanding Contribution to Hospitality. Matt, who is also Group Operations Director at Dakota Hotels, said : “Now in its 21st year, the MHA ball has become a cherished tradition within our industry, providing an opportunity to recognise achievements and support important charitable causes. “Manchester’s hotel and hospitality community continues to demonstrate remarkable resilience and collaboration, and this year’s event will be a fitting celebration of those qualities. We look forward to welcoming colleagues, partners, and friends from across the sector for what promises to be a memorable evening as always.” The event has also amassed support from key local and national sponsors such as, WGC, Expedia, MMU, Stephenson’s, Elix Air, and Percipient. MHA’s five key industry partners; Nespresso, Silentnight, Howden, Mint People, and Purple Story will also continue supporting the organisation for a second year running. Pamela Reckert at Manchester Metropolitan University, said : “Manchester Metropolitan University is proud to sponsor the 21st Manchester Hoteliers Association Ball and support an event that celebrates the people and achievements that make Greater Manchester’s hospitality industry so exceptional.” The ball will be taking place on Thursday 29th October at Emirates Old Trafford, with more than 800 people expected to turn out. Tickets are available and can be purchased here. Entries are now open for the MHA awards and can be submitted here.
koreanSummary: Membership organisation comprising more than 75 of Greater Manchester’s key hotels, the MHA, has announced plans for its 21st annual ball.
The popular event is hosted every year to raise money for local charities and celebrate the hospitality industry.
Taking place on Thursday 29th October, the ball will return to Emirates Old Trafford for the second year running.
